Know that a worker about to terminate normally waits until its outgoing messages have been received (or the receiver has terminated), and terminates abnormally with the receiver's value if the receiver panicked

out_of_scope: Creating workers and fork (concept.strands_workers)
Waiting for worker results (concept.futures_wait)
Restriction on send/receive inside lock (concept.isolation)
nodes.notes: Spec typo in 7.8.1.3: the prose says 'A sync-send-action `E -> R` is equivalent to an async-send-action `E ->> R` followed by a flush', swapping the arrows. The grammar defines async-send-action as `expression -> peer-worker ;` and sync-send-action as `expression ->> peer-worker`; items follow the grammar.

nodes.title: XML
nodes.summary: The xml sequence type with its element, processing instruction, comment and text items, xml<T> types, xml templates, concatenation, mutability and storage identity, plus namespaces with expanded names and xmlns declarations, and attribute access and navigation expressions with name patterns.

must_cover.text: Explain that an xml value is a sequence of element, processing instruction, comment and text items, that a single item is itself a sequence, that the empty xml value is distinct from `""` and `()`, and that consecutive text items are merged when an xml value is constructed, so an xml value never contains two adjacent text items

Use the built-in subtypes `xml:Element`, `xml:ProcessingInstruction`, `xml:Comment` and `xml:Text` (which also includes the empty xml value), and `xml<T>` for sequences whose items all belong to `T` (e.g. `xml<xml:Element>`), knowing that `xml<xml<T>>` equals `xml<T>`, `xml<xml:Text>` equals `xml:Text`, and `xml<never>` is just the empty value

Describe an element as a name string, an attributes map of type `map<string>` and children of type `xml`, where the attributes map also holds the element's namespace declarations, whose keys start with `{http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/}`
Explain that element, processing instruction and comment singletons have storage identity while text items and longer sequences do not, and that a sequence compares with `===` item by item

Explain that `xml:Text` is inherently immutable, elements, processing instructions and comments are selectively immutable, a multi-item sequence is read-only only if all its items are, and a read-only element has read-only attributes and children; mutable items can be mutated but the number and identity of an xml value's constituents, and the identity of an element attributes map, are fixed at construction

Construct xml with templates such as `xml `<book id="${id}">${title}</book>``, which are parsed as XML content with interpolations allowed only in character data and attribute values (not namespace attributes), knowing that an xml template inside a constant expression constructs a read-only xml value

Explain that attribute interpolations must be non-nil simple types (expected type `string`), content interpolations may be `xml` or a non-nil simple type converted to a string, and each evaluation makes a new copy with interpolations evaluated in order
Concatenate xml with `x1 + x2` (no copying of constituents), and with strings, where a non-empty string acts as a text item and an empty string yields the xml operand unchanged
Iterate over the items of an `xml<T>` value with `foreach`, each iteration value being a singleton of type `T`

Use `lang.xml` functions such as `elements`, `children`, `getName`, `getAttributes`, `getChildren`, `data`, `createElement` and `fromString` through method-call syntax, and the constants `xml:XML_NAMESPACE_URI`, `xml:XMLNS_NAMESPACE_URI` and the expanded-name constants `xml:lang`, `xml:space` and `xml:base`

Explain that element and attribute names are expanded-name strings of the form `{namespace-uri}local-name`, or just the local name when there is no namespace, and that `ex:local` with an xmlns-declared prefix evaluates to the expanded name string `{uri}local`

Declare namespace prefixes in a block with `xmlns "http://example.com/ns" as ex;`, or a default namespace by omitting `as`, where the URI is a simple constant expression of type string, or at module level, where an `xmlns` declaration applies only to the source part in which it occurs (like imports); the declared prefixes and default namespace are the in-scope namespaces used when xml templates are processed

Explain that xmlns prefixes share a symbol space with import module prefixes, separate from the main symbol space, and that `xmlns` is predeclared as `http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/` and cannot be redeclared

Explain that namespace attributes are synthesized for prefixes (other than `xml` and the default namespace) that are used by an element or its attributes but not declared on it, so prefixes survive when the element is extracted, and that converting xml to an infoset for serialization prunes redundant namespace declarations, uses the `xml` prefix for the XML namespace, reuses or generates prefixes and adds `xmlns=""` to undeclare an inherited default namespace

Read an attribute with `e.id`, of static type `string|error`, which returns an error when the value is not a singleton element (including when it is empty) or the attribute is missing, or with `e?.id`, of static type `string|error|()`, which returns `()` for an empty xml value or a missing attribute and an error when the value is not a singleton element
Name attributes with a plain identifier, an xmlns-prefixed name expanded at compile time to `{uri}local`, or a module-qualified string constant such as `xml:lang`
Write xml name patterns `*`, `name`, `ns:name`, `ns:*` and alternatives `a|b`, where an unprefixed name means a name in the in-scope default namespace if one is declared
Select element items whose name matches a pattern with `x.<book>`, of static type `xml<xml:Element>`

Use step expressions `x/*` to get the children of every element in `x` (equivalent to mapping `xml:getChildren` over `xml:elements(x)`), `x/<title>` to get the element children matching a name pattern, and `x/**/<title>` to get the matching element descendants (based on `xml:getDescendants`)

Extend steps with `.

`, `[i]` and `.method(args)`, which apply to the result for each element, e.g. `x/[0]`, knowing that ambiguity with member access and method calls is resolved by including as much as possible in the xml step expression and that navigation needs an operand whose static type is a subtype of xml

out_of_scope: Indexing x[i] (concept.field_member_access)
Per-function lang.xml semantics (lib.lang.xml)
Import declarations and module prefixes (concept.modules_imports)

nodes.title: ballerina/ai
nodes.summary: Provider-neutral APIs for LLM applications: direct calls through `ai:ModelProvider` (`chat`, typed `generate`, natural expressions), tool-using `ai:Agent`s with memory and MCP toolkits, and retrieval-augmented generation with `ai:VectorKnowledgeBase`, embedding providers and vector stores.

must_cover.text: Declare an LLM as the provider-neutral `ai:ModelProvider` type, e.g. `final ai:ModelProvider model = check new openai:ModelProvider(apiKey, modelType = openai:GPT_4O);`, so the provider can be swapped without changing calling code

Use the WSO2-hosted defaults `ai:getDefaultModelProvider()` and `ai:getDefaultEmbeddingProvider()`, whose configuration is written to `Config.toml` by the VS Code command `Configure default WSO2 Model Provider`

Call `model->generate(...)` with a backtick raw template (an `ai:Prompt`) such as Tell me a joke about `${subject}`!, whose insertions are filled from in-scope values, and receive the answer as a `string`

Bind `generate` output to a Ballerina type through the expected type (e.g. `JokeResponse r = check model->generate(...)`, arrays, or a nilable type for 'no answer'); the JSON schema sent to the LLM is derived from the type, including its `#` documentation

Make a stateless call with `model->chat(userMessage)`, where `ai:ChatUserMessage userMessage = {role: ai:USER, content: ...}`, and read the optional `content` of the returned `ai:ChatAssistantMessage`
Hold a conversation in an `ai:ChatMessage[]`, passing the whole array to `model->chat(messages)` and pushing each `ai:ChatAssistantMessage` and follow-up user message so the model sees the history
Send images to the model by interpolating an `ai:ImageDocument` (`content` is a URL or `byte[]`) into a `generate` prompt; the provider builds the multimodal request

Call an LLM with a natural expression `natural (model) { ... ${count} ... }` whose expected type (e.g. `Attraction[]|error`) drives the schema and response binding; this is experimental, needs Swan Lake Update 13+ and `bal run --experimental`

Expose a function to agents with `@ai:AgentTool` on an `isolated function` whose parameters are `anydata` and whose return type is a subtype of `anydata|http:Response|stream<anydata, error>|error`, documenting it with `#` comments, e.g. wrapping a connector call such as a Gmail or Calendar client

Group stateful tools in an `isolated class` that includes `*ai:BaseToolKit`, marks its methods with `@ai:AgentTool`, and implements `getTools()` returning `ai:getToolConfigs([self.addTask, self.listTasks])`

Create an `ai:Agent` with `check new (systemPrompt = {role: ..., instructions: ...}, model = model, tools = [sum, mult, new TaskManagerToolkit()])` (or the equivalent `ai:AgentConfiguration` record), optionally setting `maxIter` and `verbose`
Run an agent with `string response = check agent.run(userInput)`, passing `sessionId = "..."` to keep separate conversation memory per user

Configure agent memory with `new ai:ShortTermMemory(check new ai:InMemoryShortTermMemoryStore(15))` passed as `memory`, or set `memory = ()` for a stateless agent; agents get a default in-memory memory when it is omitted
Give an agent the tools of a remote MCP server with `ai:McpToolKit` (`check new ("http://localhost:9090/mcp")`, optionally limited to `["getCurrentWeather"]`) in its `tools` array

Expose an agent as a chat API with `service /tasks on new ai:Listener(8080)` and `resource function post chat(@http:Payload ai:ChatReqMessage request) returns ai:ChatRespMessage|error` that calls `agent.run(request.message, request.sessionId)`

Build an `ai:KnowledgeBase` as `new ai:VectorKnowledgeBase(vectorStore, embeddingProvider)` from an `ai:VectorStore` (e.g. `check new ai:InMemoryVectorStore()` or an external store) and an `ai:EmbeddingProvider`

Load files with `ai:DataLoader loader = check new ai:TextDataLoader("./leave_policy.md")` and `loader.load()` (an `ai:Document|ai:Document[]`), then call `knowledgeBase.ingest(documents)`, which chunks and embeds them

Control chunking yourself with `ai:Chunker` implementations such as `new ai:GenericRecursiveChunker(maxChunkSize, maxOverlapSize, ai:SENTENCE)`, `ai:MarkdownChunker` or `ai:HtmlChunker` (or the `chunker` argument of `ai:VectorKnowledgeBase`, `ai:AUTO`/`ai:DISABLE`), and ingest the resulting `ai:Chunk[]`

Answer questions with RAG by calling `knowledgeBase.retrieve(query, 10)` to get `ai:QueryMatch[]` (`chunk`, `similarityScore`), then either `ai:augmentUserQuery(context, query)` and `model->chat(...)`, or interpolate the chunks into a `generate` prompt

Filter retrieval and deletion by chunk metadata with `ai:MetadataFilters {filters: [{key: ..., operator: ai:EQUAL, value: ...}], condition: ai:AND}` passed to `retrieve(query, topK, filters)` or `knowledgeBase.deleteByFilter(filters)`

External vector store configuration (lib.ai.pinecone)
Writing MCP servers and low-level MCP clients (lib.mcp)

nodes.title: ballerinax/asb
nodes.summary: Azure Service Bus connector: an `asb:AdminClient` to manage queues, topics, subscriptions and rules, `asb:MessageSender` and `asb:MessageReceiver` clients to send, receive and settle messages, and an `asb:Listener` for event-driven consumption.

must_cover.text: Create an `asb:AdminClient` from a connection string (`check new (connectionString)`) and manage entities with `createQueue`, `createTopic`, `createSubscription`, `createRule`, `getQueue`, `listQueues`, `updateQueue`, `deleteQueue`, `queueExists` and `topicExists`

Create an `asb:MessageSender` with an `asb:ASBServiceSenderConfig` giving `connectionString`, `entityType: asb:QUEUE` (or `asb:TOPIC`) and `topicOrQueueName`, reading the connection string from a `configurable`

Send an `asb:Message` with `sender->send({body: ..., contentType: asb:TEXT, timeToLive: 60, applicationProperties: {properties: {a: "v"}}})`, or just a payload with `sender->sendPayload(value)`, and close the client with `close()`

Send several messages at once with `sender->sendBatch({messages: [...]})` (an `asb:MessageBatch`), schedule a message for later with `sender->schedule(message, scheduledEnqueueTime)` (a `time:Civil`) and cancel it with `cancel(sequenceNumber)`

Create an `asb:MessageReceiver` with an `asb:ASBServiceReceiverConfig` giving `connectionString`, `entityConfig` (`{queueName}` or `{topicName, subscriptionName}`) and `receiveMode` (`asb:PEEK_LOCK` by default, or `asb:RECEIVE_AND_DELETE`)

Receive with `receiver->receive(serverWaitTime)`, which returns `asb:Message|asb:Error?` (nil when no message arrives), bind the body directly with `receivePayload`, or fetch up to N messages with `receiveBatch(maxMessageCount)`

Settle peek-locked messages on the receiver with `complete(message)`, `abandon(message)`, `deadLetter(message)` or `defer(message)`, read deferred ones with `receiveDeferred(sequenceNumber)`, and extend the lock with `renewLock(message)`

sources.note: complete, abandon, deadLetter, defer, receiveDeferred, renewLock

must_cover.text: Consume events with `listener asb:Listener asbListener = check new (connectionString = ..., entityConfig = {queueName: "myQueue"})` and `service asb:Service on asbListener` implementing `isolated remote function onMessage(asb:Message message) returns error?`

Tune the listener with `asb:ListenerConfiguration` fields `autoComplete` (default `true`), `prefetchCount` and `maxConcurrency`, plus the receiver fields `receiveMode`, `maxAutoLockRenewDuration` and `amqpRetryOptions`

Settle messages manually in a service by setting `autoComplete: false`, adding an `asb:Caller caller` parameter to `onMessage`, and calling `caller->complete()`, `caller->abandon()`, `caller->deadLetter(deadLetterReason = ...)` or `caller->defer()`

Handle receive failures in the service with `isolated remote function onError(asb:MessageRetrievalError 'error) returns error?`, and distinguish `asb:AdminActionError` from other `asb:Error` values in admin calls

nodes.title: ballerina/auth
nodes.summary: The `auth` module provides Basic Auth (RFC 7617) providers: listener providers that authenticate credentials against a Config.toml file user store or an LDAP user store, and a client provider that generates Basic Auth tokens. Protocol connectors such as HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC and WebSocket build their Basic Auth support on it.

must_cover.text: Define the users of the file user store in `Config.toml` as `[[ballerina.auth.users]]` tables with `username`, `password` and `scopes` keys, repeating the table for each user

Create an `auth:ListenerFileUserStoreBasicAuthProvider` with `new` and call `authenticate(credential)` with the Base64-encoded `username:password` value to get an `auth:UserDetails` record (`username` and optional `scopes`) or an `auth:Error`

Describe an LDAP user store with `auth:LdapUserStoreConfig`, setting `domainName`, `connectionUrl`, `connectionName`, `connectionPassword`, the user search fields (`userSearchBase`, `userEntryObjectClass`, `userNameAttribute`, `userNameSearchFilter`, `userNameListFilter`) and the group fields (`groupSearchBase`, `groupEntryObjectClass`, `groupNameAttribute`, `groupNameSearchFilter`, `groupNameListFilter`, `membershipAttribute`)

Authenticate credentials against LDAP with `auth:ListenerLdapUserStoreBasicAuthProvider`, created from an `auth:LdapUserStoreConfig`, whose `authenticate(credential)` returns `auth:UserDetails` with the user's LDAP groups as `scopes`

Tune the LDAP connection with `userRolesCacheEnabled`, `connectionPoolingEnabled`, `connectionTimeout` and `readTimeout` (seconds), and secure it with `secureSocket` (`auth:SecureSocket` whose `cert` is a `crypto:TrustStore` or a certificate file path)

Generate a Basic Auth token for outbound calls with `auth:ClientBasicAuthProvider`, initialised with an `auth:CredentialsConfig` (`username`, `password`), and its `generateToken()` method, which returns the Base64-encoded credential or an `auth:Error`
Decode a received Basic Auth credential into a `[username, password]` tuple with `auth:extractUsernameAndPassword(credential)`, which returns an `auth:Error` for an invalid value
Write a custom user store by implementing the `auth:ListenerBasicAuthProvider` object type, i.e. an `isolated function authenticate(string credential) returns auth:UserDetails|auth:Error` method

Secure a service with Basic Auth by adding a `fileUserStoreConfig: {}` or `ldapUserStoreConfig` entry, with `scopes` for authorization, to the connector's service `auth` configuration (e.g. `@http:ServiceConfig {auth: [...]}`), knowing that failed authentication gives 401 and failed authorization 403

Call a Basic Auth-protected endpoint by setting `auth: {username, password}` in a connector client's configuration (e.g. `http:Client`), which adds the `Authorization: Basic <token>` header to each request
Handle the distinct `auth:Error` returned by the provider methods, for example for an empty credential or a failed LDAP lookup, with `check` or an `is auth:Error` test

OAuth2 grant types and token introspection (lib.oauth2)

nodes.summary: The `avro` module serializes Ballerina `anydata` values to Avro binary and deserializes them back using an `avro:Schema` created from an Avro schema definition string.

must_cover.text: Create an `avro:Schema` with `check new (schemaString)`, passing the Avro schema JSON as a string (often a string template), and get an `avro:Error` if the schema is invalid
Serialize and deserialize a primitive value with a primitive schema such as `{"type": "int", "namespace": "example.data"}`
Write an Avro `record` schema (`namespace`, `type: "record"`, `name`, `fields` with `name`/`type`) that matches a Ballerina record type such as `Student {int id; string name;}`
Serialize an `anydata` value to Avro binary with `byte[] data = check schema.toAvro(value);`
Deserialize Avro bytes into a typed value with `schema.fromAvro(data)`, whose target type is inferred from the expected type, e.g. `Student s = check schema.fromAvro(bytes);`
Handle `avro:Error` from schema creation, serialization of values that do not match the schema, and deserialization

nodes.title: ballerina/cache
nodes.summary: The `cache` module provides `cache:Cache`, a thread-safe in-memory key-value cache with LRU eviction, configurable capacity, eviction factor, per-entry max age and optional periodic cleanup, plus the `cache:AbstractCache` object type for custom cache implementations.

must_cover.text: Create a cache with default settings using `cache:Cache cache = new ();` (capacity 100, eviction factor 0.25, entries never expire)

Configure a cache with `cache:CacheConfig` fields passed to `new`, e.g. `new (capacity = 10, evictionFactor = 0.2, defaultMaxAge = 2, cleanupInterval = 3)` or `new ({capacity: 10, ...})`, where `defaultMaxAge` and `cleanupInterval` are in seconds and `evictionPolicy` is `cache:LRU`

Store entries with `check cache.put(key, value)` and read them with `cache.get(key)`, which returns `any|cache:Error`, casting the result back to the stored type (e.g. `<string> check cache.get("key1")`)
Override the default expiry for a single entry with the `maxAge` argument of `put`, e.g. `cache.put("key3", "value3", 3600)`, where `-1` means the entry never expires
Inspect a cache with `hasKey(key)`, `keys()`, `size()` and `capacity()`
Remove one entry with `cache.invalidate(key)` or all entries with `cache.invalidateAll()`, both returning `cache:Error?`

Explain when entries are evicted: an expired entry is removed when `get` reaches it, a full cache drops the least recently used entries (capacity times `evictionFactor`) on `put`, and a `cleanupInterval` starts a periodic task that removes expired entries
Handle `cache:Error`, returned by `get` for a missing or expired key and by `put` when the value is `()`, for example by checking `hasKey` first or using `check`
Implement a read-through lookup that returns the cached value when `hasKey` is true and otherwise computes or fetches the value and `put`s it in the cache

Write a custom cache (e.g. backed by a file or database) as an object that is structurally equivalent to `cache:AbstractCache`, with `put`, `get`, `invalidate`, `invalidateAll`, `hasKey`, `keys`, `size` and `capacity` methods

out_of_scope: HTTP response caching and cache-control headers (lib.http)
