nodes.title: ballerinax/cdc
nodes.summary: The change data capture (CDC) library, built on Debezium: database-specific CDC listeners (`mysql:CdcListener`, `postgresql:CdcListener`, `mssql:CdcListener`, `oracledb:CdcListener`) deliver insert, update and delete events to `cdc:Service` remote methods.

must_cover.text: Import `ballerinax/cdc`, the database module and its Debezium driver package once, e.g. `import ballerinax/mysql.cdc.driver as _;` (or `postgresql.cdc.driver`, `mssql.cdc.driver`, `oracledb.cdc.driver`)
Declare a database-specific CDC listener such as `listener mysql:CdcListener financeDBListener = new (database = {username: "root", password: "...", includedDatabases: "finance_db"});`

Attach a service with remote methods `onRead(record {} after)` (snapshot rows), `onCreate(record {} after)`, `onUpdate(record {} before, record {} after)` and `onDelete(record {} before)`, each returning `cdc:Error?`
Bind event payloads to typed records (e.g. `isolated remote function onCreate(Transactions trx) returns cdc:Error?`) instead of `record {}`, so column values are accessed as typed fields
Add the optional `string tableName` parameter to handlers (e.g. `onDelete(Entity before, string tableName)`) to branch on the table that produced the event
Route events to separate services on one listener with `@cdc:ServiceConfig {tables: ["store_db.products", "store_db.vendors"]}`, each service handling its own tables and record type
Limit captured data with the listener's `database` filters such as `includedDatabases`, `includedTables`/`excludedTables` and `includedColumns`/`excludedColumns`, which take regular expressions

Handle failures in an optional `remote function onError(cdc:Error e)` handler, checking for `cdc:EventProcessingError` (and its subtype `cdc:PayloadBindingError`) and reading the original event from `e.detail().payload`; without `onError`, errors are logged and processing continues

Tune the listener with `options` such as `snapshotMode` (`cdc:INITIAL`, `cdc:NO_DATA`, `cdc:ALWAYS`...), `skippedOperations`, `heartbeatConfig: {interval}` and `connectionRetryConfig: {maxAttempts, retryInitialDelay, retryMaxDelay}`

sources.note: Options, SnapshotMode, retry and heartbeat configuration

must_cover.text: Choose where the listener stores offsets and schema history with `offsetStorage` (`cdc:FileOffsetStorage` default `tmp/debezium-offsets.dat`, `KafkaOffsetStorage`, `MemoryOffsetStorage`, `JdbcOffsetStorage`, `RedisOffsetStorage`) and `internalSchemaStorage` (file, Kafka, memory, JDBC, Redis, Amazon S3, Azure Blob, RocketMQ), so processing resumes after a restart
Expose a liveness probe by calling `cdc:isLive(cdcListener)` from an HTTP resource and returning `http:OK` or `http:SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, with the check interval set by `livenessInterval`

out_of_scope: Database-side CDC setup (binlog, logical replication, SQL Server CDC, LogMiner) and DB-specific listener fields (lib.mysql, lib.postgresql, lib.mssql, lib.oracledb)
Event-driven architecture patterns (topic.event_driven)

sources.note: CDC library specification (service structure, health checks, storage, errors)

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-cdc main (1.4.1), its spec, the mysql/postgresql/mssql/oracledb READMEs and the two CDC BBEs. The spec's own examples use stale names (`cdc:MySqlListener`, `databaseInclude`); items follow the README/BBE form (`mysql:CdcListener`, `includedDatabases`). The spec says `onTruncate` is PostgreSQL-only, which conflicts with the Oracle README mentioning truncation events, so `onTruncate` is not itemised.

nodes.title: ballerina/constraint
nodes.summary: The `constraint` module provides annotations that attach validation rules to `int`, `float`, `decimal`, `string`, array and date types and record fields, and the `constraint:validate` function that checks a value against them.

must_cover.text: Attach a constraint to a type definition, e.g. `@constraint:Int {minValue: 18} type Age int;`, and reuse the constrained type in record fields
Attach constraint annotations directly to record fields, e.g. `@constraint:String {minLength: 5, maxLength: 10} string name;`
Constrain `int` values with `@constraint:Int` using `minValue`, `maxValue`, `minValueExclusive`, `maxValueExclusive` and `maxDigits`

Constrain `float` values with `@constraint:Float` and any of `int`, `float` or `decimal` with `@constraint:Number` (constraint values typed `decimal`), using min/max (inclusive and exclusive), `maxIntegerDigits` and `maxFractionDigits`
Constrain string length with `@constraint:String` using `length`, or `minLength`/`maxLength` (`length` cannot be combined with them)

Require a string to fully match a regular expression with the `pattern` field of `@constraint:String`, given as a `string:RegExp` `re` template (for example the student-id pattern `[0-9]{6}[A-Z|a-z]` or an `Email` type pattern)
Constrain array sizes with `@constraint:Array` using `length`, `minLength` and `maxLength`

Validate dates with `@constraint:Date` on `time:Date` or a record with `year`, `month` and `day` (checked against Gregorian calendar rules), adding `option: constraint:PAST`, `PAST_OR_PRESENT`, `FUTURE` or `FUTURE_OR_PRESENT`

Validate a value explicitly with `constraint:validate(value)`, which returns the validated value typed as the expected type or a `constraint:Error`, e.g. `student = check constraint:validate(student);`
Validate while converting by assigning `constraint:validate` to a different expected type (or passing its `typedesc`), in which case the value is first cloned to that type and then validated
Give custom error messages per constraint with the record form `{value: 10, message: "Name should be less than 10 characters"}`, and an overall `message` on `@constraint:Date`
Handle `constraint:Error` and its subtypes `constraint:ValidationError` and `constraint:TypeConversionError`, reporting the failure with `error.message()`

Know that constraint annotations are also enforced automatically by library data binding, such as HTTP payload binding and the `data.jsondata`, `data.xmldata`, `data.csv` and `data.yaml` parse functions, unless disabled

out_of_scope: Annotation syntax in general (concept.annotations)
Regular expression syntax (concept.regexp)
HTTP and messaging payload validation configuration (lib.http, lib.kafka, lib.rabbitmq)
nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-constraint master 1.7.2 (= latest tag). The README table lists `maxIntegerDigits`/`maxFractionDigits` for `@constraint:Int`, but `IntConstraints` in constraint.bal only has `maxDigits` (and `FloatConstraints` has no `maxDigits`); items follow the source.

nodes.title: ballerina/crypto
nodes.summary: The `crypto` module provides hashing, HMAC, CRC32B checksums, password hashing, key decoding from files and keystores, RSA/AES/PGP encryption and decryption, RSA/ECDSA/ML-DSA signing and verification, HKDF, key encapsulation (KEM) and hybrid public key encryption (HPKE), all operating on `byte[]` values.

must_cover.text: Hash data with `crypto:hashMd5`, `hashSha1`, `hashSha256`, `hashSha384`, `hashSha512` or `hashKeccak256`, passing `string.toBytes()` input and an optional `salt`, and encode the `byte[]` digest with `toBase16()` or `toBase64()`
Compute a CRC32B checksum of a `byte[]` with `crypto:crc32b(input)`, which returns a hex-encoded `string`
Generate an HMAC with `crypto:hmacMd5`, `hmacSha1`, `hmacSha256`, `hmacSha384` or `hmacSha512(input, key)`, which return `byte[]|crypto:Error`

Store passwords safely with `crypto:hashBcrypt(password, workFactor)` / `crypto:verifyBcrypt` or `crypto:hashArgon2(password, iterations, memory, parallelism)` / `crypto:verifyArgon2`, which return a hash `string` and a `boolean` match result

Hash and verify passwords with PBKDF2 using `crypto:hashPbkdf2(password, iterations, algorithm)` (algorithm `crypto:SHA1`, `crypto:SHA256` by default, or `crypto:SHA512`) and `crypto:verifyPbkdf2(password, hashedPassword)`
Compare a computed hash or HMAC with an expected value in constant time using `crypto:equalConstantTime(value, expectedValue)`, which accepts `byte[]` or `string` and returns a `boolean`
Describe PKCS#12 key and trust stores with the `crypto:KeyStore` and `crypto:TrustStore` records (`path`, `password`), as used by key-decoding functions and by `secureSocket` configurations

Obtain RSA keys as `crypto:PrivateKey` / `crypto:PublicKey` with `crypto:decodeRsaPrivateKeyFromKeyFile(keyFile, keyPassword)`, `decodeRsaPrivateKeyFromKeyStore(keyStore, keyAlias, keyPassword)`, `decodeRsaPublicKeyFromCertFile(certFile)`, `decodeRsaPublicKeyFromTrustStore(trustStore, keyAlias)`, the `...FromContent(byte[])` variants, or `buildRsaPublicKey(modulus, exponent)`

Sign data with `crypto:signRsaSha256(input, privateKey)` (also `signRsaMd5`, `signRsaSha1`, `signRsaSha384`, `signRsaSha512`) and check the signature with the matching `crypto:verifyRsaSha256Signature(data, signature, publicKey)`, which returns `boolean|crypto:Error`

Sign and verify with RSASSA-PSS using `crypto:signRsaSsaPss256` / `verifyRsaSsaPss256Signature`, and with ECDSA using `crypto:signSha256withEcdsa` / `verifySha256withEcdsaSignature` (or the SHA384 variants) and EC keys from `decodeEcPrivateKeyFromKeyFile`, `decodeEcPrivateKeyFromKeyStore`, `decodeEcPublicKeyFromCertFile` or `decodeEcPublicKeyFromTrustStore`

Encrypt with a public key and decrypt with the private key using `crypto:encryptRsaEcb(input, key, padding)` and `crypto:decryptRsaEcb`, with padding `crypto:PKCS1` (default) or an OAEP mode such as `crypto:OAEPWithSHA256AndMGF1` or `crypto:OAEPwithSHA512andMGF1`

Encrypt and decrypt with a shared AES key using `crypto:encryptAesCbc(input, key, iv, padding)` / `decryptAesCbc`, `encryptAesEcb(input, key, padding)` / `decryptAesEcb` (padding `crypto:PKCS5` by default or `crypto:NONE`), and `encryptAesGcm(input, key, iv, padding, tagSize)` / `decryptAesGcm`, generating a 16-byte key and IV

Encrypt with PGP using `crypto:encryptPgp(plainText, publicKeyPath, ...options)` (options such as `compressionAlgorithm`, `symmetricKeyAlgorithm`, `armor`, `withIntegrityCheck`) and decrypt with `crypto:decryptPgp(cipherText, privateKeyPath, passphrase)`, using ASCII-armored key files

Encrypt or decrypt large content as streams with `crypto:encryptStreamAsPgp` and `crypto:decryptStreamFromPgp`, which take a `stream<byte[], error?>` (e.g. from `io:fileReadBlocksAsStream`) and return `stream<byte[], crypto:Error?>`
Derive key material with `crypto:hkdfSha256(input, length, salt, info)`, where `salt` and `info` default to empty byte arrays

Sign and verify with the post-quantum ML-DSA-65 algorithm using `crypto:signMlDsa65` / `crypto:verifyMlDsa65Signature` and keys from `decodeMlDsa65PrivateKeyFromKeyStore`, `decodeMlDsa65PrivateKeyFromKeyFile`, `decodeMlDsa65PublicKeyFromTrustStore` or `decodeMlDsa65PublicKeyFromCertFile`

Establish a shared secret with a key encapsulation mechanism: `crypto:encapsulateMlKem768(publicKey)`, `encapsulateRsaKem` or `encapsulateRsaKemMlKem768` return a `crypto:EncapsulationResult` (`encapsulatedSecret`, `sharedSecret`), and the matching `decapsulate...` function recovers the secret with the private key

Use hybrid public key encryption with `crypto:encryptMlKem768Hpke(input, publicKey)` or `encryptRsaKemMlKem768Hpke`, which return a `crypto:HybridEncryptionResult` (`encapsulatedSecret`, `cipherText`), and decrypt with `decryptMlKem768Hpke(cipherText, encapsulatedSecret, privateKey)`
Handle the distinct `crypto:Error` returned by HMAC, key decoding, encryption and signing functions, e.g. for an unreadable key file or an invalid key, with `check` or an `is crypto:Error` test

out_of_scope: Issuing and validating JWTs (lib.jwt)
TLS/mTLS `secureSocket` configuration of listeners and clients (lib.http)
Generating random numbers for keys and IVs (lib.random)
`byte[]` Base16/Base64 conversions in detail (lib.lang.array)
Security best practices such as key management (topic.security)

sources.note: Version history of newer APIs (bcrypt/argon2 2.8.0, PBKDF2 and RSASSA-PSS 2.10.0, equalConstantTime 2.11.0)

nodes.title: ballerina/data.csv
nodes.summary: The `data.csv` module parses CSV given as a string, byte array, byte-block stream or `string[][]` into record arrays or `anydata[][]` with projection, transforms record arrays between shapes, streams large files record by record, and supports fail-safe parsing with error logging.

must_cover.text: Parse a CSV string with a header row into a record array with `csv:parseString`, e.g. `Book[] books = check csv:parseString(csvString);`, where values are converted to the field types
Parse CSV into `string[][]`, `anydata[][]` or a tuple array such as `[string, int][]` by choosing the expected type of `csv:parseString`

Project only the needed columns by targeting a closed record type such as `record {| string name; string author; |}[]`, or a fixed-length inner array such as `string[][2]` to keep the first two columns
Parse CSV held in a `byte[]` with `csv:parseBytes`
Parse a CSV byte-block stream, such as the result of `io:fileReadBlocksAsStream`, into a complete array with `csv:parseStream`
Process large CSV files incrementally with `csv:parseToStream(byteStream)`, which returns `stream<Book, csv:Error?>` parsing one record at a time, and consume it with `forEach` or `foreach`
Convert a `string[][]` to records or typed arrays with `csv:parseList`, naming columns with `customHeaders` and treating leading rows as headers with `headerRows`
Reshape a record array into another record type or into `anydata[][]` with `csv:transform`, using `headerOrder` in `csv:TransformOptions` to fix column order for list output
Map a CSV header to a differently named field with `@csv:Name {value: "empId"}` on the record field
Parse non-standard CSV with `csv:ParseOptions` such as `delimiter: "|"`, `textEnclosure`, `escapeChar`, `comment: "#"`, `lineTerminator` (`csv:LF`, `csv:CRLF`), `encoding` and `locale`

Handle header rows with the `header` option of `csv:ParseOptions` and supply column names with `customHeadersIfHeadersAbsent` when the data has none; set `outputWithHeaders: true` to include the headers as the first row of list output
Skip specific data rows with `skipLines`, e.g. `{skipLines: [2, 4]}`, in parse and transform options
Control nil handling with `nilValue` (`csv:NULL`, `csv:NOT_APPLICABLE`, `csv:EMPTY_STRING`, `csv:NIL`) and `allowDataProjection: {nilAsOptionalField: true, absentAsNilableType: true}`

Keep parsing past bad rows with the `failSafe` option, logging errors to the console (`enableConsoleLogs`) and to a file via `fileOutputMode: {filePath: ..., contentType: csv:METADATA | csv:RAW | csv:RAW_AND_METADATA, fileWriteOption: csv:APPEND | csv:OVERWRITE}`
Rely on `@constraint` annotations on the target record being validated during parsing (`enableConstraintValidation`, on by default)
Handle `csv:Error` returned for malformed input or type mismatches, e.g. declaring `Book[]|csv:Error result = csv:parseString(s);` and testing the result

out_of_scope: Reading and writing CSV files directly with `io:fileReadCsv`/`io:fileWriteCsv` (lib.io)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)
Querying the parsed arrays (concept.query_expressions)

edges.note: io:fileReadCsv/fileWriteCsv offer simpler file-level CSV I/O

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-data.csv master 1.0.1 (= latest tag). The exact semantics of the `header` option values and the string form of `skipLines` (type `int[]|string`) were not documented with examples, so items stay general on `header` and use only the `int[]` form of `skipLines`. The module has no CSV string writer; serialization to CSV files is done with lib.io.

nodes.title: ballerina/data.jsondata
nodes.summary: The `data.jsondata` module converts JSON given as a `json` value, string, byte array or byte-block stream into typed Ballerina values (records, arrays, tuples, maps) with projection and constraint validation, and adds `toJson`, `prettify` and JSONPath queries.

must_cover.text: Convert a `json` value to a record with `jsondata:parseAsType`, letting the target type be inferred from the declaration, e.g. `Book book = check jsondata:parseAsType(jsonContent);`
Parse JSON text into a typed value with `jsondata:parseString`, for example content read with `io:fileReadString` or received as a string payload
Parse JSON from a `byte[]` into a typed value with `jsondata:parseBytes`
Parse JSON from a byte-block stream `stream<byte[], error?>` (such as the result of `io:fileReadBlocksAsStream`) with `jsondata:parseStream`
Pass the target type explicitly through the `typedesc<anydata>` parameter `t` when there is no contextually expected type, e.g. `var book = check jsondata:parseString(s, t = Book);`

sources.note: parseString(string s, Options options = {}, typedesc<anydata> t = <>) returns t|Error

must_cover.text: Map nested JSON objects to nested record types (e.g. `Author` with a `Book[] books` field) in a single `parseAsType` or `parseString` call
Convert a JSON array to a Ballerina array such as `Book[]` or to a tuple such as `[Book, Book]` by choosing the expected type

Use a closed record type (`record {| ... |}`) to keep only the fields you need, so extra JSON members such as `year` and `publisher` are dropped, versus an open record which keeps them as `anydata` rest fields

Control projection with `jsondata:Options`: set `allowDataProjection: false` to reject members not in the target type, or pass `{allowDataProjection: {nilAsOptionalField: true, absentAsNilableType: true}}` to treat `null` as an absent optional field and absent members as nil
Map a JSON key that differs from the field name with `@jsondata:Name {value: "first-name"}` on a record field

sources.note: const annotation NameConfig Name on record field

must_cover.text: Rely on parse functions validating `@constraint` annotations on the target type by default, and turn this off with `{enableConstraintValidation: false}`
Convert an `anydata` value such as a record to `json` with `jsondata:toJson(value)`
Format a `json` value as indented text with `jsondata:prettify(value)` or `jsondata:prettify(value, 2)` (default indentation 4)
Query a `json` value with `jsondata:read(value, query)`, where the query is a backtick JSONPath template such as `$..title` and the result is returned as `json`
Use JSONPath filter expressions and functions with `jsondata:read`, such as `$..[?(@.price > 80)].year` and `$..price.sum()`
Handle `jsondata:Error` returned when the input is malformed or does not match the target type, using `check` or an `is jsondata:Error` test

out_of_scope: The `json` type, member access and the langlib `cloneWithType`/`fromJsonWithType`/`toJson` functions (concept.json_anydata, lib.lang.value)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)
Reading files (lib.io)
HTTP payload data binding (lib.http)

edges.note: jsondata:parseAsType/toJson versus langlib cloneWithType/fromJsonWithType/toJson

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-data.jsondata master 1.1.7 (= latest tag). The README covers parse functions and projection only; `@jsondata:Name`, `Options`, `toJson`, `prettify` and `read` are taken from the public API source and the jsonpath-expressions BBE. Whether `toJson` honours `@jsondata:Name` was not confirmed, so it is not claimed.

nodes.title: ballerina/data.xmldata
nodes.summary: The `data.xmldata` module converts XML given as an `xml` value, string, byte array or byte-block stream into typed records with projection, maps names, attributes and namespaces through annotations, and converts records and JSON back to XML, with XSD validation and XPath queries.

must_cover.text: Convert an `xml` value to a record with `xmldata:parseAsType`, letting the target record type be inferred, e.g. `Book book = check xmldata:parseAsType(xmlValue);`
Parse XML text into a record with `xmldata:parseString`, for example content read from a file or received as a string payload
Parse XML from a `byte[]` with `xmldata:parseBytes` or from a `stream<byte[], error?>` with `xmldata:parseStream`

Model child elements as record fields named after the element's local name, using nested or inline record types for elements with children and delimited identifiers such as `title\-name` for names that are not valid identifiers
Type element text content as `string`, `int`, `float`, `decimal` or `boolean` fields, and know that untyped numeric text becomes `decimal` and other text `string`
Map repeated sibling elements such as multiple `<author>` elements to an array field like `string[] author` or `Item[] items`
Map XML attributes to record fields, and mark a field with `@xmldata:Attribute` to make it an attribute (attributes otherwise lose to a same-named child element)
Capture the text of an element that also has attributes in a `string` field named `#content` (written `\#content`), or rename it with the `textFieldName` option
Map an element or type name that differs from the Ballerina name with `@xmldata:Name {value: "title-name"}` on a record field or type

Bind XML namespaces with `@xmldata:Namespace {prefix: "bk", uri: "http://example.com/book"}` on record types and fields, knowing that field names use local names and namespace prefixes are not part of them
Use a closed record to convert only the needed elements and attributes (others are dropped), versus an open record which keeps unmapped elements as extra fields

Tune parsing with `xmldata:SourceOptions`: `allowDataProjection: false` to reject unexpected content, `attributePrefix`, `textFieldName`, `useSemanticEquality`, and `enableConstraintValidation` (on by default) to validate `@constraint` annotations
Convert a record or map to XML with `xmldata:toXml(value)`, using `@xmldata:Name`, `@xmldata:Namespace` and `@xmldata:Attribute` on the record type to control element names, namespaces and attributes

Convert a `json` value to XML with `xmldata:fromJson`, where keys prefixed with `@` become attributes, and adjust `attributePrefix`, `arrayEntryTag` (default `item`) and `rootTag` through `xmldata:JsonOptions`
Convert XML to JSON by parsing it into a record with `xmldata:parseAsType` and then calling `toJson()` on the record

Validate an XML document against an XML schema with `xmldata:validate(xmlValue, "schema.xsd")` or against a record type that models the XSD, which can use `@xmldata:Element`, `@xmldata:Sequence`, `@xmldata:Choice` (with `minOccurs`/`maxOccurs`) and `@xmldata:SequenceOrder`

Query XML with XPath using `xmldata:transform(xmlValue, query)`, where the query is a backtick XPath template and the result is projected to the expected type (`string`, `int`, `float`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `xml` or nil)
Handle `xmldata:Error` returned for malformed XML, type mismatches or failed validation, using `check` or an `is xmldata:Error` test

out_of_scope: The `xml` type, XML literals, navigation and mutation (concept.xml, lib.lang.xml)
XSLT transformations (lib.xslt)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)

sources.note: Module README: XML to record canonical representation

edges.note: quoted/escaped identifiers

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-data.xmldata master 1.7.1 (= latest tag). The README covers parse functions, name/attribute/namespace mapping and projection; `toXml`, `fromJson`, `validate`, `transform` (XPath) and the XSD annotations are taken from the public API source plus the xml-from-record/xml-from-json BBEs. The `@xmldata:Any` annotation is not covered.

nodes.title: ballerina/data.yaml
nodes.summary: The `data.yaml` module parses YAML given as a string, byte array or byte-block stream into typed `anydata` values such as records with projection, and serializes Ballerina values to YAML strings with configurable formatting.

must_cover.text: Parse YAML text, e.g. a config file read with `io:fileReadString`, into a record with `yaml:parseString`, letting the target type be inferred: `ServerConfig config = check yaml:parseString(content);`
Parse YAML from a `byte[]` with `yaml:parseBytes` or from a `stream<byte[], error?>` with `yaml:parseStream`
Parse YAML into a generic value such as `json` or `map<json>` when there is no record type for it
Map nested YAML mappings and sequences to nested record types and array fields, e.g. a `database` mapping to a `DatabaseConfig` field
Project YAML onto closed records to drop unwanted keys (e.g. a `password`) and onto fixed-length arrays such as `int[2]` to keep only the first members of a sequence
Adjust projection with `yaml:Options`: `allowDataProjection: false` to reject extra content, or `allowDataProjection: {nilAsOptionalField: true, absentAsNilableType: true}`
Parse a multi-document YAML stream into a tuple, setting `allowDataProjection: {enableYamlStreamReorder: true}` so documents are matched to tuple members even when their order is unknown

sources.note: enableYamlStreamReorder: yaml document to top level tuple value will be re-ordered

must_cover.text: Choose the YAML schema used to resolve scalars with `schema: yaml:FAILSAFE_SCHEMA`, `yaml:JSON_SCHEMA` or `yaml:CORE_SCHEMA` (default), and control `allowAnchorRedefinition` and `allowMapEntryRedefinition`
Serialize a record, map or `json` value to YAML text with `yaml:toYamlString(value)`, which returns `string|yaml:Error`

Format output with `yaml:WriteConfig` options such as `indentationPolicy`, `blockLevel`, `flowStyle`, `useSingleQuotes`, `forceQuotes`, `canonical` and `isStream` for writing a stream of YAML documents
Rely on `@constraint` annotations on the target type being validated during parsing (`enableConstraintValidation`, on by default)
Handle `yaml:Error` returned for malformed YAML or values that do not match the target type

out_of_scope: TOML handling (lib.toml)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)
Reading files (lib.io)

sources.note: Public API with Options and WriteConfig

edges.note: both parse configuration-style documents

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-data.yaml master 1.0.1 (= latest tag). Option and WriteConfig semantics come from field doc comments in yaml_api.bal; the stream-reorder behaviour is documented only briefly, so the item stays at that level.

nodes.title: ballerina/edi
nodes.summary: The `edi` module provides schema-driven, envelope-aware conversion between X12 or EDIFACT EDI text and JSON or typed records, schema-free envelope header inspection, and is the runtime behind parsers generated by the `bal edi` tool and the prebuilt `ballerinax/edifact.d03a.*` packages.

must_cover.text: Read X12 envelope headers without a schema with `edi:x12HeadersFromEdiString` (or `edi:x12HeadersFromEdiFile`), getting an `edi:X12Headers` with the `isa` segment (`senderId`, `receiverId`, `controlNumber`) and an optional `gs` (`edi:X12GS?`)

Read EDIFACT envelope headers without a schema with `edi:edifactHeadersFromEdiString` (or `edi:edifactHeadersFromEdiFile`), getting `unb` (sender, recipient, `controlRef`) and an optional `unh` with its `messageIdentifier`
Route inbound EDI messages by trading partner or message type using the schema-free header functions before any full parse

Parse a UN/EDIFACT D03A message into a typed record with a prebuilt package, e.g. `import ballerinax/edifact.d03a.supplychain.mORDERS;` and `mORDERS:EDI_ORDERS_ORDERS po = check mORDERS:fromEdiString(text);`
Build a typed EDI record and serialize it to EDI text with the generated `toEdiString` function, e.g. `mORDERS:toEdiString(purchaseOrder)`

Parse a full interchange with `interchangeFromEdiString` into typed interchange records and iterate its `transactions`, where each `body` is `T|error` so failed messages can be quarantined while the rest are processed
Serialize a full interchange back to EDI text with `interchangeToEdiString`, which recomputes envelope counts

Generate typed records and parser functions from a schema with the EDI tool: `bal tool pull edi`, `bal edi convertEdifactSchema` or `bal edi convertX12Schema` to obtain a JSON schema, then `bal edi codegen -i schema.json -o orders.bal`

Use the low-level API directly: load a JSON EDI schema with `edi:getSchema`, parse a transaction body to `json` with `edi:fromEdiString(text, schema)` and serialize with `edi:toEdiString(json, schema)`

Parse only the envelope headers against a schema with `edi:headersFromEdiString` or `edi:headersFromEdiFile`, and parse the envelope hierarchy into `edi:EdiInterchange`, `edi:EdiFunctionalGroup` and `edi:EdiTransaction` with `edi:interchangeFromEdiString`

Define or adapt a JSON EDI schema for a partner-specific format with `name`, `delimiters` (`segment`, `field`, `component`, `repetition`), `segments` with `code`, `tag`, `minOccurances`/`maxOccurances` and typed `fields`, plus `ignoreSegments`
Handle `edi:Error` and its subtypes `edi:InvalidEnvelopeError`, `edi:SchemaCompatibilityError` and `edi:SerializationError`

out_of_scope: Full command reference of the EDI CLI tool, including libgen (tool.bal_edi)
Sending the parsed transactions to brokers such as Kafka (lib.kafka)

sources.note: EDI specification: envelopes, errors, schema grammar

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-edi master 1.7.1 (= latest tag) and the four EDI BBEs. The prebuilt `ballerinax/edifact.d03a.*` packages are covered here only as consumers of this module; their generated type names follow the BBEs.

nodes.title: ballerina/email
nodes.summary: The email library sends mail over SMTP with `email:SmtpClient` and reads mail over POP3 and IMAP4 with `email:PopClient`/`email:ImapClient` or polling `email:PopListener`/`email:ImapListener` services, with SSL/STARTTLS and attachments.

must_cover.text: Create an `email:SmtpClient` with `check new ("smtp.email.com", "sender@email.com", "pass123")`, optionally passing `email:SmtpConfiguration` with `port` (465 SSL by default, 587 for STARTTLS)
Compose an `email:Message` with `to`, `cc`, `bcc` (a string or string array), `subject`, `body`, `'from`, `sender` and `replyTo`, and send it with `smtpClient->sendMessage(email)`
Send mail without building a record by calling `smtpClient->send(to, subject, from, body = "...", cc = [...], bcc = [...], replyTo = [...])` with named arguments
Send HTML mail with `htmlBody` and attach files with `attachments` set to an `email:Attachment {filePath, contentType}`, an array of them, or `mime:Entity` values for complex MIME parts

Read mail with `email:ImapClient` or `email:PopClient` (`check new (host, username, password)`), calling `receiveMessage(timeout = 30)` which returns `email:Message?`, in a loop, and `close()` the client when done

Poll for new mail with `listener email:ImapListener` (or `email:PopListener`) configured with `host`, `username`, `password`, `pollingInterval` and `port`, and a `service` with `remote function onMessage(email:Message email)`, `onError(email:Error)` and `onClose(email:Error?)`

Choose transport security with the `security` field (`email:SSL`, `email:START_TLS_AUTO`, `email:START_TLS_ALWAYS`, `email:START_TLS_NEVER`) and configure certificates with `secureSocket: {cert, protocol, ciphers, verifyHostName}` on clients and listeners, matching the protocol's standard ports

Authenticate SMTP with OAuth2 (XOAUTH2) by setting `auth` in `email:SmtpConfiguration` to an access-token string or an `oauth2:ClientCredentialsGrantConfig`/`oauth2:PasswordGrantConfig`, omitting the password and passing `clientConfig = smtpConfig`

out_of_scope: Building MIME entities in depth (lib.mime)
OAuth2 grant configuration details (lib.oauth2)
nodes.notes: SMTP OAuth2 support appears in the email 2.14.2 README (master == latest tag at research time).

nodes.title: ballerina/file
nodes.summary: The `file` module creates, deletes, copies and renames files and directories, reads file metadata, manipulates paths in an OS-independent way, and provides a directory listener that reacts to file create, modify and delete events.

must_cover.text: Inspect paths with `file:getAbsolutePath`, `file:isAbsolutePath`, `file:basename` and `file:parentPath`, each returning a value or a `file:Error`

Build and decompose paths portably with `file:joinPath("/", "foo", "bar")`, `file:splitPath`, `file:relativePath(base, target)` and `file:normalizePath(path, file:CLEAN)` (other options `file:SYMLINK`, `file:NORMCASE`)
Use `file:pathSeparator` (`/` on Unix, `\` on Windows) and `file:pathListSeparator` (`:` or `;`) instead of hard-coding separators
Get the program's working directory with `file:getCurrentDir()`
Create an empty file with `file:create(path)` and a directory with `file:createDir(path)`, passing `file:RECURSIVE` to create missing parent directories
Check a path with `file:test(path, option)` using `file:EXISTS`, `file:IS_DIR`, `file:IS_SYMLINK`, `file:READABLE` or `file:WRITABLE`

Copy files or directories with `file:copy(source, destination, ...options)` using `file:REPLACE_EXISTING`, `file:COPY_ATTRIBUTES` or `file:NO_FOLLOW_LINKS`, and move or rename with `file:rename(oldPath, newPath)`
Delete a file or empty directory with `file:remove(path)` and a non-empty directory tree with `file:remove(path, file:RECURSIVE)`
Read file metadata with `file:getMetaData(path)`, returning a readonly `file:MetaData` record with `absPath`, `size`, `modifiedTime` (a `time:Utc`), `dir`, `readable` and `writable`
List a directory's entries with `file:readDir(path)`, which returns `file:MetaData[]`, and filter them, e.g. by `dir` or file extension

Create temporary files and directories with `file:createTemp()` and `file:createTempDir()`, optionally passing `suffix`, `prefix` and `dir` (e.g. `file:createTemp(dir = tmpDir)`), which return the absolute path
Declare a directory listener with `listener file:Listener inFolder = new ({path: "/data/in", recursive: false});`, setting `recursive: true` to also watch subdirectories
Attach a service to a `file:Listener` with remote methods `onCreate`, `onModify` and `onDelete` that each take a `file:FileEvent` (with `name` and `operation` fields)

Annotate `onCreate` or `onModify` with `@file:FunctionConfig` to delete or move the file after processing, using `afterProcess` and `afterError` set to `file:DELETE` or a `file:Move` record such as `{moveTo: "/data/archive", preserveSubDirs: true}`
Handle `file:Error` and its distinct subtypes such as `file:FileNotFoundError`, `file:PermissionError`, `file:InvalidOperationError` and `file:IOError`

Avoid path injection (static rule `ballerina/file:2`): do not build paths passed to `file:` functions from untrusted input without validating that the resolved path stays inside the intended directory

sources.note: 6.2 File function calls should not be vulnerable to path injection attacks

out_of_scope: Reading and writing file contents (lib.io)
Remote file transfer over FTP/SFTP (lib.ftp)
Listener and service lifecycle in general (concept.services_listeners)

edges.note: lib.file manages files and paths; lib.io reads and writes their contents

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-file master 1.14.0 (= latest tag). `@file:FunctionConfig` post-processing is documented in the current README and spec. Static rule `ballerina/file:1` (publicly writable directories) is not covered as a separate item.

nodes.title: ballerina/ftp
nodes.summary: The FTP library reads, writes and manages files on FTP, SFTP and FTPS servers with `ftp:Client`, and reacts to new or deleted files with a polling `ftp:Listener` whose services bind file content to typed handler parameters.

must_cover.text: Create an `ftp:Client` with `check new ({protocol: ftp:FTP, host, port, auth: {credentials: {username, password}}})`, where `protocol` defaults to FTP

Write files with the typed methods `putText`, `putJson` (json or a record), `putXml`, `putCsv` (`string[][]` or a record array, writing a header row), `putBytes`, and `putBytesAsStream`/`putCsvAsStream` for large data, passing `ftp:APPEND` instead of the default `OVERWRITE` to append

Read files with `getText`, `getJson`, `getXml`, `getCsv` and `getBytes`, binding JSON/XML/CSV to the expected type (e.g. `User u = check ftpClient->getJson(path)`, `Person[] rows = check ftpClient->getCsv(path)`), and stream large files with `getBytesAsStream`/`getCsvAsStream`, closing the stream
Manage remote files and directories with `list` (returning `ftp:FileInfo[]`), `mkdir`, `rmdir` (recursive), `delete`, `rename`/`move`, `copy`, `exists`, `size` and `isDirectory`
Connect over SFTP with `protocol: ftp:SFTP`, port 22 and `auth` holding `credentials` and/or `privateKey: {path, password}`

Connect over FTPS with `protocol: ftp:FTPS` and `auth.secureSocket` holding `key`/`cert` keystores, `mode: ftp:EXPLICIT` (port 21) or `ftp:IMPLICIT` (port 990) and `dataChannelProtection: ftp:PRIVATE`

Watch a remote directory with `listener ftp:Listener` (connection fields plus `pollingInterval`) and a service annotated `@ftp:ServiceConfig {path: "/home/in", fileNamePattern: "(.*).txt"}`, so several services on one listener can watch different directories

Process new files with content handlers that receive bound content first, then optional `ftp:FileInfo` and `ftp:Caller`: `onFileText(string)`, `onFileJson(json|record)`, `onFileXml(xml|record)`, `onFileCsv(string[][]|record[]|stream)` and `onFile(byte[]|stream<byte[], error?>)`, routed by file extension
Override extension-based routing with `@ftp:FunctionConfig {fileNamePattern: ...}` on a handler, and react to removed files with `remote function onFileDelete(string deletedFile)`
Move or delete files after handling with `@ftp:FunctionConfig {afterProcess: {moveTo: "/home/processed"}, afterError: {moveTo: "/home/failed"}}` or `ftp:DELETE`
Use the `ftp:Caller` handler parameter to act on the server while processing a file, e.g. `caller->putText(fileInfo.pathDecoded, receipt, ftp:APPEND)` or `caller->move(...)`

Handle content binding failures in `remote function onError(ftp:Error err, ftp:Caller caller)`, checking for `ftp:ContentBindingError` and reading `err.detail().filePath`, and use `csvFailSafe: {contentType: ftp:RAW_AND_METADATA}` to skip malformed CSV rows

Filter picked-up files in `@ftp:ServiceConfig` with `fileAgeFilter: {minAge, maxAge}` to skip files still being written and `fileDependencyConditions` (`targetPattern`, `requiredFiles`, `matchingMode`) to wait for companion files

Handle the `ftp:Error` hierarchy, checking specific types such as `ftp:FileNotFoundError`, `ftp:FileAlreadyExistsError`, `ftp:ConnectionError`, `ftp:ServiceUnavailableError` and `ftp:CircuitBreakerOpenError` before the general type

Add client resiliency with `retryConfig: {count, interval, backOffFactor, maxWaitInterval}` for whole-file reads (failing with `ftp:AllRetryAttemptsFailedError`) and `circuitBreaker: {failureThreshold, resetTime, rollingWindow, failureCategories}`
Run several listener instances against one directory without duplicate processing using `coordination: {memberId, coordinationGroup, databaseConfig, livenessCheckInterval, heartbeatFrequency}`

out_of_scope: Local file system operations (lib.file, lib.io)
SMB file shares (ballerina/smb is not in this graph)
General CSV and XML data binding outside file transfer (lib.data.csv, lib.data.xmldata)
nodes.notes: Per the 2.22 spec, untyped `get`, `put` and `append`, the `onFileChange`/`ftp:WatchEvent` handler, `onFileDeleted`, and listener-level `path`/`fileNamePattern` are deprecated, so they are not items. The README still shows `put` with `compressionType=ZIP` and listener-level `path`; these were omitted as deprecated.

nodes.title: ballerina/graphql
nodes.summary: The GraphQL library generates a GraphQL schema from a Ballerina service (resource methods are queries, remote methods are mutations, `subscribe` resources are subscriptions) and provides a GraphQL client with data-bound `query`, `mutate` and `subscribe` operations.

must_cover.text: Create a `graphql:Listener` from a port (`new graphql:Listener(9090)`) or an existing `http:Listener`, and attach a `service graphql:Service /graphql on ...` whose schema is generated automatically

Define `Query` fields with `resource function get <name>(args) returns T`, use scalar arguments (`int`, `string`, `boolean`, `float`, `decimal`) as field arguments, and create nested object types with hierarchical resource paths such as `resource function get profile/name/first()`
Define `Mutation` fields with `remote function` methods in the service, e.g. `remote function updateName(int id, string name) returns Profile|error`

Define `Subscription` fields with `resource function subscribe <name>() returns stream<T, error?>` (e.g. from a stream generator class), served to clients over WebSocket with the `graphql-transport-ws` protocol

Return records, arrays, tables, enums and nilable types (`Profile?`) from resolvers so they map to GraphQL object, list, enum and nullable types, with nested record fields becoming nested object types
Return `service class` objects whose `resource function get` methods become fields of an output object type, so fields can take arguments and compute values lazily

Accept input objects as record-typed parameters (e.g. `remote function addProfile(NewProfile newProfile)`), enums and lists as arguments, mark `ID` scalars with `@graphql:ID`, and validate inputs with `@constraint` annotations on the input record

Model GraphQL interfaces as `distinct service object` types implemented by `distinct service class`es (including interfaces that include other interfaces with `*Profile`), and GraphQL unions as unions of distinct service classes such as `type SearchResult Profile|Address`
Return `T|error` (or `T|error?` for nullable fields) from resolvers so failures appear in the response `errors` array with partial `data`, knowing a resolver cannot return only `error`

Use `graphql:Context` by declaring a `contextInit` function `(http:RequestContext, http:Request) returns graphql:Context|error` in `@graphql:ServiceConfig`, storing values with `context.set()` and reading them in resolvers with `context.get()` (e.g. for authorization checks)
Take a `graphql:Field` parameter in a resolver and inspect the selection with `'field.getName()` and `'field.getSubfieldNames()` to avoid fetching unrequested data

Write interceptors as `readonly service class`es including `*graphql:Interceptor` with `isolated remote function execute(graphql:Context context, graphql:Field 'field) returns anydata|error` that call `context.resolve('field)`, and engage them service-wide via `@graphql:ServiceConfig {interceptors: [...]}` or per field via `@graphql:ResourceConfig`, with `@graphql:InterceptorConfig {global: false}`

Solve the N+1 problem with `ballerina/graphql.dataloader`: register a `dataloader:DefaultDataLoader` with a batch function via `ctx.registerDataLoader()` in `contextInit`, add keys in a prefetch method (`pre<Field>` by convention or named with `@graphql:ResourceConfig {prefetchMethodName}`), and read results with `ctx.getDataLoader(name).get(key)`

Enable response caching for whole operations with `@graphql:ServiceConfig {cacheConfig: {}}` or per field with `@graphql:ResourceConfig {cacheConfig: {maxAge, maxSize}}` (or `enabled: false`), and evict entries from mutations with `context.invalidate("field")` and `context.invalidateAll()`
Limit query cost with `@graphql:ServiceConfig {queryComplexityConfig: {maxComplexity, defaultFieldComplexity}}` and per-field `@graphql:ResourceConfig {complexity: n}`
Accept file uploads in mutations with a `graphql:Upload` parameter, reading `file.fileName` and writing `file.byteStream` to disk

Enable the GraphiQL client with `@graphql:ServiceConfig {graphiql: {enabled: true, path: "/testing"}}`, document the schema with Ballerina doc comments (`#` lines become descriptions), and mark fields or enum members deprecated with `@deprecated`

Secure a GraphQL service with `secureSocket` on the `graphql:Listener` (TLS and mutual TLS) and `@graphql:ServiceConfig {auth: [...]}` using `fileUserStoreConfig`, `ldapUserStoreConfig`, `jwtValidatorConfig` or `oauth2IntrospectionConfig` with `scopes`

Consume GraphQL APIs with `graphql:Client` using `query(document, variables)` and `mutate(document, variables)` with the response bound to a record containing `data` (include `*graphql:GenericResponseWithErrors` to also receive `errors` for partial responses), `subscribe(document)` returning a stream, and the `auth`/`secureSocket` client settings

Handle `graphql:ClientError` subtypes from client calls, such as `graphql:PayloadBindingError`, `graphql:InvalidDocumentError` (also returned when the document does not match the invoked method) and `graphql:HttpError`, using `do`/`on fail` and type tests

out_of_scope: HTTP listener and request details beneath GraphQL (lib.http)
Generating GraphQL schemas and clients with the CLI (tool.bal_graphql)
Constraint annotation definitions (lib.constraint)
nodes.notes: In graphql 1.19.x the client's `execute()` and `executeWithType()` are deprecated in favour of `query()`, `mutate()` and `subscribe()`; the BBE client examples still call `execute()`, so items follow the module source and README. SSL/TLS and auth BBEs for the client exist but are folded into client_operations.

nodes.title: ballerina/grpc
nodes.summary: The gRPC library implements gRPC services and clients over HTTP/2 from Protocol Buffers definitions, supporting unary, server-streaming, client-streaming and bidirectional-streaming RPCs, headers, deadlines and security.

must_cover.text: Start from a `.proto` service definition and generate the Ballerina stub (`*_pb.bal` with message records, the `<Service>Client` and the descriptor constant) using `bal grpc --input <file>.proto --mode service|client --output <dir>`, then copy it into the package

Implement a unary RPC as `service "HelloWorld" on new grpc:Listener(9090)` annotated with `@grpc:Descriptor {value: <DESC_CONSTANT>}`, where each RPC is a `remote function hello(string request) returns string|error`
Call a unary RPC through the generated client, e.g. `HelloWorldClient ep = check new ("http://localhost:9090"); string result = check ep->hello("WSO2");`

Implement server streaming by returning `stream<string, error?>` (e.g. `greets.toStream()`) from the remote function, and consume it on the client as `stream<string, grpc:Error?>` with `forEach` or a query action

Implement client streaming with a `stream<T, error?> clientStream` parameter iterated by `from ... in clientStream do {...}`, and on the client obtain the generated streaming client (e.g. `LotsOfGreetingsStreamingClient`) to call `sendString()`, `complete()` and `receiveString()`

Implement bidirectional streaming with a generated caller parameter (e.g. `ChatStringCaller caller`) plus the client stream, replying with `caller->sendString()` and `caller->complete()`, and on the client send with `sendChatMessage()` while reading responses concurrently (e.g. a `start`ed reader calling `receiveString()` until nil)

Send and read gRPC headers with context records such as `wrappers:ContextString {content, headers}` from `ballerina/protobuf.types.wrappers`, call the generated `*Context` client method (e.g. `helloContext`), and read values with `grpc:getHeader(headers, "key")`

Set a call deadline on the client with `grpc:setDeadline(time:utcAddSeconds(time:utcNow(), 5))` passed as headers, and check it in the service with `grpc:isCancelled(request.headers)`, returning `error grpc:DeadlineExceededError(...)`

Handle gRPC status errors as `grpc:Error` subtypes such as `grpc:NotFoundError`, `grpc:InvalidArgumentError`, `grpc:UnauthenticatedError`, `grpc:UnavailableError` and `grpc:DeadlineExceededError`, and return such errors from service methods (e.g. `return error grpc:NotFoundError("...")`) instead of a response

Secure gRPC with `secureSocket`: listener `key: {certFile, keyFile}` (plus `mutualSsl: {verifyClient: grpc:REQUIRE, cert}` for mTLS) and client `cert` (plus `key`), connecting the client to an `https://` URL
Secure gRPC services with `@grpc:ServiceConfig {auth: [...]}` using `fileUserStoreConfig`, `ldapUserStoreConfig`, `jwtValidatorConfig` or `oauth2IntrospectionConfig` with `scopes`
Authenticate gRPC client calls with the `auth` config of the generated client: Basic, bearer token, self-signed JWT and OAuth2 client credentials, password, refresh token and JWT bearer grants
Configure client retries with `retryConfiguration: {retryCount, interval, maxInterval, backoffFactor, errorTypes}` and request gzip compression by adding headers from `grpc:setCompression()`
Enable gRPC server reflection with `new grpc:Listener(9090, {reflectionEnabled: true})` so tools can discover services without the stub

Explain how protobuf types map to Ballerina: wrapper types to `int`, `float`, `string`, `boolean`, `byte[]`, `google.protobuf.Empty` to `()`, `Timestamp` to `time:Utc`, `Duration` to `time:Seconds`, `Struct` to `map<anydata>`, `Any` to `'any:Any`, and messages to records

sources.note: 3. Protocol buffers to Ballerina data mapping

out_of_scope: The `bal grpc` command options in depth (tool.bal_grpc)
Protobuf well-known type submodules and `'any:pack`/`unpack` (lib.protobuf)
JWT and OAuth2 internals (lib.jwt, lib.oauth2)
nodes.notes: In the BBEs the gRPC service name is a string literal matching the proto service (`service "HelloWorld" on ...`); the README also shows an identifier form. The README's client-streaming sample uses `sendstring` (lowercase) while the BBE uses `sendString`; items follow the BBE.

nodes.title: ballerina/http
nodes.summary: The HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 library that exposes REST services through `http:Listener` and resource methods and calls remote endpoints through `http:Client`, with data binding, interceptors, security and resiliency built in.

must_cover.text: Declare an HTTP service with `service /base on new http:Listener(9090)` (or a module-level `listener http:Listener`), write `resource function get|post|put|patch|delete` methods with hierarchical resource paths, use `.` for the service root, and catch all methods and paths with `resource function 'default [string... paths]`

Bind request data to resource parameters: path parameters such as `albums/[string title]`, query parameters as plain typed parameters (`string artist`, `int id = 10`, nilable `string?` for optional, arrays for repeated values, `@http:Query` for structured types), and headers with `@http:Header string accept`, `@http:Header {name: "x-api-version"}`, a header record, or an `http:Headers` parameter

Bind the request body to a typed parameter: a single record, array, `map<json>`, table or `xml` parameter of a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE resource is the payload by default, `@http:Payload` marks other types (e.g. `string`), mismatches return 400, and `@constraint` annotations on the record are validated automatically

Return `anydata` (records, arrays, `json`, `xml`, `string`, `byte[]`) from resource methods and rely on automatic serialization and Content-Type inference, the default status codes (201 for POST, 200 otherwise, 202 when returning nil), `returns error?`, and `@http:Payload {mediaType: "..."}` on the return type to override the media type

Return specific status codes with status code response types and constants such as `http:NotFound`/`http:NOT_FOUND`, `http:Conflict`, `http:Created`, `http:Accepted`, `http:BadRequest`, `http:TemporaryRedirect`, and define custom subtypes like `record {| *http:Created; Album body; |}` with `body`, `headers` and `mediaType` fields in union return types such as `Album|http:NotFound`

Work with the low-level message objects: take an `http:Request` parameter and read it with `getJsonPayload()`, `getTextPayload()`, `getHeader()`, `getQueryParamValue()`, `getMatrixParams()`; build an `http:Response` with `setPayload()`, `setHeader()` and `statusCode`; and respond explicitly through an `http:Caller` with `caller->respond(...)` (including `100-continue` handling)

Call HTTP endpoints with `http:Client` created by `check new ("localhost:9090")`, using resource-access syntax `albumClient->/albums`, `->/albums/[id]`, `->/albums.post(payload)`, query parameters as named arguments `->/albums(artist = "x")` and a header map argument, or the remote methods `get("/path")`, `post("/path", payload)`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `execute` and `forward("/path", req)` for passthrough proxies

Bind client responses directly to the expected type (`Album[] albums = check albumClient->/albums;`, `json|xml`, nilable types for empty bodies, `targetType = json` with `var`), take the whole `http:Response` when headers or status are needed, use `http:StatusCodeClient` to bind to status code records, and handle `http:PayloadValidationError` when `@constraint` checks fail

Handle client failures as `http:ClientError`, distinguishing 4xx/5xx responses (`http:ClientRequestError`, `http:RemoteServerError`, both `http:ApplicationResponseError`) whose `detail()` carries `statusCode`, `headers` and `body`, from connection-level and resiliency errors

Explain the default error handling (an `error` returned or `check`ed in a resource becomes a 500 response, and listener errors such as binding or dispatching failures map to 400/404/405/415 or 401/403) and override it with `do`/`on fail` or an error interceptor (`*http:ResponseErrorInterceptor` with `remote function interceptResponseError(error err)`, or `*http:RequestErrorInterceptor`) that returns a consistent error payload

Write request and response interceptors as service classes including `*http:RequestInterceptor` (a `resource function 'default [string... path](http:RequestContext ctx, ...)` returning `ctx.next()`) and `*http:ResponseInterceptor` (`remote function interceptResponse(http:RequestContext ctx, http:Response res)`), engage them from `service http:InterceptableService` via `createInterceptors()`, and share data with `ctx.set()`/`ctx.get()`

Configure services and resources with `@http:ServiceConfig` and `@http:ResourceConfig`: CORS via `cors: {allowOrigins, allowCredentials, allowHeaders, exposeHeaders, maxAge}`, and content negotiation via `consumes` and `produces` media type lists

Secure services declaratively with `@http:ServiceConfig {auth: [...]}` (or per resource with `@http:ResourceConfig`) using `fileUserStoreConfig` or `ldapUserStoreConfig` for Basic auth, `jwtValidatorConfig` (issuer, audience, `signatureConfig`, `scopeKey`) for JWT, or `oauth2IntrospectionConfig` for OAuth2, together with required `scopes`

Authenticate outbound requests with the client `auth` field: Basic (`username`, `password`), bearer `token`, self-signed JWT (`issuer`, `audience`, `signatureConfig`), and OAuth2 client credentials, password (`refreshConfig: oauth2:INFER_REFRESH_CONFIG`), refresh token and JWT bearer grants via `tokenUrl`/`refreshUrl`, `clientId`, `clientSecret` and `scopes`

Enable HTTPS with `secureSocket`: on the listener `key: {certFile, keyFile}` and for mutual TLS `mutualSsl: {verifyClient: http:REQUIRE, cert}`; on the client `cert` to trust the server and `key` to present a client certificate

Make clients resilient with `timeout`, `retryConfig {interval, count, backOffFactor, maxWaitInterval}`, `circuitBreaker {rollingWindow, failureThreshold, resetTime, statusCodes}`, `http:LoadBalanceClient` with round-robin `targets`, and `http:FailoverClient` with `targets`, `failoverCodes` and `interval`

Add response caching with `returns @http:Cache {maxAge: 15} Album|http:NotFound` (setting Cache-Control, ETag and Last-Modified) and a caching client via the `cache` config (e.g. `isShared: true`), and control compression with `compression: {enable: http:COMPRESSION_ALWAYS, contentTypes}` in `@http:ServiceConfig` or the client configuration

Manage cookies and redirects: create `http:Cookie` values and add them with `response.addCookie()`, read them with `request.getCookies()`, enable client cookie handling with `cookieConfig: {enabled: true}`, and follow 3xx responses with `followRedirects: {enabled: true, maxCount: 5}`

Send and receive files and multipart messages: upload with `request.setFileAsPayload(path, contentType = mime:APPLICATION_PDF)`, stream large bodies with `request.getByteStream()`, build multipart bodies with `mime:Entity` parts and `setBodyParts(parts, contentType = mime:MULTIPART_FORM_DATA)`, and decode them with `getBodyParts()`

Stream server-sent events by returning `stream<http:SseEvent, error?>` from a resource and consuming it on the client as `stream<http:SseEvent, error?>`; choose protocol behaviour knowing HTTP/2 is the default, with `httpVersion = http:HTTP_1_1` to downgrade, `http2Settings: {http2PriorKnowledge: true}`, chunking via `chunking: http:CHUNKING_ALWAYS` or `http1Settings`, and HTTP/2 server push with `http:PushPromise`

out_of_scope: General resource method syntax and service/listener semantics of the language (concept.resource_methods, concept.services_listeners)
Designing REST APIs end to end (topic.rest_api)
Generating services and clients from OpenAPI (tool.bal_openapi)
MIME entity API details beyond HTTP multipart usage (lib.mime)
JWT and OAuth2 token handling outside HTTP configuration (lib.jwt, lib.oauth2)
Constraint annotation definitions (lib.constraint)
HTTP trace and access log Config.toml settings (topic.observability)
nodes.notes: Item texts follow ballerina/http 2.18.1 (master == latest tag at research time). HTTP trace/access logs (`ballerina.http.traceLogAdvancedConfig`, `ballerina.http.accessLogConfig` in Config.toml), proxy config, service contract types (`*http:ServiceContract`), `laxDataBinding`, imperative auth handlers and OpenAPI introspection resources are documented but were not given their own item because of the 20-item cap.

nodes.title: ballerinax/ibm.ibmmq
nodes.summary: IBM MQ connector: connect to a queue manager with `ibmmq:QueueManager`, put and get messages on `ibmmq:Queue` and `ibmmq:Topic` clients, and consume asynchronously with an `ibmmq:Listener` service.

must_cover.text: Add the IBM MQ client jar as a platform dependency in `Ballerina.toml` with a `[[platform.java21.dependency]]` entry for `groupId = "com.ibm.mq"`, `artifactId = "com.ibm.mq.allclient"`

Connect with `ibmmq:QueueManager queueManager = check new (name = queueManagerName, host = host, port = port, channel = channel, userID = userID, password = password)`, typically from `configurable` values, and end the connection with `queueManager.disconnect()`
Open a queue with `queueManager.accessQueue(queueName, ibmmq:MQOO_OUTPUT)` or combined open options such as `ibmmq:MQOO_OUTPUT | ibmmq:MQOO_INPUT_AS_Q_DEF`, and close it with `queue->close()`

Send a message with `queue->put({payload: "...".toBytes()})`, setting `ibmmq:Message` fields such as `properties`, `correlationId`, `replyToQueueName`, `priority`, `persistence` and `expiry`, and optional put options such as `ibmmq:MQPMO_NO_SYNCPOINT`

Receive with `queue->get(options = ibmmq:MQGMO_WAIT, waitInterval = ...)`, which returns `ibmmq:Message?`, optionally selecting by `matchOptions` (`messageId`, `correlationId`), and decode the body with `string:fromBytes(message.payload)`

Publish and subscribe on topics with `queueManager.accessTopic(topicName, topicString, ibmmq:OPEN_AS_PUBLICATION, ibmmq:MQOO_OUTPUT)` (or `ibmmq:OPEN_AS_SUBSCRIPTION`), then `topic->put(...)`/`topic->get()`, or `topic->send(message)` for JMS-compatible delivery

Attach IBM MQ headers through the `headers` field, e.g. an `ibmmq:MQRFH2` with `flags` and a `fieldValues` table of `{folder, 'field, value}` entries, or `ibmmq:MQIIH`, `ibmmq:MQCIH`, `ibmmq:MQRFH`, and read them back from consumed messages
Secure the connection by passing `sslCipherSuite = ibmmq:TLS12ORHIGHER` and `secureSocket = {cert: {path, password}, key: {path, password}}` (truststore and keystore) to the `ibmmq:QueueManager`

Consume asynchronously with `listener ibmmq:Listener ibmmqListener = new ({name, host, port, channel, userID, password})` and a service annotated `@ibmmq:ServiceConfig {queueName, pollingInterval}` implementing `remote function onMessage(ibmmq:Message message) returns error?`

Subscribe a service to a topic with `@ibmmq:ServiceConfig {topicName, consumerType: ibmmq:DURABLE, subscriberName}`, optionally filtering with `messageSelector` and tuning `pollingInterval` and `receiveTimeout`

Set `sessionAckMode: ibmmq:CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE` or `ibmmq:SESSION_TRANSACTED` in `@ibmmq:ServiceConfig`, add an `ibmmq:Caller caller` parameter to `onMessage`, and call `caller->acknowledge(message)`, `caller->'commit()` or `caller->'rollback()`

Handle `ibmmq:Error` values, whose `ibmmq:ErrorDetails` detail carries `reasonCode`, `errorCode` and `completionCode`, and add `remote function onError(ibmmq:Error err) returns error?` to a service for receive or dispatch failures

out_of_scope: Generic JMS providers and the JMS session API (lib.java.jms)
Configurable variables and Config.toml (tool.config_toml)
Declaring platform dependencies in Ballerina.toml in general (tool.ballerina_toml)

nodes.title: ballerina/io
nodes.summary: The `io` module provides console I/O and file read/write APIs for bytes, strings, lines, CSV, JSON and XML, in both whole-content and streaming forms, plus lower-level byte, character, CSV and data channels.

must_cover.text: Print one or more values to standard output with `io:println` and `io:print`, which accept any number of `any`, `error` or string-template values and write them without separators

Write to standard error or standard output explicitly with `io:fprintln(io:stderr, ...)` and `io:fprint(io:stdout, ...)`, where the first argument is an `io:FileOutputStream` (`io:stdout` or `io:stderr`)
Read a line of user input with `io:readln("Enter choice: ")` (the optional argument is printed as a prompt), get it as a `string` and convert it as needed, e.g. with `int:fromString`
Read a whole file as a `readonly & byte[]` with `io:fileReadBytes` and write a `byte[]` with `io:fileWriteBytes`, e.g. to copy a binary file such as an image

Stream large binary files with `io:fileReadBlocksAsStream(path, blockSize)`, which returns `stream<io:Block, io:Error?>` (default block size 4096 bytes), and write a byte stream with `io:fileWriteBlocksFromStream`
Read a whole text file into a `string` with `io:fileReadString` and write a string with `io:fileWriteString`
Read a file as a `string[]` of lines with `io:fileReadLines` (line terminators removed) and write a `string[]` with `io:fileWriteLines`, which adds a newline after each line

Process a large text file line by line with `io:fileReadLinesAsStream`, which returns `stream<string, io:Error?>`, iterating with `foreach` or `forEach`, and write a line stream (e.g. `lines.toStream()`) with `io:fileWriteLinesFromStream`

Append instead of overwrite by passing `io:APPEND` as the `io:FileWriteOption` argument (default `io:OVERWRITE`) to `io:fileWriteString`, `io:fileWriteLines`, `io:fileWriteBytes`, `io:fileWriteCsv` and the stream-writing functions
Read a JSON file into a `json` value with `io:fileReadJson` and write a `json` value with `io:fileWriteJson`

Read an XML file with `io:fileReadXml` and write an `xml` value with `io:fileWriteXml`, using `xmlEntityType: io:EXTERNAL_PARSED_ENTITY` when appending or writing multiple roots (the default `io:DOCUMENT_ENTITY` requires a single root and disallows `io:APPEND`) and `doctype` to emit a DOCTYPE
Read a CSV file as `string[][]` with `io:fileReadCsv` (optionally skipping header rows with `skipHeaders`) and write a `string[][]` with `io:fileWriteCsv`

Map CSV rows to records by declaring the expected type, e.g. `Employee[] rows = check io:fileReadCsv(path);` where the first CSV row holds matching headers, and write a record array with `io:fileWriteCsv`, which writes the headers in `OVERWRITE` mode

Stream CSV content with `io:fileReadCsvAsStream`, typed as `stream<string[], io:Error?>` or `stream<Employee, io:Error?>`, and write a stream of string arrays or records with `io:fileWriteCsvFromStream`

Use byte channels: open an `io:ReadableByteChannel` with `io:openReadableFile` (or `io:createReadableChannel(bytes)` for in-memory content) and call `read(n)`, `readAll()` or `blockStream(size)`; open an `io:WritableByteChannel` with `io:openWritableFile` and call `write(content, offset)`; always `close()` the channel

Wrap a byte channel with `new io:ReadableCharacterChannel(byteChannel, "UTF-8")` to `read(n)`, `readString()`, `readAllLines()`, `readJson()`, `readXml()` or get a `lineStream()`, and with `new io:WritableCharacterChannel(byteChannel, "UTF-8")` to `write`, `writeLine`, `writeJson` or `writeXml`

Read CSV through `io:openReadableCsvFile(path, fieldSeparator, charset, skipHeaders)`, iterating with `hasNext()`/`getNext()` or `csvStream()`, or load it into a keyed table with `toTable(Employee, ["id"])`; write rows with `io:openWritableCsvFile(...)` and `write(string[])`

sources.note: getTable is deprecated in favour of toTable

must_cover.text: Read and write binary primitives with `io:ReadableDataChannel` and `io:WritableDataChannel` (`readInt32`/`writeInt32`, `readFloat64`/`writeFloat64`, `readBool`/`writeBool`, `readString(nBytes, encoding)`/`writeString(value, encoding)`, `readVarInt`/`writeVarInt`), choosing byte order `"BE"` (default) or `"LE"`

Handle `io:Error` returned by every file API with `check` or by testing distinct subtypes such as `io:FileNotFoundError`, `io:AccessDeniedError`, `io:EofError`, `io:TypeMismatchError` and `io:ConfigurationError`

Avoid path injection (static rule `ballerina/io:1`): never concatenate untrusted input into a path passed to `io:fileReadString` and similar functions; map the caller's choice to a fixed path or validate it against a known set

sources.note: 8.1 I/O function calls should not be vulnerable to path injection attacks

out_of_scope: File system operations such as create, delete, copy, metadata and path manipulation (lib.file)
Typed parsing of JSON, XML, CSV and YAML content into records with projection (lib.data.jsondata, lib.data.xmldata, lib.data.csv, lib.data.yaml)
Stream type semantics and stream query expressions (concept.streams, concept.query_expressions)
Logging (lib.log)

nodes.title: ballerinax/java.jdbc
nodes.summary: The generic JDBC connector: a `jdbc:Client` that implements the `sql:Client` API for any relational database reachable through a JDBC URL and a driver JAR added to the package.

must_cover.text: Add the JDBC driver of the target database to `Ballerina.toml` under `[[platform.java17.dependency]]`, either with `path = "..."` to a downloaded JAR or with Maven coordinates (e.g. `groupId = "com.h2database"`, `artifactId = "h2"`, `version = "2.0.206"`)

Create a `jdbc:Client` from a JDBC URL, e.g. `jdbc:Client dbClient = check new ("jdbc:h2:~/path/to/database", "root", "root");` (url, user, password), where the URL is mandatory and user/password are optional
Configure `jdbc:Options` with a `datasourceName` (e.g. `"org.h2.jdbcx.JdbcDataSource"`) and driver `properties` such as `{"loginTimeout": "2000"}` applied to that data source

Control for which operations auto-generated keys are requested with `requestGeneratedKeys` in `jdbc:Options` (`jdbc:NONE`, `jdbc:EXECUTE`, `jdbc:BATCH_EXECUTE`, `jdbc:ALL`, default `ALL`), knowing a `jdbc:sqlserver` URL only accepts `EXECUTE` or `NONE`

Pass `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}` or a shared `sql:ConnectionPool` record to `jdbc:Client` with named arguments (e.g. `new (url = "jdbc:...", connectionPool = connPool)`), or omit it to use the global pool

Use the `sql:Client` remote methods on `jdbc:Client` (`query`, `queryRow`, `execute`, `batchExecute`, `call`) against any JDBC database, reading `lastInsertId` from `sql:ExecutionResult` for generated keys
Keep a `jdbc:Client` for the application lifetime and close it with `check dbClient.close()` at shutdown

out_of_scope: Generic query/execute/call semantics, typed values and errors (lib.sql)
Database-specific connectors with dedicated options and types (lib.mysql, lib.postgresql, lib.mssql, lib.oracledb)

nodes.title: ballerinax/java.jms
nodes.summary: Java Message Service connector that works with any JMS provider (such as ActiveMQ) through a `jms:Connection`, `jms:Session`, `jms:MessageProducer` and `jms:MessageConsumer`, plus a `jms:Listener` whose services receive messages asynchronously.

must_cover.text: Bring in the JMS provider's client libraries with a driver import such as `import ballerinax/activemq.driver as _;` next to `import ballerinax/java.jms;`

Open a `jms:Connection` with `check new (initialContextFactory = "org.apache.activemq.jndi.ActiveMQInitialContextFactory", providerUrl = "tcp://localhost:61616")`, optionally setting `connectionFactoryName`, `username`, `password` and `properties`, and control it with `'start()`, `stop()` and `close()`

Create a `jms:Session` with `connection->createSession()` and choose an acknowledgement mode: `jms:AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE` (default), `jms:CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE`, `jms:DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE` or `jms:SESSION_TRANSACTED`
Describe destinations as `jms:Destination` values such as `{'type: jms:QUEUE, name: "order-queue"}`, using `jms:TOPIC`, `jms:TEMPORARY_QUEUE` or `jms:TEMPORARY_TOPIC` as needed

Build messages as `jms:TextMessage` (`string` content), `jms:MapMessage` (`map<anydata>` content) or `jms:BytesMessage` (`byte[]` content), all including `jms:Message` header fields such as `correlationId`, `replyTo` and `properties`
Create a producer with `session.createProducer({'type: jms:QUEUE, name: "order-queue"})` and send with `producer->send(message)`, e.g. a `jms:MapMessage` built from an HTTP request payload
Create a producer without a default destination via `session.createProducer()` and choose the destination per message with `producer->sendTo({'type: jms:QUEUE, name: "order-queue"}, message)`

Create a consumer with `session.createConsumer(destination = {...})` and read messages synchronously with `consumer->receive(timeoutMillis)` or `receiveNoWait()`, which return `jms:Message?`, then narrow with `is jms:TextMessage`, `is jms:MapMessage` or `is jms:BytesMessage`
Acknowledge messages explicitly by creating the session with `jms:CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE` and calling `consumer->acknowledge(message)` after processing

Create durable or shared topic subscriptions with `session.createConsumer({'type: jms:DURABLE, destination: {'type: jms:TOPIC, name: ...}, subscriberName: ...})` (also `jms:SHARED`, `jms:SHARED_DURABLE`), using `messageSelector` and `noLocal`, and remove one with `session->unsubscribe(subscriptionId)`
Send messages atomically using a `jms:SESSION_TRANSACTED` session, calling `session->'commit()` after the sends and `session->'rollback()` in an `on fail` clause

Consume asynchronously with a service on `new jms:Listener(connectionConfig = {initialContextFactory: ..., providerUrl: ...}, consumerOptions = {destination: {'type: jms:QUEUE, name: "MyQueue"}})` that implements `remote function onMessage(jms:Message message) returns error?`

Set `acknowledgementMode = jms:CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE` (or `jms:SESSION_TRANSACTED`) on the `jms:Listener`, add a `jms:Caller caller` parameter to `onMessage`, and call `caller->acknowledge(message)`, `caller->'commit()` or `caller->'rollback()`
Subscribe a listener service to a topic by giving `consumerOptions` with a `jms:TOPIC` destination and, for durable or shared subscriptions, `'type: jms:DURABLE` and a `subscriberName`

out_of_scope: General listener and service declaration semantics (concept.services_listeners)
IBM MQ native queue-manager API (lib.ibm.ibmmq)
Declaring Java platform dependencies in Ballerina.toml (tool.ballerina_toml)

The repository master branch (unreleased) changes the API: `jms:Listener` takes the connection configuration directly, services are bound with `@jms:ServiceConfig {queueName | topicName, sessionAckMode, messageSelector}`, an `onError(jms:Error)` method is added, and the message subtypes are replaced by a single `jms:Message` with `content` of `string|map<jms:Value>|byte[]`.
