nodes.title: ballerina/jballerina.java
nodes.summary: The `jballerina.java` module provides the Java interoperability layer of jBallerina: annotations that bind external Ballerina functions to Java methods, constructors and fields, plus helpers for the `handle` type such as string conversion, null handling and casting.

must_cover.text: Bind a Ballerina function to a static Java method with `function randomUUID() returns handle = @java:Method {'class: "java.util.UUID"} external;`, adding `name: "..."` when the Java method name differs from the Ballerina function name

Call a Java instance method by binding it with `@java:Method` and passing the receiver object as an extra first `handle` parameter, e.g. `function push(handle receiver, handle e) = @java:Method {'class: "java.util.ArrayDeque"} external;`
Create Java objects by binding a function to a constructor with `@java:Constructor {'class: "java.util.ArrayDeque"}`, which returns a `handle` to the new instance

Select an overloaded Java method or constructor with `paramTypes`, listing class names such as `"int"` or `"java.lang.String"` and array types as `java:ArrayType` records like `{'class: "char", dimensions: 1}`
Read or update Java static or instance fields with `@java:FieldGet` and `@java:FieldSet`, e.g. `function pi() returns float = @java:FieldGet {name: "PI", 'class: "java/lang/Math"} external;`
Explain that a `handle` is an opaque reference to a Java object, array or `null` that can only be created by external functions, and keep it as a private field of a Ballerina class for type safety
Convert between Ballerina and Java strings with `java:fromString(s)`, which returns a `handle` to a `java.lang.String`, and `java:toString(h)`, which returns `string?`
Guard against Java `null` by testing a returned handle with `java:isNull(h)` before using it, and pass a Java `null` with `java:createNull()`

Wrap a Java class in a Ballerina class (e.g. `StringStack` holding a private `handle jObj` created in `init`) whose methods call the bound external functions and convert values, to present a typed Ballerina API
Explain that an unchecked Java exception thrown by a bound method becomes a Ballerina panic, and stop it with `trap`, e.g. `handle|error e = trap pop(deque);`

Bind Java methods or constructors that throw checked exceptions by including `error` in the return type (e.g. `returns handle|error`), knowing that the error message is the exception's class name and the detail holds `message` and `cause`

Map types across the boundary: Java `boolean`, `long`/`int`/`short`/`byte`/`char` and `double`/`float` correspond to Ballerina `boolean`, `int` and `float`, any Java reference type to `handle`, and Ballerina `string`, arrays, maps, records, objects and errors are received in Java as runtime API values such as `BString`, `BArray`, `BMap`, `BObject` and `BError`

Pass Ballerina arrays and maps directly to Java code, e.g. `function arrayReverse(int[] arr) returns int[] = @java:Method {'class: "javalibs.app.ArrayReverse"} external;` implemented in Java against `io.ballerina.runtime.api.values.BArray` from the `ballerina-runtime` dependency

Work with generated binding classes that include `java:JObject` (a `handle jObj` field) and convert between them with `java:cast(value, typedesc)` according to Java assignability, and obtain a `java.lang.Class` handle with `java:getClass(name)`

out_of_scope: Generating bindings automatically with `bal bindgen` (tool.bal_bindgen)
Declaring Java platform dependencies (JARs, Maven artifacts) in Ballerina.toml (tool.ballerina_toml)
The `external` function body syntax in the language itself (concept.external_functions)
Writing the Java side against the Ballerina runtime API in depth (scheduling, async `Environment` usage)
nodes.notes: The FFI guide's asynchronous-call example uses `BalEnv`/`BalFuture` names on the Java side; it was not cross-checked against the current runtime API, so it is left out.

nodes.title: ballerina/jwt
nodes.summary: The `jwt` module issues self-signed JWTs and decodes and validates JWTs (RFC 7519/7515/7517), and provides the listener and client JWT auth providers that protocol connectors use for JWT authentication.

must_cover.text: Issue a self-signed JWT with `jwt:issue(issuerConfig)`, building a `jwt:IssuerConfig` with `issuer`, `username` (mapped to `sub`), `audience` (`string` or `string[]`), `keyId` (`kid`), `jwtId` (`jti`) and `expTime` in seconds (default 300)
Add custom claims to an issued JWT with the `customClaims` field (`map<json>`) of `jwt:IssuerConfig`, e.g. `customClaims: {"scp": "admin"}` to carry scopes

Sign an issued JWT through `signatureConfig` (`jwt:IssuerSignatureConfig`): pick `algorithm` (`jwt:RS256` by default, `jwt:RS384`, `jwt:RS512`, `jwt:HS256`, `jwt:HS384`, `jwt:HS512` or `jwt:NONE`) and give `config` as a private-key file record (`keyFile`, optional `keyPassword`), a keystore record (`keyStore`, `keyAlias`, `keyPassword`), a `crypto:PrivateKey`, or a `string` secret for HMAC

Validate a JWT with `jwt:validate(jwt, validatorConfig)`, which checks the signature, expiry and the expected `issuer`, `audience`, `username`, `jwtId`, `keyId` and `customClaims` given in a `jwt:ValidatorConfig` (with `clockSkew` in seconds) and returns the `jwt:Payload` or a `jwt:Error`
Verify JWT signatures by setting `signatureConfig` (`jwt:ValidatorSignatureConfig`) to a `certFile` path or `crypto:PublicKey`, a `trustStoreConfig` (`trustStore`, `certAlias`), or an HMAC `secret`

Validate tokens from an identity provider against its JWKS endpoint with `signatureConfig: {jwksConfig: {url: ...}}`, optionally adding a `cacheConfig` and a `clientConfig` (`jwt:ClientConfiguration` with `httpVersion` and `secureSocket`)
Cache validated JWTs by setting `cacheConfig` (a `cache:CacheConfig`) on `jwt:ValidatorConfig`
Decode a JWT without validating it with `jwt:decode(jwt)`, which returns a `[jwt:Header, jwt:Payload]` tuple or a `jwt:Error`, and destructure the result

Read the registered claims of a `jwt:Payload` (`iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `jti`), custom claims through its open-record fields, and the `jwt:Header` fields `alg`, `typ`, `cty` and `kid`
Authenticate an incoming bearer token with `jwt:ListenerJwtAuthProvider`, constructed from a `jwt:ValidatorConfig`, and its `authenticate(credential)` method returning `jwt:Payload|jwt:Error`
Generate a self-signed token for outbound calls with `jwt:ClientSelfSignedJwtAuthProvider`, constructed from a `jwt:IssuerConfig`, and its `generateToken()` method returning `string|jwt:Error`

Secure a service with JWT by adding a `jwtValidatorConfig` entry (`issuer`, `audience`, `signatureConfig`, and the connector's `scopeKey` naming the scope claim) together with `scopes` to the connector's service `auth` configuration, e.g. `@http:ServiceConfig`

Make a connector client send a self-signed JWT as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by passing JWT issuer fields (`username`, `issuer`, `audience`, `keyId`, `customClaims`, `expTime`, `signatureConfig`) as the client's `auth` configuration, e.g. `http:Client`

out_of_scope: Basic Auth providers and user stores (lib.auth)
OAuth2 grant types and token introspection (lib.oauth2)
Full HTTP auth configuration records such as `http:JwtValidatorConfig` and auth handlers (lib.http)
Low-level signing, key decoding and keystores (lib.crypto)

nodes.title: ballerinax/kafka
nodes.summary: Apache Kafka connector: a `kafka:Producer` client to publish records, a `kafka:Consumer` client to poll them with data binding into Ballerina types, and a `kafka:Listener` that dispatches polled records to `onConsumerRecord` remote methods, with SSL/SASL security and manual offset control.

must_cover.text: Create a `kafka:Producer` with `check new (kafka:DEFAULT_URL, config)` (bootstrap servers as a `string` or `string[]`) and a `kafka:ProducerConfiguration` that sets fields such as `clientId`, `acks: kafka:ACKS_ALL` and `retryCount`

Publish a record with `producer->send({topic: "order-topic", key: ..., value: newOrder})`, where `value` can be any `anydata` such as a record received in an HTTP resource, and use `sendWithMetadata` to get a `kafka:RecordMetadata` (offset, partition, timestamp)
Flush buffered records with `producer->'flush()`, look up partitions with `producer->getTopicPartitions(topic)`, and release the client with `producer->close()`

Create a `kafka:Consumer` with a `kafka:ConsumerConfiguration` giving `groupId`, `topics`, `offsetReset` (`kafka:OFFSET_RESET_EARLIEST`/`LATEST`/`NONE`) and `autoCommit`, or subscribe later with `subscribe`, `subscribeWithPattern` and `unsubscribe`
Poll with `consumer->pollPayload(timeout)` and bind the record values straight to a typed array, e.g. `Order[] orders = check orderConsumer->pollPayload(15);`, when the Kafka metadata is not needed

Define a subtype of `kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord` such as `record {| *kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord; Order value; |}` and call `consumer->poll(timeout)` to get typed values together with `key`, `offset`, `timestamp` and `headers`; use `kafka:BytesConsumerRecord` for raw `byte[]` values

Declare `listener kafka:Listener orderListener = new (kafka:DEFAULT_URL, {groupId, topics})` and a `service on orderListener` whose `remote function onConsumerRecord(Order[] orders)` receives each polled batch, bound either to payload types or to `kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord` subtypes

Create a `kafka:Service` value with a `service object { remote function onConsumerRecord(...) }` expression and manage it with `listener.attach`, `'start`, `gracefulStop`/`immediateStop`, registering a programmatically started listener with `runtime:registerListener`

Turn off auto commit with `autoCommit: false` and commit offsets yourself, using a `kafka:Caller` parameter in `onConsumerRecord(kafka:Caller caller, ...)` with `caller->'commit()` or `caller->commitOffset(offsets)`, or `consumer->'commit()` on a polling consumer

Set `autoSeekOnValidationFailure: false` and add `remote function onError(kafka:Error 'error, kafka:Caller caller)` that checks for `kafka:PayloadBindingError` or `kafka:PayloadValidationError` and skips the bad record with `caller->seek({partition: 'error.detail().partition, offset: 'error.detail().offset + 1})`

Add `ballerina/constraint` annotations such as `@constraint:String {maxLength: 30, minLength: 1}` to the bound record so consumers and listeners validate each payload (controlled by the `validation` configuration, on by default)

Work with partitions and offsets using `kafka:TopicPartition` and `kafka:PartitionOffset` with consumer methods `assign`, `getAssignment`, `seek`, `seekToBeginning`, `seekToEnd`, `getCommittedOffset`, `getPositionOffset`, `pause` and `resume`
Scale consumption by running several consumers with the same `groupId` so topic partitions are shared among them, or assign a partition manually with `consumer->assign([topicPartition])`

Encrypt connections by setting `secureSocket: {cert: "./path/public.crt", protocol: {name: kafka:SSL}}` (or a `crypto:TrustStore` plus an optional `key`) together with `securityProtocol: kafka:PROTOCOL_SSL` on producers, consumers and listeners

Authenticate with SASL by setting `auth: {mechanism: kafka:AUTH_SASL_PLAIN, username, password}` (or `kafka:AUTH_SASL_SCRAM_SHA_256`/`512`) and `securityProtocol: kafka:PROTOCOL_SASL_PLAINTEXT` or `kafka:PROTOCOL_SASL_SSL`

Serialize values as Avro through a schema registry by setting `valueSerializerType: kafka:SER_AVRO`, `valueSchema` and `schemaRegistryConfig` on the producer, and `valueDeserializerType: kafka:DES_AVRO` with `schemaRegistryUrl` on the consumer or listener

Tune delivery with `kafka:ProducerConfiguration` fields such as `compressionType` (`kafka:COMPRESSION_GZIP`...), `enableIdempotence`, `batchSize`, `linger` and `transactionalId`, and consumer fields such as `isolationLevel: kafka:ISOLATION_COMMITTED`, `maxPollRecords` and `pollingInterval`

out_of_scope: General listener and service declaration semantics (concept.services_listeners)
Declaring constraint annotations and calling `constraint:validate` directly (lib.constraint)
Exposing the HTTP API that produces Kafka records (lib.http)
Event-driven architecture patterns built on Kafka (topic.event_driven)

edges.note: poll/pollPayload infer the target type from the expected type
Both are message brokers with producer/consumer clients and listener services

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.array
nodes.summary: The `lang.array` module (basic type list) provides functions on arrays and tuples for length and iteration, adding and removing members, searching, slicing, sorting, higher-order processing and Base64/Base16 conversion of byte arrays.

must_cover.text: Use `arr.length()` to get the number of members and `arr.iterator()` to get an iterator object whose `next()` returns `record {| T value; |}` or nil at the end
Mutate an array at its end with `push(...vals)` (appends values) and `pop()` (removes and returns the last member; the array must not be empty)
Mutate an array at its start with `shift()` (removes and returns the first member; the array must not be empty) and `unshift(...vals)` (adds values at the start, keeping them in the order given)
Remove members with `remove(index)` (returns the removed member and panics if there is no member at `index`) and `removeAll()` (panics if any member cannot be removed)
Change an array's length in place with `setLength(n)`, knowing that `setLength(arr, 0)` is equivalent to `removeAll(arr)`

Use `slice(startIndex, endIndex = arr.length())` to get a new array with the members whose index is >= startIndex and < endIndex, and `reverse()` to get a new array in reverse order without modifying the original
Search with `indexOf(val, startIndex = 0)` and `lastIndexOf(val, startIndex = arr.length() - 1)`, which compare using `==`, return `int?` (nil when not found) and require an array of anydata members

Apply functions to members in order with `map` (new array of results), `filter` (new array of members for which the predicate returns true) and `forEach` (for side effects), passing function values or arrow functions such as `arr.map(x => x * 2)`

Combine members with `reduce(func, initial)`, where `func` takes the accumulated value and a member and returns the new accumulated value, e.g. `reduce([1, 2, 3], function (int total, int n) returns int { return total + n; }, 0)`
Test members with `some(func)`, which stops at the first true result and returns false for an empty array, and `every(func)`, which stops at the first false result and returns true for an empty array
Use `enumerate()` to get a new array of `[int, T]` index-member pairs, e.g. for `foreach [int, string] [i, s] in names.enumerate()`

Sort with `sort(direction = array:ASCENDING, key = ())`, which returns a new sorted array, takes `array:DESCENDING` (from the `array:SortDirection` enum; needs `import ballerina/lang.array;`) for descending order, and needs a `key` function `isolated function(T val) returns OrderedType` when the member type is not ordered (e.g. sorting records by a field)
Explain that `sort` orders members the same way as the `order by` clause of query expressions, so nil and NaN go at the end in both directions and equal keys keep their original relative order
Explain `array:OrderedType` (`()|boolean|int|float|decimal|string|OrderedType[]`) as a necessary but not sufficient condition for a type to be ordered

Convert `byte[]` to and from text with `toBase64`/`fromBase64` and `toBase16`/`fromBase16`, where the `to` functions produce strings without whitespace (Base16 uses lower-case `a..f`) and the `from` functions return `byte[]|error`
Use `toStream()` to get a `stream<T,()>` over an array's members, which uses an iterator over the array and so handles mutation of the array the same way an iterator does

out_of_scope: Array and tuple types, list constructors and indexing (concept.arrays_tuples)
The iterator mutation rules themselves (concept.loops)
Stream operations (lib.lang.stream, concept.streams)
Generic typing annotations and method-call dispatch (lib.langlib)
nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_array node. Stable ordering of equal keys comes from 6.35.6, where entries with equal keys keep their input order; `sort` is defined to work like the query sort clause. The spec does not say which inherent types make `removeAll` panic (e.g. fixed-length arrays); the item keeps only the stated rule. The `toStream` doc comment has a garbled sentence ('Theutation of the `arr`') and uses an undeclared type parameter `T`. `array` is not a predeclared prefix (8.1), so module-qualified references such as `array:DESCENDING` need an import.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.decimal
nodes.summary: The `lang.decimal` module (basic type decimal) provides functions for aggregating, rounding, quantizing and parsing decimal values.

must_cover.text: Use `decimal:sum(...xs)` (0 for no arguments) and `decimal:max(x, ...xs)`, `decimal:min(x, ...xs)` and `decimal:avg(x, ...xs)`, which require at least one argument
Use `d.abs()` (IEEE abs), `d.floor()` (largest integral decimal not greater than `d`) and `d.ceiling()` (smallest integral decimal not less than `d`)

Round with `d.round(fractionDigits = 0)`, which returns the decimal with exponent `-fractionDigits` closest to `d` and picks the one whose final digit is even on a tie, e.g. `amount.round(2)` for two digits after the decimal point
Convert a decimal to int with `<int>d`, which is the same as `<int>d.round(0)` and so rounds half to even rather than truncating

Use `decimal:quantize(x, y)` (the IEEE quantize operation) to get a value equal to `x` (apart from rounding) with the exponent of `y`, e.g. to fix a decimal to two fraction digits, and contrast `decimal:round` with fractionDigits 0 with IEEE roundToIntegralTiesToEven, which keeps a positive exponent

Parse decimals with `decimal:fromString(s)`, which accepts DecimalFloatingPointNumber syntax with an optional leading sign but no `d`/`f` suffix and no NaN or Infinity, returns `decimal|error`, and is the inverse of `value:toString` on a decimal

out_of_scope: Decimal type, literals and NumericConvert (concept.numeric_types)
Arithmetic operators and overflow (concept.arithmetic_operators)
Float maths and formatting (lib.lang.float)

edges.note: float and decimal share the round/floor/ceiling/abs/sum/max/min/avg function names with different empty-argument and NaN rules

nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_numeric node (decimal_aggregates, decimal_quantize, and the decimal halves of rounding, round_vs_cast and number_from_string) and the lang_decimal item of concept.langlib. `amount.round(2)` is an illustrative example derived from the doc comment.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.error
nodes.summary: The `lang.error` module (basic type error) provides functions to read an error's message, cause, detail record and stack trace and to convert errors to strings, plus the `NoMessage` and `Retriable` error types and the `DefaultRetryManager` used by retry statements.

must_cover.text: Get an error's message string with `e.message()`, e.g. when logging or returning a failure description
Get the error that caused an error with `e.cause()`, which returns `error?`, and walk a chain of causes

Get an error's detail record with `e.detail()`, which returns an immutable value typed `readonly & D` for an `error<D>`, and read its fields, e.g. `e.detail().code` for `error<record {| int code; |}>`
Explain that every error detail record must belong to `error:Detail` (`record {| error:Cloneable...; |}`), where `error:Cloneable` is `readonly|xml|Cloneable[]|map<Cloneable>|table<map<Cloneable>>`
Use `e.stackTrace()` to get the error's stack trace as `error:StackFrame[]`, whose first member is the top of the call stack, and call `toString()` on each frame (a single line without newlines)
Convert an error to a string with `e.toString()` (direct style) or `e.toBalString()` (expression style, in Ballerina syntax), both defined by the ToString abstract operation

Handle `error:NoMessage`, the distinct error type a receive action (e.g. `int|error:NoMessage v = <- w1;`) evaluates to when no message has been sent to it, so it appears in the receive action's static type
Define errors as retryable by making them belong to the distinct type `error:Retriable` (e.g. `type ConnectionError distinct error:Retriable;`), so that the default retry manager retries them

Use `error:DefaultRetryManager`, the retry manager a `retry` statement uses when no type parameter is given: `init(int count = 3)` sets the retry budget and `shouldRetry(e)` returns true (and decrements the count) only while `e is error:Retriable` and the count is above 0, e.g. `retry<error:DefaultRetryManager>(5) { ... }`

out_of_scope: Error types, error constructors, check, fail, panic and on fail (concept.errors)
The retry statement and custom RetryManager classes (concept.retry)
Worker message passing (concept.worker_messages)
The current call stack via runtime:getStackTrace (lib.lang.runtime)

edges.note: lang.error and lang.runtime both define a StackFrame type (duplicated to avoid a dependency)

nodes.notes: Expands the lang_error item of the removed concept.langlib node. The `type ConnectionError distinct error:Retriable;` and `retry<error:DefaultRetryManager>(5)` examples are illustrative; the spec says the retry statement's type parameter defaults to `DefaultRetryManager` (7.23.3) and that the retry statement creates the manager with `new T(A)`. The detail field-access example assumes a closed detail record type.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.float
nodes.summary: The `lang.float` module (basic type float) provides IEEE constants and functions for classification, aggregation, rounding, maths, parsing, hexadecimal and fixed/scientific formatting, and bit-level conversion of float values.

must_cover.text: Use the `lang.float` constants `float:PI`, `float:E`, `float:NaN` (`0.0/0.0`) and `float:Infinity` (`1.0/0.0`)
Classify floats with `isNaN`, `isFinite` and `isInfinite`, exactly one of which is true for any float value

Use `float:sum`, `float:max`, `float:min` and `float:avg`, which take zero or more arguments: `sum` of no arguments is +0.0, `max` is -∞, `min` is +∞ and `avg` is NaN, and `sum`, `max` and `min` return NaN if any argument is NaN

Round with `x.round(fractionDigits = 0)`, which rounds to the nearest multiple of 10^-fractionDigits with ties to even (e.g. `2.5.round()` is 2.0; with 0 digits it matches IEEE roundToIntegralTiesToEven) and returns NaN, ±0 and ±∞ unchanged, and use `floor`, `ceiling` and `abs`
Explain that converting with `<int>x` is the same as `<int>x.round(0)` for both float and decimal, so the conversion rounds half to even rather than truncating

Use the float maths functions that correspond to IEEE operations: `sqrt`, `cbrt`, `pow(x, y)`, `log`, `log10`, `exp`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2(y, x)`, `sinh`, `cosh` and `tanh` (results in radians where relevant)

Parse floats with `float:fromString(s)`, which accepts DecimalFloatingPointNumber syntax with an optional sign, also `NaN` and `Infinity` with an optional sign, but no `f`/`d` suffix, returns `float|error`, and is the inverse of `value:toString` on a float

Use `float:toHexString` (HexFloatingPointLiteral form with `0x` for finite values, a `-` sign when negative, and `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and `NaN` for the special values) and `float:fromHexString` (optional sign, `NaN` and `Infinity` allowed; returns `float|error`)
Use `toBitsInt` and `float:fromBitsInt` to convert between a float and its IEEE 64-bit binary representation as an int, knowing that every NaN bit pattern maps to the single float NaN value

Format floats with `toFixedString(fractionDigits)` (no exponent) and `toExpString(fractionDigits)` (one digit before the point and a lower-case `e` exponent with a sign and at least two digits), where `()` means the minimum digits needed, 0 means no decimal point, rounding is ties-to-even, NaN and infinities format as `value:toString` does, and a negative fractionDigits panics

out_of_scope: Float type, literals and NumericConvert (concept.numeric_types)
Arithmetic operators and float equality (concept.arithmetic_operators, concept.comparison_equality)
value:toString formatting of numbers (lib.lang.value)
Decimal rounding and quantize (lib.lang.decimal)
nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_numeric node (float items; the shared rounding, round_vs_cast and number_from_string items were split between lib.lang.float and lib.lang.decimal). Float `ceiling`'s return doc says 'decimal value' (a copy-paste error). The `2.5.round()` example is derived from the stated ties-to-even rule, not quoted from the spec. The spec does not say what `round` does with a negative fractionDigits.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.int
nodes.summary: The `lang.int` module (basic type int) provides the sized integer subtypes, range constants, and functions for aggregation, parsing, hexadecimal formatting and stepped integer ranges.

must_cover.text: Use the `lang.int` built-in subtypes `int:Signed8`, `int:Signed16`, `int:Signed32`, `int:Unsigned8`, `int:Unsigned16` and `int:Unsigned32` as variable, field and parameter types to restrict ints to a sized range, e.g. `int:Signed32 code = 404;`

Use the `lang.int` constants `int:MAX_VALUE` (9223372036854775807), `int:MIN_VALUE` (defined as `-9223372036854775807 - 1` because the literal 9223372036854775808 would overflow) and the subtype bounds `SIGNED32_MAX_VALUE`, `SIGNED32_MIN_VALUE`, `SIGNED16_*`, `SIGNED8_*` and `UNSIGNED32/16/8_MAX_VALUE`
Use `int:abs(n)` (or `n.abs()`), `int:sum(...ns)` (0 for no arguments), `int:max(n, ...ns)` and `int:min(n, ...ns)`, which need at least one argument
Use `int:avg(n, ...ns)`, which computes the average with the decimal type, returns `decimal` (not int) and panics if the sum overflows decimal

Parse and format ints with `int:fromString(s)` (decimal digits with an optional leading `+` or `-`; returns an error otherwise; the inverse of `value:toString` on an int), `toHexString()` (lower-case, no `0x` prefix, `-` prefix for negatives) and `int:fromHexString(s)` (upper- or lower-case digits, optional sign, no `0x`/`0X` prefix allowed)

Use `int:range(start, end, step)` to get an `object:Iterable` over `start + step*i` that is increasing and < end when step > 0, decreasing and > end when step < 0, and panics when step is 0, e.g. `foreach int i in int:range(10, 0, -2)`

Aggregate int fields in a query with unqualified calls such as `sum(qty)`, `max(qty)` and `avg(qty)` on an aggregated variable after `group by` or in a `collect` clause, which resolve to `int:sum`, `int:max` and `int:avg`

out_of_scope: Int type, literals, ranges, byte and NumericConvert (concept.numeric_types)
Arithmetic operators and overflow (concept.arithmetic_operators)
value:toString formatting of numbers (lib.lang.value)
Built-in subtype conventions and empty-list aggregation rules (lib.langlib)
nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_numeric node (int items) and the lang_int item of concept.langlib. Spec doc-comment issues: lang.int Signed16/Signed8 comments say 'non-negative' but give signed ranges; `int:max` and `int:avg` return docs mention `x`/`xs` and 'minimum value' (copy-paste errors). The `foreach ... int:range(10, 0, -2)` example is derived from the stated range rules; the aggregation_query item is derived from 6.15 and the B.2 change note that `int:avg` etc. were added for aggregation.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.map
nodes.summary: The `lang.map` module (basic type mapping) provides functions on maps and records for size, key lookup and removal, iteration over members or key-member entries, and higher-order processing.

must_cover.text: Use `m.length()` for the number of members and `m.hasKey(k)` to test whether a map has a member with string key `k`
Use `m.keys()` to get a new `string[]` of all keys and `m.toArray()` to get an array of all members
Use `m.get(k)` when the key is known to exist: it returns the member typed `T` and panics if there is no member with key `k`, unlike `m[k]`, which returns `()` for a missing key
Iterate over a map's members (not its keys) with `foreach` or `m.iterator()`, whose `next()` returns `record {| T value; |}` or nil at the end
Use `m.entries()` to get a new `map<[string, T]>` of key-member pairs, e.g. `foreach [string, int] [k, v] in scores.entries()`, to iterate over keys and members together

Transform maps with `m.map(func)`, which returns a `map<T1>` with the same keys holding `func`'s results, and `m.filter(func)`, which returns a new `map<T>` with only the members for which the predicate returns true
Use `m.forEach(func)` to apply a function to each member of a map for its side effects
Combine a map's members with `m.reduce(func, initial)`, where `func` takes the accumulated value and a member, e.g. totalling `map<int>` values
Remove members with `m.remove(k)`, which returns the removed member and panics if there is no member with key `k`, or `m.removeIfHasKey(k)`, which returns `T?` (nil when the key is absent)
Clear a map with `m.removeAll()`, which panics if any member cannot be removed
Call `lang.map` functions on record values, which belong to basic type mapping, e.g. `person.keys()`, `person.hasKey("age")` or `person.toArray()`

out_of_scope: Map types, mapping constructors and member access (concept.maps)
Record types (concept.records)
Iteration mutation rules (concept.loops)
nodes.notes: Expands the lang_map item of the removed concept.langlib node. records_as_maps follows from the method-call rule (6.16) and the fact that record types are mapping types; the spec has no record-specific example. The iterator doc comment says iteration is over members, not keys, and points to `entries` and `keys` for the others.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.regexp
nodes.summary: The preview `lang.regexp` module provides the `RegExp`, `Span` and `Groups` types and functions for finding, matching, replacing and splitting with `re` regular expressions.

must_cover.text: Use `regexp:RegExp`, the built-in subtype naming the tagged data basic type for tag `re`, as the type of `re`...`` values and of function parameters that take regular expressions, importing `ballerina/lang.regexp` to refer to it
Use a `regexp:Span`, a readonly object with `startIndex`, `endIndex` (the index after the end, so the length is `endIndex - startIndex`) and a `substring()` method that returns the matched text

Use `regexp:Groups` (`readonly & [Span, Span?...]`), where member 0 is the match of the whole regular expression and member i is the i-th capturing group (groups ordered by the position of their opening parenthesis), which is nil if the match did not use that group
Find the first match at or after `startIndex` (default 0) with `re.find(str, startIndex)` returning `Span?`, or with `findGroups` returning `Groups?`
Find all matches with `findAll` (returns `Span[]`) and `findAllGroups` (returns `Groups[]`), knowing that each search continues where the previous match ended, so matches never overlap
Test for a match that starts exactly at an index with `matchAt(str, startIndex = 0)` (returns `Span?` whose `startIndex` equals the given index) or `matchGroupsAt` (returns `Groups?`)

Test whether a regular expression matches the whole string (from index 0 to its length) with `isFullMatch(str)`, or get the groups of such a match with `fullMatchGroups(str)`, which returns nil if there is no full match

Replace the first match with `replace(str, replacement, startIndex = 0)` and every non-overlapping match with `replaceAll(str, replacement, startIndex = 0)`, where `replacement` is a `Replacement` (a fixed string or a `ReplacerFunction`)
Write a `ReplacerFunction` (`isolated function(Groups groups) returns string`) that builds each replacement from the match's groups, e.g. to reformat captured dates
Split a string with `re.split(str)`, which returns the substrings before the first match, between matches and after the last match of the separator pattern, or `[str]` if nothing matches
Build a regular expression at runtime with `regexp:fromString(str)`, which accepts the same syntax as the `re` template and returns an error if `str` is not a valid regular expression

Explain that `matchGroupsAt` corresponds to the ECMAScript abstract matching function and that `matchAt`, `find`, `findGroups`, `findAll`, `findAllGroups`, the full-match functions and `isFullMatch` can be defined in terms of it

out_of_scope: Regular expression syntax, flags, the `re` template and interpolation (concept.regexp)
string:matches and string:includesMatch (lib.lang.string)
nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_regexp node. lang.regexp is preview in 2024R1. Spec typos: the `Groups` doc comment says 'The group with index i, where i > 1, is the i-th capturing group' (should read i >= 1); section 10.1 refers to a `fullMatchGroup` function while the module defines `fullMatchGroups`; the `findAllGroups` return doc says 'a `Group`' for each match. The spec does not say what happens for an out-of-range `startIndex`. That `regexp` needs an import is derived from the 8.1 predeclared-prefix list, which omits it.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.runtime
nodes.summary: The `lang.runtime` module provides runtime functions that are not tied to a basic type, for sleeping, dynamically registering listeners, getting the current stack trace and registering graceful-shutdown handlers.

must_cover.text: Pause the current strand with `runtime:sleep(seconds)` (after `import ballerina/lang.runtime;`), where `seconds` is a decimal such as `runtime:sleep(0.5)`, knowing that sleeping makes the strand yield
Implement `runtime:DynamicListener`, an object type with `start()`, `gracefulStop()` and `immediateStop()` methods each returning `error?`, to create a listener that can be registered at run time

Use `runtime:registerListener(l)` to make a `DynamicListener` a module listener of the calling module, so it is started and stopped with the module's listeners, and `runtime:deregisterListener(l)` to remove it
Get the current call stack with `runtime:getStackTrace()`, which returns `runtime:StackFrame[]` with the top of the stack first, and print each frame with `toString()`

Register cleanup with `runtime:onGracefulStop(handler)`, where `handler` is a `runtime:StopHandler` (`function() returns error?`); each handler is called once during graceful shutdown, after `gracefulStop` has been called on all registered listeners, in reverse order of registration

out_of_scope: Listener declarations, services and the module lifecycle (concept.services_listeners, concept.program_execution)
Error stack traces via e.stackTrace() (lib.lang.error)
Scheduling and timed jobs (lib.task)
nodes.notes: Expands the lang_runtime item of the removed concept.langlib node. 'Started and stopped with the module's listeners' is derived from the registerListener doc ('The listener becomes a module listener of the module from which this function is called') together with the module-listener lifecycle in 5.7.4/8.3; the spec has no example. `runtime` is not a predeclared prefix (8.1), so the module must be imported.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.stream
nodes.summary: The `lang.stream` module (basic type stream) provides functions to iterate, read, close, map, filter and reduce `stream<T,C>` values, where `C` is the completion type (`error?`).

must_cover.text: Read a stream one member at a time with `stm.next()`, which returns `record {| T value; |}` for the next member or the completion value `C` (nil at the end, or an error), or get an iterator with `stm.iterator()` whose `next()` behaves the same way
Release a stream's resources with `stm.close()`, which returns `C?` (nil on success, or an error), and know that closing an already closed stream has no effect and returns nil
Use `stm.map(func)` to get a new `stream<T1,C>` containing the result of applying `func` to each member in order
Use `stm.filter(func)` to get a new `stream<T,C>` containing only the members for which the predicate returns true
Use `stm.forEach(func)` to apply a function to each member in order, knowing that it returns the stream's completion value `C`, so `check stm.forEach(...)` propagates a stream error
Combine a stream's members with `stm.reduce(func, initial)` on a `stream<T,E?>`, which returns the combined value or the stream's error (`T1|E`)

out_of_scope: Stream types, stream constructors and stream-producing queries (concept.streams)
Database result streams (lib.sql)
nodes.notes: Expands the lang_stream item of the removed concept.langlib node. In the spec the stream iterator's `next()` and `stream:next` both return `record {| Type value; |}|CompletionType`. The `check stm.forEach(...)` usage is derived from the return type, not quoted.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.string
nodes.summary: The `lang.string` module (basic type string) provides the `string:Char` subtype and functions for measuring, slicing, searching, comparing, case-converting, trimming, padding, encoding and regex-matching strings.

must_cover.text: Use `str.length()`, which counts characters (code points), and iterate over a string with `foreach` or `str.iterator()`, which yields length-1 substrings of type `string:Char` in order
Use the built-in subtype `string:Char` for single-character strings, e.g. as the type of `padChar` and of `toCodePointInt`'s parameter
Combine strings with `string:concat(...strs)` (empty string for no arguments) and `string:'join(separator, ...strs)` (separator placed between the strings)
Extract text with `substring(startIndex, endIndex = str.length())`, which returns the characters with index >= startIndex and < endIndex

Search with `indexOf(substr, startIndex = 0)` (first occurrence at or after startIndex) and `lastIndexOf(substr, startIndex = str.length() - substr.length())` (last occurrence at or before startIndex), which return `int?` with nil when not found, and with `includes(substr, startIndex = 0)`
Test prefixes and suffixes with `startsWith(substr)` and `endsWith(substr)`
Change case with `toLowerAscii` and `toUpperAscii`, which convert only A-Z/a-z and leave other characters unchanged, and compare case-insensitively with `equalsIgnoreCaseAscii`
Use `trim()` to remove ASCII white space (0x9 to 0xD and 0x20) from both ends of a string

Compare strings with `codePointCompare(str1, str2)`, which returns a negative, zero or positive int by lexicographic Unicode code point order, and know that this order often differs from culturally expected sort order

Convert between strings and code points with `getCodePoint(index)`, `toCodePointInts()`, `toCodePointInt(ch)`, `fromCodePointInts(ints)` and `fromCodePointInt(cp)`, where the `from` functions return an error for an invalid code point (outside 0 to 0x10FFFF or in the surrogate range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF)
Encode a string to UTF-8 with `toBytes()` returning `byte[]` and decode with `string:fromBytes(bytes)`, which returns `string|error`
Pad strings to a length with `padStart(len, padChar = " ")` and `padEnd(len, padChar = " ")`, which return `str` unchanged when its length is already >= `len`
Use `padZero(len, zeroChar = "0")` to add zeros at the start of a string but after a leading `+` or `-` sign, e.g. for formatting numbers to a fixed width

Match strings against `re` regular expressions with `str.matches(re)`, which requires a full match (equivalent to `regexp:isFullMatch(re, str)`), and `str.includesMatch(re, startIndex = 0)`, which accepts a match anywhere (equivalent to `regexp:find(re, str, startIndex) != ()`); `string:RegExp` refers to `regexp:RegExp`

out_of_scope: String literals, escapes, string templates and immutability (concept.strings)
Converting other values to strings (lib.lang.value, concept.value_cloning) and parsing numbers (lib.lang.int, lib.lang.float, lib.lang.decimal)
Regular expression syntax (concept.regexp) and the full lang.regexp API, including splitting and replacing (lib.lang.regexp)
nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_string node. The doc comment for `matches` says it is equivalent to `regex:isFullMatch`; the module prefix is spelled `regex` there (a typo for `regexp`). The spec does not say whether `substring` or `getCodePoint` panic on out-of-range indexes, so no such claim is made. The 2024R1 lang.string module has no split or replace function; those are in lang.regexp.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.table
nodes.summary: The `lang.table` module (basic type table) provides functions to add, replace, look up and remove table members by key, iterate over members, and map, filter and reduce tables.

must_cover.text: Use `t.length()` for the number of members and iterate over a table's members (not its keys) with `foreach` or `t.iterator()`
Add a row with `t.add(val)`, which appends it as the last member and panics if `val` has the same key as an existing member or is inconsistent with the table's inherent type

Insert or replace a row with `t.put(val)`, which replaces a member with the same key value while keeping its position (otherwise appends) and panics if `val` is inconsistent with the table's inherent type
Look up a row by key with `t.get(k)` on a keyed table `table<R> key<K>`, which returns the member and panics if there is no member with key `k`
Test whether a keyed table has a member with key `k` with `t.hasKey(k)`
Remove rows by key with `t.remove(k)` (returns the removed member; panics if there is none) or `t.removeIfHasKey(k)` (returns `R?`, nil when the key is absent)
Clear a table with `t.removeAll()`, which panics if any member cannot be removed
Use `t.keys()` to get a new `K[]` of all key values of a keyed table and `t.toArray()` to get an array of all rows
Transform rows with `t.map(func)`, where `func` maps each row to another mapping and the result is a new keyless table `table<R1> key<never>`
Select rows with `t.filter(func)`, which returns a new table with the same key specifier (`table<R> key<K>`) holding the rows for which the predicate returns true
Use `t.forEach(func)` to process each row for side effects and `t.reduce(func, initial)` to combine rows into one value, e.g. summing a salary field
Use `t.nextKey()` on a table with an int key (`table<R> key<int>`) to get the next available key, the maximum used key + 1 or 0 if no key is used, for auto-increment style ids

out_of_scope: Table types, key specifiers, table constructors and member access (concept.tables)
Query expressions that produce tables (concept.query_expressions)
nodes.notes: Expands the lang_table item of the removed concept.langlib node. The lang.table iterator doc comment mentions an `entries` function that lang.table does not define, so it is not covered. The `nextKey` doc comment has an open question ('XXX should it be 0, if the maximum used key value is < 0?'), so the negative-key case is left out.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.value
nodes.summary: The `lang.value` module provides functions that work on values of more than one basic type, for cloning, type-directed conversion, safe casting, string and Ballerina-syntax conversion, JSON conversion and parsing, and aggregation helpers.

must_cover.text: Use `v.clone()` on a `value:Cloneable` value (`readonly|xml|Cloneable[]|map<Cloneable>|table<map<Cloneable>>`) to get a deep copy that does not copy immutable subtrees and so can be used safely alongside the original
Use `v.cloneReadOnly()` to get an immutable clone typed `T & readonly`, e.g. to pass data to isolated code or store it in a `final` readonly field

Convert anydata to a target type with `v.cloneWithType(t)`, where `t` defaults to the inferred typedesc (`Person p = check m.cloneWithType();`): the inherent type and read-only bits come from `t`, numbers convert with NumericConvert, record defaults fill missing fields, the result is a tree, and an error is returned if this cannot be done or `v` has cycles

Safely cast with `v.ensureType(t)` (inferred `t` by default, e.g. `int n = check j.ensureType();`), which casts like a type cast expression but returns an error instead of panicking when the cast fails
Convert any value to a string with `v.toString()`, the direct-style ToString conversion that leaves a string value unchanged

Use `v.toBalString()` to get the expression-style string of a value in Ballerina syntax (for acyclic anydata, an expression that evaluates to a value `==` to `v`) and `value:fromBalString(s)` to parse that subset back into `anydata|error`

Convert anydata to json with `v.toJson()`, a deep copy in which xml becomes a string (as by `toString`), a table becomes a list of mappings, arrays get inherent type `json[]` and mappings `map<json>`; it panics if `v` has cycles
Serialize anydata to a JSON string with `v.toJsonString()`, which first converts `v` as by `toJson`

Parse JSON text with `s.fromJsonString()` returning `json|error`, knowing that numbers become `decimal` except that a negative zero becomes float `-0.0` and an integer without decimal point or exponent that fits in int becomes `int`

Parse JSON with a fixed number representation using `s.fromJsonFloatString()` (returns `value:JsonFloat|error`, numbers as float) or `s.fromJsonDecimalString()` (returns `value:JsonDecimal|error`, numbers as decimal)

Convert json to a user-defined type with `j.fromJsonWithType(t)` (like `cloneWithType` but also undoing the conversions of `toJson`) or parse and convert in one step with `s.fromJsonStringWithType(t)`, e.g. `Order o = check payload.fromJsonStringWithType();`

Merge two json values with `j1.mergeJson(j2)`: nil yields the other value, two mappings merge recursively key by key (adding missing keys), any other combination fails with an error, and `j1` is unchanged when the merge fails
Use `value:count(...vs)`, `value:first(v, ...vs)` and `value:last(v, ...vs)` with aggregated variables, e.g. `count(id)` or `first(name)` in a `collect` clause or after `group by`

Import `ballerina/lang.value` (it has no predeclared prefix) to call its functions in qualified form such as `value:fromBalString(s)` or `value:mergeJson(j1, j2)`, and know that the method form `x.f()` reaches `lang.value` whenever the module of `x`'s basic type does not define `f`

out_of_scope: The Clone, ImmutableClone, NumericConvert and ToString abstract operations themselves (concept.value_cloning)
json and anydata types (concept.json_anydata)
Type cast expressions and type tests (concept.type_cast_test)
Group-by and collect semantics (concept.query_expressions)
Typed JSON/XML/CSV binding with annotations (lib.data.jsondata)
nodes.notes: Expands the lang_value item of the removed concept.langlib node. Method-call forms on json/anydata values (e.g. `j1.mergeJson(j2)`, `s.fromJsonString()`) follow from the 6.16 rule: lang.string does not define these functions, so string receivers dispatch to lang.value. The `typedesc<anydata> t = <>` default means the target type is inferred from the contextually expected type. Code examples in items are illustrative, not quoted from the spec.

nodes.title: ballerina/lang.xml
nodes.summary: The `lang.xml` module (basic type xml) provides the xml item subtypes, namespace constants, and functions for accessing, constructing, selecting, transforming and parsing xml values.

must_cover.text: Use the built-in subtypes `xml:Element`, `xml:ProcessingInstruction`, `xml:Comment` and `xml:Text` (empty or a text singleton) and sequence types such as `xml<xml:Element>` to type xml values, e.g. as the parameter type of `getName` or the result of `elements()`
Use the constants `xml:XML_NAMESPACE_URI`, `xml:XMLNS_NAMESPACE_URI` and the expanded attribute names `xml:space`, `xml:lang` and `xml:base` (e.g. `"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang"`)
Use `x.length()` for the number of items in an xml sequence and iterate with `foreach` or `x.iterator()`, where each item is an xml singleton

Use `x.get(i)` to get the item at index `i`, and distinguish it from `x[i]`: `get` panics when there is no item with that index, whereas `x[i]` returns empty xml for an index >= the length (and panics only for a negative index)
Build sequences with `xml:concat(...xs)`, which concatenates xml and string values (strings become text) and returns an empty xml sequence when given no arguments
Read and change an element's expanded name with `getName()` and `setName(xName)`
Use `getAttributes()` to get an element's attributes as `map<string>` keyed by expanded attribute names, including namespace attributes
Read and replace an element's children with `getChildren()` and `setChildren(xml|string)`, knowing that `setChildren` panics if it would make the element structure cyclic
Use `getDescendants()` to get the children together with, recursively, the descendants of each child element, in document order (each element immediately precedes its descendants)

Use `xml:data(x)` to get the character data of an xml value: text characters and, recursively, element content, with comments, processing instructions and empty sequences contributing the empty string
Use `getTarget()` on a processing instruction and `getContent()` on a processing instruction or comment

Construct items with `xml:createElement(name, attributes = {}, children = xml``)` (copies the attributes into a new map), `xml:createProcessingInstruction(target, content)`, `xml:createComment(content)` and `xml:createText(data)`, which returns empty xml for an empty string
Use `slice(startIndex, endIndex = x.length())` to get the subsequence of items with index >= startIndex and < endIndex
Use `strip()` to remove comments, processing instructions and text items consisting entirely of XML white space (the S production of XML 1.0) from an xml sequence

Select items with `elements(nm = ())` (element items, optionally only those with expanded name `nm`), `children()` (equivalent to `elements(x).map(getChildren)`), `elementChildren(nm = ())` (equivalent to `children(x).elements(nm)`) and `text()` (the concatenated text items)
Transform xml sequences item by item with `map` (returns `xml<XmlType>`), `forEach` and `filter`, where each item is passed as a singleton
Parse XML text with `xml:fromString(s)`, which parses using the XML 1.0 `content` production and returns `xml|error`

out_of_scope: xml types, the xml template, xml concatenation with +, namespace declarations and navigation syntax `x/*`, `x/<a>`, `x.<a>` (concept.xml)
Converting xml to and from records with annotations (lib.data.xmldata)

edges.note: XML step expressions (navigation) are defined in terms of xml:map, xml:elements, xml:getChildren and xml:getDescendants

nodes.notes: Content moved from the removed concept.langlib_xml node, plus the built-in subtype part of concept.langlib#lang_xml. The empty-xml result of `x[i]` comes from 6.14 (member access); the `get` doc comment only says that `get` panics where `x[i]` does not. The `xml:Text` doc comment says 'singleton test sequence' (a typo for text).

nodes.title: langlib
nodes.summary: The lang library is the set of `ballerina/lang.*` modules defined by the specification, which provide the basic operations on language values through predeclared module prefixes and method-call syntax. This node covers the conventions shared by all modules and the small modules (boolean, function, future, object, typedesc, transaction) that have no node of their own.

must_cover.text: Explain that modules in the `ballerina` organization whose names start with `lang.` are reserved for the lang library defined by the specification, and that every module except `lang.value`, `lang.transaction` and `lang.runtime` corresponds to a basic type

Use the predeclared module prefixes `boolean`, `decimal`, `error`, `float`, `function`, `future`, `int`, `map`, `object`, `stream`, `string`, `table`, `transaction`, `typedesc` and `xml`, which refer to the corresponding `lang.*` module without an import and without a quoted identifier (e.g. `int:fromString(s)`)

Override a predeclared prefix with an `import` declaration that binds the same prefix to another module, and import modules without a predeclared prefix, such as `ballerina/lang.array`, `ballerina/lang.value`, `ballerina/lang.regexp` and `ballerina/lang.runtime`, explicitly (e.g. `import ballerina/lang.runtime;` before calling `runtime:sleep(1)`)

Explain how `v.f(args)` on a non-object value becomes the lang library call `m:f(v, args)`, where `m` is `lang.B` if the static type of `v` is a subtype of basic type B and `lang.B` defines `f`, and `lang.value` otherwise (e.g. `[1,2].length()` calls `array:length`, `x.toString()` calls `value:toString`)

Explain that a method call converted to a lang library call must satisfy every constraint of the equivalent function call (a compile error otherwise), and is isolated under the same conditions as that function call

Explain the `@typeParam` annotation: a lang library type definition marked with it acts as a type parameter, so every use of it within one function declaration (e.g. `Type` in `push(Type[] arr, Type... vals)`) refers to the same type, and its definition is an upper bound; the lang library uses this annotation because Ballerina 2024R1 has no user-defined generic types

Explain the `@isolatedParam` annotation on a function-typed parameter of an isolated langlib function: when the call must be isolated, the argument supplied (e.g. the callback to `map` or `filter`) must also be isolated

List the built-in subtypes and their ranges: `int:Signed8` (-128..127), `int:Signed16` (-32,768..32,767), `int:Signed32` (-2,147,483,648..2,147,483,647), `int:Unsigned8` (0..255), `int:Unsigned16` (0..65,535), `int:Unsigned32` (0..4,294,967,295), `string:Char` (length 1), and `xml:Element`, `xml:ProcessingInstruction`, `xml:Comment` and `xml:Text` (empty or a text singleton)
Reference a built-in subtype `T` of basic type `B` with a qualified type reference `M:T` where `M` refers to `ballerina/lang.B`, and know that `int:Unsigned8` is equivalent to the predefined `byte`

Explain that `@builtinSubtype` marks a lang library type definition whose meaning comes from the specification rather than from its type descriptor (e.g. `@builtinSubtype type Signed32 int;`), and that using it outside the lang library is an error

Explain that a call `f(x)` where `f` is unqualified and the only argument is an aggregated variable of type `T` (e.g. `sum(price)` after `group by` or in `collect`) resolves `f` in `lang.B` when `T` is a subtype of `B[]` and `lang.B` defines `f`, and in `lang.value` otherwise (e.g. `count`, `first`, `last`); when the function needs at least one argument but the list may be empty (e.g. `max(x)` in a `collect` clause), the call returns nil for an empty list and its return type is unioned with nil

Use `lang.boolean` functions `boolean:fromString(s)` (accepts `true`/`false` in any letter case and `1`/`0`, otherwise returns an error; the inverse of `value:toString` on a boolean), `boolean:some(...bs)` (false when given no arguments) and `boolean:every(...bs)` (true when given no arguments)

Use `function:call(func, ...args)` from `lang.function` (basic type function) to call a function value dynamically with `any|error` arguments, getting an `any|error` result, knowing that it panics if the arguments are not of the types `func` requires
Use `future:cancel(f)` (or `f.cancel()`) from `lang.future` (basic type future) to set the cancellation flag of the strand behind a future, which then terminates abnormally the next time it yields

Make a class iterable by including `*object:Iterable;` (the distinct object type from `lang.object`) and defining an `iterator()` method whose result has `next() returns record {| T value; |}|error?`, so its objects can be used in `foreach` and query `from` clauses

Use `object:RawTemplate`, the distinct object type of raw template values, with fields `strings` (`readonly & string[]`, the literal parts split at the interpolations, one longer than `insertions`) and `insertions` (`(any|error)[]`, the evaluated interpolations)

Use `typedesc:typeIds(t, primaryOnly = false)` from `lang.typedesc` (basic type typedesc) to get the type-ids induced by a typedesc as `readonly & TypeId[]` (each with a `ModuleId` of `organization`, `name` and `platformParts` and a `localId` of type `string|int`, where an int is compiler-generated), or nil if `t` is not definite

Use `transaction:info()` (a `transactional` function, callable only in a transactional scope) and `transaction:getInfo(xid)` to read a transaction's `transaction:Info` record (`xid`, `retryNumber`, `prevAttempt`, `startTime` as a `transaction:Timestamp` with `toMillisecondsInt()` and `toString()`), and know that `lang.transaction` does not correspond to a basic type and that `transaction:Error` is the commit action's error type

Call `transaction:setRollbackOnly(e)` to make the transaction manager decide to roll back, `transaction:getRollbackOnly()` to test whether a rollback is already known, and `transaction:setData(data)`/`getData()` to attach `readonly` data to the current transaction branch

Register `transaction:onCommit(handler)` with a `CommitHandler` (`isolated function(Info info)`) and `transaction:onRollback(handler)` with a `RollbackHandler` (`isolated function(Info info, error? cause, boolean willRetry)`) to run code when the global transaction commits or rolls back

out_of_scope: The Ballerina standard library (ballerina/http, ballerina/io, ...), which the spec explicitly does not specify

Detailed functions of the larger modules (lib.lang.array, lib.lang.string, lib.lang.int, lib.lang.float, lib.lang.decimal, lib.lang.map, lib.lang.table, lib.lang.value, lib.lang.error, lib.lang.xml, lib.lang.regexp, lib.lang.stream, lib.lang.runtime)
General import syntax and module prefixes (concept.modules_imports)
Group-by/collect semantics and aggregated variables (concept.query_expressions)
Transaction and retry-transaction statements (concept.transactions)
nodes.notes: Content merged from the removed concept.langlib and concept.langlib_conventions nodes (see langlib_map.json). Spec 11.1 says generic types are planned for a future version. The lang.int doc comments for Signed16 and Signed8 say 'non-negative integers' but then give signed ranges; the 11.2 table is taken as authoritative. Saying that `lang.array`, `lang.value`, `lang.regexp` and `lang.runtime` are not predeclared is derived from the predeclared-prefix list in 8.1, which omits them; the spec does not say this explicitly. In lang.transaction, the types `Error` and `Info` are written without `public` in the spec text even though the commit action's type is `transaction:Error?`; treat them as part of the module's API. `f.cancel()` method form follows from the method-call rule in 6.16.

nodes.title: ballerina/ldap
nodes.summary: The LDAP library connects to directory servers with `ldap:Client` to add, modify, rename, compare, search and delete directory entries.

must_cover.text: Create an `ldap:Client` with `check new (hostName = "localhost", port = 389, domainName = "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com", password = "...")`, optionally with `clientSecureSocket: {cert, verifyHostName, tlsVersions}` for LDAPS, and release it with `close()`

Add an entry with `ldapClient->add(dn, entry)` where `entry` is an `ldap:Entry` such as `{"objectClass": ["top", "person"], "sn": "user", "cn": "user"}`, delete it with `delete(dn)`, and check `ldap:LdapResponse.resultCode`
Update attributes of an entry with `modify(dn, entry)` and rename it with `modifyDn(currentDn, newRdn, deleteOldRdn)`

Search with `search(baseDn, "(sn=user)", ldap:SUB)` (scopes `ldap:BASE`, `ldap:ONE`, `ldap:SUB`, `ldap:SUBORDINATE_SUBTREE`, optional attribute list) and read `ldap:SearchResult` `resultCode`, `entries` and `searchReferences`
Bind directory data to Ballerina types with `searchWithType(baseDn, filter, scope)` returning a record array and `getEntry(dn)` returning the expected `anydata` type
Check an attribute value with `compare(dn, attributeName, value)` returning `boolean`, and handle `ldap:Error` whose detail carries `resultCode`

out_of_scope: LDAP user stores for HTTP basic authentication (lib.http, lib.auth)
nodes.notes: The README names the rename operation `modifyDN`, but the client source defines `modifyDn`; the item uses the source name.

nodes.title: ballerina/log
nodes.summary: The `log` module prints leveled, structured log records with key-value context and errors, configured through Config.toml (level, per-module levels, logfmt/JSON format, stdout/stderr/file destinations with rotation, root context), and offers root, child and configured loggers, runtime level changes and sensitive-data masking.

must_cover.text: Log messages with `log:printDebug`, `log:printInfo`, `log:printWarn` and `log:printError`, knowing that only `INFO` and higher are printed by default and that records go to `stderr` in logfmt format

Attach context as named key-value arguments, e.g. `log:printInfo("Processing order", orderId = 845315, amount = 99.99, user = user)`, where values can be any `anydata` including records (keys such as `message`, `time`, `level` and `error` are reserved)

Pass an `isolated function() returns anydata` (`log:Valuer`) as a key-value so it is evaluated only when the level is enabled, and use raw templates such as `` `Product: ${name}` `` as the message or a value

Log an error value with `log:printError("msg", err)` (or `'error = err`), together with extra key-values, so that the error message, its cause chain and detail fields appear in the record; an explicit `stackTrace` can also be passed
Set the global log level in `Config.toml` with `[ballerina.log]` `level = "DEBUG"` (one of `ERROR`, `WARN`, `INFO`, `DEBUG`)
Override the level for one module with a `[[ballerina.log.modules]]` entry that sets `name = "<org>/<module>"` and `level`
Switch the output format between logfmt and JSON with `format = "json"` or `"logfmt"` under `[ballerina.log]`

Send logs to `stderr`, `stdout` or a file by adding `[[ballerina.log.destinations]]` entries with `type` or a `path` ending in `.log` (file `mode` is `APPEND` by default or `TRUNCATE`), instead of the deprecated `log:setOutputFile()`

Rotate log files with a `[ballerina.log.destinations.rotation]` table (or a `rotation` record in code) setting `policy` (`SIZE_BASED`, `TIME_BASED` or `BOTH`), `maxFileSize` in bytes, `maxAge` in seconds and `maxBackupFiles`
Add default context to every log record with `keyValues` under `[ballerina.log]` (e.g. a `[ballerina.log.keyValues]` table with `env` and `nodeId`)

Get the root logger with `log:root()` and derive child loggers that carry context with `logger.withContext(requestId = id)` (returns `log:Logger|error`), nesting them and calling `printInfo` and friends on the `log:Logger`

Create a logger with its own settings using `log:fromConfig(...)` and a `log:Config` (`level`, `format` as `log:JSON_FORMAT` or `log:LOGFMT`, `destinations`, `keyValues`, `enableSensitiveDataMasking`), which returns `log:Logger|log:Error`, e.g. for a separate audit log

Change log levels at runtime: give a logger an `id` in `log:fromConfig`, call `setLevel(log:DEBUG)` / `getLevel()` on it, and find registered loggers with `log:getLoggerRegistry()` and its `getIds()` and `getById(id)` methods
Mark record fields with `@log:Sensitive` so they are excluded from log output once masking is enabled with `enableSensitiveDataMasking = true` under `[ballerina.log]` or in a logger's `log:Config`

Choose a masking strategy with `@log:Sensitive {strategy: {replacement: "****"}}` or a `replacement` function of type `log:ReplacementFunction` (`isolated function(string) returns string`), the default strategy being `log:EXCLUDE`
Get the masked string form of an `anydata` value for custom output with `log:toMaskedString(value)`

Write a custom logger as an `isolated class` that includes `*log:Logger` and implements `printDebug`, `printInfo`, `printWarn`, `printError`, `withContext`, `getLevel` and `setLevel`, using `log:evaluateTemplate` to render `log:PrintableRawTemplate` messages

out_of_scope: General Config.toml syntax and providing configurable values (tool.config_toml)
Metrics and tracing (lib.observe)
Shipping logs to observability platforms and log-based monitoring practices (topic.observability)
Printing plain output to the console (lib.io)
nodes.notes: Loggers, file destinations, rotation, the logger registry and sensitive-data masking are documented in the current README (log 2.17.x) and BBEs. The child-loggers BBE uses `check` on `withContext`, matching the `log:Logger` object type (`returns Logger|error`).

nodes.title: ballerina/math.vector
nodes.summary: The `math.vector` module provides vector operations on `float[]` values: L1/L2 norms, dot product, cosine similarity, Euclidean distance and Manhattan distance, useful for comparing embeddings.

must_cover.text: Compute the norm of a `float[]` with `vector:vectorNorm(v, vector:L2)` (square root of the sum of squares, e.g. 3.7416573867739413 for `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]`) or `vector:L1` (sum of absolute values)
Compute the dot product of two equal-length vectors with `vector:dotProduct(v1, v2)`, e.g. 32.0 for `[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]` and `[4.0, 5.0, 6.0]`
Measure the similarity of two vectors, such as text embeddings, with `vector:cosineSimilarity(v1, v2)`, which returns the dot product divided by the product of their L2 norms
Compute distances between equal-length vectors with `vector:euclideanDistance(v1, v2)` and `vector:manhattanDistance(v1, v2)`

Explain that these functions panic rather than return errors when the vectors have different lengths, or for `cosineSimilarity` when either vector is all zeros, and guard inputs or use `trap` accordingly
Find the most similar item by computing `vector:cosineSimilarity` between a query vector and each candidate `float[]` and keeping the highest score

out_of_scope: Embedding generation and vector stores for retrieval-augmented generation (lib.ai)
Scalar math functions such as `float:pow` and `float:sqrt` (lib.lang.float)

nodes.title: ballerina/mcp
nodes.summary: Model Context Protocol support over the Streamable HTTP transport: MCP servers written as services whose remote methods become tools (or advanced services with `onListTools`/`onCallTool`), and an `mcp:StreamableHttpClient` that discovers and calls tools on MCP servers.

must_cover.text: Create the server endpoint with `listener mcp:StreamableHttpListener mcpListener = check new (9090);` (a port or an existing `http:Listener`), replacing the deprecated `mcp:Listener` used in older code

Write an MCP server as `service mcp:StreamableHttpService /mcp on mcpListener` whose `remote function`s become tools, with tool descriptions and input schemas generated from the method signatures and `#` documentation
Override a tool's description with the optional `@mcp:Tool {description: "..."}` annotation on the remote method; without it the documentation string is used

Respect the tool rules: parameters must be subtypes of `anydata` (except runtime-injected `mcp:Session` and `mcp:Meta?`) and the return type a subtype of `anydata|error`, e.g. `remote function getCurrentWeather(string city) returns Weather|error`
Configure the server with `@mcp:StreamableHttpServiceConfig {info: {name: "MCP Weather Server", version: "1.0.0"}, sessionMode: mcp:AUTO, httpConfig: {cors: {...}}, options: {instructions: "..."}}`
Choose a session mode: `mcp:STATEFUL` (transport-managed session IDs the client must keep), `mcp:STATELESS` (independent requests) or `mcp:AUTO` (default, decided by the client's initialization)

Keep per-client state in a stateful service by declaring `mcp:Session session` as the first tool parameter and using `session.set(key, value)`, `session.get(key)`, `session.getWithType(key)`, `session.hasKey(key)` and `session.getSessionId()`

Read client-supplied request metadata by adding a nilable `mcp:Meta? meta` parameter to a tool and reading keys with member access such as `meta["requestId"]`; it is excluded from the tool's input schema

Bind HTTP request information in `mcp:StreamableHttpService` tools with `@http:Header` parameters, an `http:Headers` parameter or an `http:Request` parameter (header parameters are excluded from the input schema)

sources.note: Constraints for defining MCP tools, item 6

must_cover.text: Control tool listing and dispatch with `service mcp:StreamableHttpAdvancedService` implementing exactly `remote isolated function onListTools() returns mcp:ListToolsResult|mcp:ServerError` (tool `name`, `description`, JSON `inputSchema`) and `onCallTool(mcp:CallToolParams params)`

In `onCallTool(mcp:CallToolParams params, mcp:Session? session)`, dispatch on `params.name`, bind `params.arguments.cloneWithType()` to a record, return `mcp:CallToolResult` such as `{content: [{'type: "text", text: result.toJsonString()}]}`, and return `error mcp:ServerError(...)` for unknown tools

Use the transport-agnostic `mcp:Service` and `mcp:AdvancedService` types when tools need no HTTP request information; they are still supported, but `mcp:StreamableHttpService`/`mcp:StreamableHttpAdvancedService` are preferred

Create an MCP client with `final mcp:StreamableHttpClient mcpClient = check new ("http://localhost:3000/mcp")`, optionally passing `mcp:StreamableHttpClientTransportConfig` fields such as `timeout` and `followRedirects`
Start the MCP session with `mcpClient->initialize({name: "My MCP Client", version: "1.0.0"})`, optionally passing client capabilities such as `{roots: {listChanged: true}}` and custom headers
Discover tools with `mcp:ListToolsResult toolsResult = check mcpClient->listTools();` and iterate the `mcp:ToolDefinition` values (`name`, optional `description`, `inputSchema`)
Invoke a tool with `mcpClient->callTool({name: "getCurrentWeather", arguments: {city: "London"}}, headers)` returning `mcp:CallToolResult`, and release the connection with `mcpClient->close()`
Handle client failures through `mcp:ClientError` and its subtypes such as `mcp:ClientInitializationError`, `mcp:ListToolsError`, `mcp:ToolCallError` and `mcp:StreamableHttpTransportError`

out_of_scope: Using MCP tools from an AI agent via `ai:McpToolKit` (lib.ai)
HTTP service configuration such as CORS in general (lib.http)
Designing agent tool sets (topic.ai_agents)

edges.note: Doc comments become tool descriptions
cloneWithType on params.arguments
