nodes.title: ballerina/mime
nodes.summary: The MIME library models message entities (headers plus body) with `mime:Entity`, and is used to build and parse multipart bodies, set and read typed content, handle large files as streams and work with media types.

must_cover.text: Create a `mime:Entity` with `new` and set its body with `setJson()`, `setXml()`, `setText()`, `setByteArray()` or `setBody()`, then read it back with `getJson()`, `getXml()`, `getText()` and `getByteArray()`, handling `mime:ParserError`

Manipulate entity headers with `setHeader()`, `addHeader()`, `getHeader()`, `getHeaders()`, `hasHeader()`, `removeHeader()` and `getHeaderNames()`, and set metadata with `setContentType()`, `getContentType()`, `setContentId()` and `setContentLength()`, handling `mime:HeaderNotFoundError`

Use the media type constants such as `mime:APPLICATION_JSON`, `mime:APPLICATION_XML`, `mime:TEXT_PLAIN`, `mime:APPLICATION_PDF`, `mime:IMAGE_JPEG` and `mime:MULTIPART_FORM_DATA`, and parse a Content-Type string with `mime:getMediaType()` to compare `getBaseType()`
Describe body parts with `mime:ContentDisposition` (setting `name`, `fileName` and `disposition` such as `"form-data"` or `"attachment"`) and attach it with `entity.setContentDisposition()`

Build multipart bodies by creating child `mime:Entity` parts and calling `setBodyParts(parts, contentType = mime:MULTIPART_FORM_DATA)` (or `MULTIPART_MIXED`, `MULTIPART_ALTERNATIVE`, `MULTIPART_RELATED`, `MULTIPART_PARALLEL`), including nested multipart parts, and attach them to an `http:Request`/`http:Response`
Decode multipart messages with `getBodyParts()`, iterate the returned `mime:Entity[]`, dispatch on each part's base media type, and recurse into parts whose content type starts with `multipart/`

Handle large content without loading it into memory by setting a file as the body with `setFileAsEntityBody(path, contentType)` and reading the body as `stream<byte[], io:Error?>` with `getByteStream()`, closing the stream when done
Encode and decode content with `mime:base64Encode()`, `mime:base64Decode()`, `mime:base64EncodeBlob()` and `mime:base64DecodeBlob()`, handling `mime:EncodeError` and `mime:DecodeError`
Build an email attachment as a `mime:Entity` with a content disposition, content ID and `setFileAsEntityBody(path, mime:IMAGE_JPEG)` and pass it in the `attachments` field of an `email:Message`

out_of_scope: HTTP request/response APIs that wrap entities (lib.http)
Sending email (lib.email)
General byte-stream and file I/O (lib.io)
nodes.notes: API names confirmed against ballerina/mime master natives.bal. The `@untainted`/`@tainted` annotations still present in the source are not relevant to user code.

nodes.title: ballerinax/mongodb
nodes.summary: The MongoDB connector: a `mongodb:Client` connected by connection parameters or a connection string, with `mongodb:Database` and `mongodb:Collection` clients for document CRUD, typed queries returning streams, aggregation pipelines and index management.

must_cover.text: Create a `mongodb:Client` from connection parameters, e.g. `check new ({connection: {serverAddress: {host: "localhost", port: 27017}, auth: <mongodb:ScramSha256AuthCredential>{username, password, database: "admin"}}})`
Create a `mongodb:Client` from a connection string (e.g. one copied from MongoDB Atlas) with `check new ({connection: "mongodb+srv://..."})`

Choose an authentication record (`mongodb:BasicAuthCredential`, `mongodb:ScramSha1AuthCredential`, `mongodb:ScramSha256AuthCredential`, `mongodb:X509Credential`, `mongodb:GssApiCredential`) and set connection `options` such as `sslEnabled`, `secureSocket`, `replicaSet`, `readConcern`, `writeConcern`, `readPreference` and `maxPoolSize`
Navigate and manage data with `mongoDb->getDatabase("movies")`, `db->getCollection("movies")`, `listDatabaseNames()`, `listCollectionNames()`, `createCollection(name)` and `drop()`
Insert Ballerina records as documents with `collection->insertOne(movie)` and `collection->insertMany(movies)`

Query documents with `collection->find({year: 2010})`, binding results to `stream<Movie, error?>` through the inferred `targetType`, passing `mongodb:FindOptions` (`sort`, `'limit`, `skip`, `batchSize`), and closing the stream when done
Fetch a single document with `collection->findOne(filter)`, which returns the typed record or `()` when nothing matches
Limit returned fields either implicitly through a target record type with a subset of fields or explicitly with a `projection` map such as `{title: 1, year: 1}`

Update documents with `collection->updateOne(filter, {set: {...}, inc: {...}})` or `updateMany`, using `mongodb:Update` operators and `{upsert: true}` in `mongodb:UpdateOptions`, and read `matchedCount`, `modifiedCount` and `upsertedId` from `mongodb:UpdateResult`
Delete documents with `collection->deleteOne(filter)` or `deleteMany(filter)` and read `deletedCount` from `mongodb:DeleteResult`
Count matching documents with `collection->countDocuments(filter)` and get distinct field values as a stream with `collection->'distinct("genre")`
Run aggregation pipelines with `collection->aggregate([{"$match": {...}}, {"$group": {...}}], ResultType)`, which returns a `stream` of the target type
Manage indexes with `collection->createIndex({title: 1}, {unique: true})`, `listIndexes()`, `dropIndex(name)` and `dropIndexes()`

Handle `mongodb:Error` (a union of `mongodb:DatabaseError` with detail `mongoDBExceptionType`, `mongodb:ApplicationError` and `error`) and close the client with the remote call `check mongoDb->close()`

out_of_scope: Relational database access (lib.sql)
General connector usage patterns (topic.connectors)

sources.note: ConnectionConfig, credentials, options, Update, result types

edges.note: Filters, updates and pipelines are map<json>

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-mongodb master (5.2.4). The README quickstart calls `collection->insert(movie)`, but the Collection API defines `insertOne`/`insertMany`; items use the source names.

nodes.title: ballerina/mqtt
nodes.summary: The MQTT library publishes messages with `mqtt:Client` and subscribes to topics with an `mqtt:Listener` service, supporting QoS, manual acknowledgements, request-response and TLS/basic authentication.

must_cover.text: Create an `mqtt:Client` with `check new (mqtt:DEFAULT_URL, clientId)` (a unique id, e.g. `uuid:createType1AsString()`) and publish with `mqttClient->publish("mqtt/topic", {payload: data.toJsonString().toBytes()})`, which returns an `mqtt:DeliveryToken`
Build and read `mqtt:Message` records with `payload` (`byte[]`), `qos` (0, 1 or 2), `retained`, and on received messages `topic`, `messageId` and `duplicate`

Subscribe with `service on new mqtt:Listener(mqtt:DEFAULT_URL, clientId, "mqtt/topic")` implementing `remote function onMessage(mqtt:Message message)`, converting the payload with `string:fromBytes()` and `value:fromJsonStringWithType()`, plus optional `onError(mqtt:Error err)`
Acknowledge messages explicitly by setting `manualAcks: true` in `mqtt:ListenerConfiguration` and calling `caller->complete()` on the `mqtt:Caller` parameter of `onMessage`
Subscribe to several topics or with a chosen QoS by passing `string[]` or `mqtt:Subscription {topic, qos}` values as the listener's subscriptions

Implement request-response: the publisher calls `subscribe(responseTopic)`, publishes with `properties: {responseTopic, correlationData}` and reads replies from `receiveResponse()`, while the subscriber replies with `caller->respond({payload: ...})`
Authenticate and secure connections with `connectionConfig: {username, password, secureSocket: {cert, key}}` in the client or listener configuration, using an `ssl://` URL for TLS
Manage client connections with `isConnected()`, `reconnect()`, `disconnect()` and `close()`

out_of_scope: Other messaging brokers (lib.kafka, lib.rabbitmq, lib.nats)
Event-driven architecture patterns (topic.event_driven)
nodes.notes: Remote method names (`publish`, `subscribe`, `receiveResponse`, `isConnected`, `reconnect`, `disconnect`, `close`, caller `complete`/`respond`) are from the mqtt spec (mqtt 1.4.x).

nodes.title: ballerinax/mssql
nodes.summary: The Microsoft SQL Server connector: an `mssql:Client` implementing the `sql:Client` API, with SQL Server connection options, TLS encryption, money and spatial typed values, and an `mssql:CdcListener` for SQL Server change data capture.

must_cover.text: Add the SQL Server JDBC driver by importing `ballerinax/mssql.driver as _;`, or pin a version in `Ballerina.toml` with `[[platform.java21.dependency]]` `groupId = "com.microsoft.sqlserver"`, `artifactId = "mssql-jdbc"`

Create an `mssql:Client` with `new ("localhost", "rootUser", "rootPass", "information_schema", 1433)` (host, user, password, database, port) or named arguments, knowing the defaults are user `"sa"` and port 1433 and that a named SQL Server instance is given with the `instance` argument
Configure `mssql:Options` fields `loginTimeout`, `socketTimeout`, `queryTimeout` and `useXADatasource`

Encrypt the connection with `secureSocket: {encrypt: true, trustServerCertificate: false, cert: {path, password}, key: {path, password}}` in `mssql:Options`, using `trustServerCertificate: true` only for local testing
Pass `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}` or a shared `sql:ConnectionPool` record to `mssql:Client`, or omit it to use the global pool
Use the `sql:Client` remote methods on `mssql:Client` (`query`, `queryRow`, `execute`, `batchExecute`, `call`) with `sql:ParameterizedQuery` templates
Pass SQL Server `MONEY` and `SMALLMONEY` parameters with `mssql:MoneyValue` and `mssql:SmallMoneyValue` (values of `decimal`, `float` or `string`)

Pass SQL Server geometry values with `mssql:PointValue` (from `mssql:Point {x, y}` and an optional `srid`), `mssql:LineStringValue`, `mssql:PolygonValue`, `mssql:MultiPointValue` and `mssql:GeometryCollectionValue`

Enable SQL Server CDC (SQL Server Agent running, `EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db`, `EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table`) and configure an `mssql:CdcListener` whose `database` gives `username`, `password`, `databaseNames` and optionally `databaseInstance`, `includedSchemas` and `includedTables`

out_of_scope: Generic query/execute/call semantics and common typed values (lib.sql)
CDC service handlers, options and offset storage (lib.cdc)
Using SQL Server through generated persist clients (lib.persist)
nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-mssql master (1.19.1). The README CDC example omits `databaseNames`, but `MsSqlDatabaseConnection.databaseNames` is a required field in the source. The README SSL sample is missing a comma after `trustServerCertificate: false`.

nodes.title: ballerinax/mysql
nodes.summary: The MySQL connector: a `mysql:Client` that implements the `sql:Client` API for MySQL, plus MySQL-specific connection options (SSL, failover, timeouts, XA) and a `mysql:CdcListener` for change data capture.

must_cover.text: Add the MySQL JDBC driver by importing `ballerinax/mysql.driver as _;` (bundles the driver JAR and enables GraalVM native builds)

Use a specific MySQL driver version instead by declaring it in `Ballerina.toml` under `[[platform.java17.dependency]]`, either with `path = "..."` or with `groupId = "mysql"`, `artifactId = "mysql-connector-java"` and `version`

Create a `mysql:Client` with positional arguments `new ("localhost", "root", "Test@123", "MUSIC_STORE", 3306)` (host, user, password, database, port) or with named arguments such as `new (user = "rootUser", password = "rootPass", options = mysqlOptions)`, and handle the `sql:Error` returned on failure
Configure `mysql:Options` fields `connectTimeout`, `socketTimeout`, `serverTimezone` and `noAccessToProcedureBodies` when creating the client

Connect over SSL by setting `ssl` in `mysql:Options` with a `mode` (`mysql:SSL_PREFERRED`, `mysql:SSL_REQUIRED`, `mysql:SSL_VERIFY_CA`, `mysql:SSL_VERIFY_IDENTITY`, `mysql:SSL_DISABLED`), `.p12` `key`/`cert` keystores (`{path, password}`) and optionally `allowPublicKeyRetrieval`
Configure server failover with `failoverConfig: {failoverServers: [{host: "...", port: 3306}], timeBeforeRetry: ..., queriesBeforeRetry: ..., failoverReadOnly: true}` in `mysql:Options`
Enable XA (distributed) transactions for the client with `useXADatasource: true` in `mysql:Options`
Pass `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}` (client-owned pool) or a shared `sql:ConnectionPool` record to `mysql:Client`, or omit it to use the global pool

Use the `sql:Client` remote methods on `mysql:Client` (`query`, `queryRow`, `execute`, `batchExecute`, `call`), e.g. in an HTTP service that stores the client in a `private final mysql:Client db` field initialized in `init`
Insert into a table with an `AUTO_INCREMENT` key and read the generated id from `sql:ExecutionResult.lastInsertId`

Make an order insert and inventory update atomic with `transaction { ... check commit; }`, rolling back when `affectedRowCount == 0`, and inspect MySQL error codes in `on fail` via `e is sql:DatabaseError` and `e.detail().errorCode` (e.g. 3819 for a CHECK constraint violation)

Create a MySQL procedure with `IN`/`INOUT`/`OUT` parameters via `execute`, then call it with `mysqlClient->call(`{CALL GetCount(${id}, ${totalCount})}`, [Student])` using `sql:InOutParameter` and `sql:IntegerOutParameter`, and close the `sql:ProcedureCallResult`

Prepare MySQL for change data capture (binary logging with `log-bin` and `binlog-format=ROW`) and configure a `mysql:CdcListener` with MySQL-specific `database` fields such as `hostname`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `includedDatabases` and `includedTables`

out_of_scope: Generic query/execute/call semantics, typed values and error types (lib.sql)
CDC service handlers, options and offset storage (lib.cdc)
Using MySQL through generated persist clients (lib.persist)

sources.note: Client init, Options, FailoverConfig, SecureSocket, SSL modes
MySQL BBE series (query, queryRow, execute, batch, transactions, procedures)

edges.note: key/cert are crypto:KeyStore / crypto:TrustStore

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-mysql master (1.19.1). The MySQL CDC driver package (`ballerinax/mysql.cdc.driver`) is listed on lib.cdc.

nodes.title: ballerinax/nats
nodes.summary: NATS connector for core publish-subscribe and request-reply messaging through `nats:Client` and `nats:Listener` services, plus persistent JetStream messaging through `nats:JetStreamClient` and `nats:JetStreamListener`.

must_cover.text: Create a `nats:Client` with `check new (nats:DEFAULT_URL)`, a server URL, or an array of URLs plus `nats:ConnectionConfiguration` fields such as `connectionName`, `noEcho`, `retryConfig` and `ping`, and close it with `close()`
Publish with `client->publishMessage({content: newOrder, subject: "orders.valid"})`, where `content` is any `anydata`, optionally setting a `replyTo` subject
Send a request and wait for the reply with `client->requestMessage({content, subject}, timeout)`, binding the reply to a subtype such as `record {| *nats:AnydataMessage; string content; |}`

Subscribe with a service on `nats:Listener`, naming the subject as the service name (`service "orders.valid" on new nats:Listener(nats:DEFAULT_URL)`) or with `@nats:ServiceConfig {subject: "demo.example.*"}` wildcards, and handle messages in `remote function onMessage(Order 'order)`
Bind `onMessage` parameters to the payload type directly or to `nats:AnydataMessage`/`nats:BytesMessage` subtypes to also read the `subject` and `replyTo` fields
Load-balance a subject across service instances by setting `queueName` in `@nats:ServiceConfig {subject: ..., queueName: ...}` so each message goes to one member of the queue group
Answer request messages with `remote function onRequest(Order 'order) returns string|error`, whose return value is published to the request's `replyTo` subject

Validate bound payloads with `@constraint` annotations and handle binding or validation failures in `remote function onError(nats:AnydataMessage message, nats:Error err)`, checking for `nats:PayloadValidationError`
Secure client and listener connections with `secureSocket = {cert: "path/public.crt"}` or a `nats:SecureSocket` with truststore `cert` and keystore `key`
Authenticate with `auth = {username: "alice", password: "alice@123"}` (`nats:Credentials`) or a token via `nats:Tokens {token}` when creating the client or listener

Create a `nats:JetStreamClient` from a `nats:Client`, define a stream with `addStream({name: "demo", subjects: ["orders"], storageType: nats:MEMORY})` and publish `byte[]` content with `publishMessage({subject, content})`

Consume JetStream messages with `listener nats:JetStreamListener` created from a `nats:Client`, a `service nats:JetStreamService` annotated with `@nats:StreamServiceConfig {subject, autoAck: false}`, and `remote function onMessage(nats:JetStreamMessage message)` that converts `message.content` bytes to a record
Pull a JetStream message with `jetStreamClient->consumeMessage(subject, timeout)` and settle it with `ack(message)`, `nak(message)` or `inProgress(message)`

Manage streams with `updateStream`, `deleteStream` and `purgeStream`, configuring `nats:StreamConfiguration` options such as `retentionPolicy` (`nats:LIMITS`, `INTEREST`, `WORKQUEUE`), `storageType` (`nats:FILE`, `MEMORY`), `maxMsgs` and `maxAge`

out_of_scope: General listener and service declaration semantics (concept.services_listeners)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)
Converting bytes to JSON and records in general (lib.data.jsondata)

edges.note: Both provide broker-based publish/consume clients and listener services

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-nats master (3.3.2, same as latest on Central). The README snippet `natsClient->publish(...)` does not match the API (the method is `publishMessage`). The JetStream BBEs are not listed on the BBE site (isLearnByExample false); the BBE URLs are given by slug. `nats:JetStreamCaller` (ack/nak/inProgress) exists, but no README/BBE shows it as an `onMessage` parameter, so it is not listed as a service item.

nodes.title: ballerina/oauth2
nodes.summary: The `oauth2` module talks to OAuth2 authorization servers (RFC 6749, RFC 7662): a client provider that obtains and caches access tokens with the client credentials, password, refresh token and JWT bearer grants, and a listener provider that validates tokens through an introspection endpoint.

must_cover.text: Obtain an access token with the client credentials grant by creating an `oauth2:ClientOAuth2Provider` from an `oauth2:ClientCredentialsGrantConfig` (`tokenUrl`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, optional `scopes`) and calling `generateToken()`, which returns `string|oauth2:Error`
Use the password grant with an `oauth2:PasswordGrantConfig` (`tokenUrl`, `username`, `password`, optional `clientId`, `clientSecret` and `scopes`)
Let the password grant refresh expired tokens by setting `refreshConfig` to an `oauth2:RefreshConfig` (`refreshUrl`, `scopes`, ...) or to `oauth2:INFER_REFRESH_CONFIG` to reuse the grant's own values
Use the refresh token grant with an `oauth2:RefreshTokenGrantConfig` (`refreshUrl`, `refreshToken`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, optional `scopes`)
Use the JWT bearer grant with an `oauth2:JwtBearerGrantConfig` (`tokenUrl`, an `assertion` holding a JWT, optional `clientId`, `clientSecret` and `scopes`)
Explain that `generateToken()` reuses the cached access token until it expires, and tune this with `defaultTokenExpTime` (used when the response has no `expires_in`, default 3600 s) and `clockSkew`

Choose how the client credentials reach the token endpoint with `credentialBearer` (`oauth2:AUTH_HEADER_BEARER` by default or `oauth2:POST_BODY_BEARER`) and send extra request parameters with `optionalParams`

Configure the HTTP client used to call the token or introspection endpoint with `clientConfig` (`oauth2:ClientConfiguration`: `httpVersion`, `customHeaders`, `customPayload`, `auth`, `secureSocket` with `cert` and `key`, `connectTimeout`, `reqTimeout`)

Set default token-endpoint timeouts for every provider through the module configurables `globalConnectTimeout` (default 15 s) and `globalReqTimeout` (default 30 s) under `[ballerina.oauth2]` in Config.toml

Validate an incoming access token with `oauth2:ListenerOAuth2Provider`, created from an `oauth2:IntrospectionConfig` (`url`, optional `tokenTypeHint`, `optionalParams`, `cacheConfig`, `defaultTokenExpTime`, `clientConfig`), by calling `authorize(token)`
Check the `active` flag of the returned `oauth2:IntrospectionResponse` and read its `scope`, `clientId`, `username`, `tokenType`, `exp`, `iat`, `sub`, `aud`, `iss` and `jti` fields

Secure a service with OAuth2 by adding an `oauth2IntrospectionConfig` entry (introspection `url`, `tokenTypeHint`, `scopeKey`, `clientConfig`) and `scopes` to the connector's service `auth` configuration, e.g. `@http:ServiceConfig`

Make a connector client fetch and attach OAuth2 access tokens automatically by passing a grant configuration (client credentials, password, refresh token or JWT bearer fields) as the client's `auth` configuration, e.g. `http:Client`

out_of_scope: Basic Auth providers (lib.auth)
Issuing and validating JWTs locally (lib.jwt)
Full HTTP auth configuration records and auth handlers (lib.http)

nodes.title: ballerina/observe
nodes.summary: The `observe` module exposes Ballerina's built-in observability: custom tracing spans and tags, custom counter and gauge metrics, and the runtime switches, while extension modules (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Jaeger, Zipkin, New Relic, Moesif) report the collected metrics and traces once observability is included at build time and enabled in Config.toml.

must_cover.text: Include observability in the build by setting `observabilityIncluded = true` under `[build-options]` in Ballerina.toml (generated by default by `bal new`) or by running with the `--observability-included` flag

Enable metrics and tracing at runtime in Config.toml with `[ballerina.observe]` `enabled = true` and a `provider`, or separately with `metricsEnabled`/`metricsReporter` and `tracingEnabled`/`tracingProvider` (e.g. `otel`, `prometheus`, `jaeger`, `zipkin`, `newrelic`)

Expose metrics for Prometheus by adding `import ballerinax/prometheus as _;`, setting `metricsReporter = "prometheus"`, and configuring the `/metrics` endpoint with `[ballerinax.prometheus]` `host` and `port` (default 9797)

Publish traces to Jaeger or Zipkin by adding `import ballerinax/jaeger as _;` (or `ballerinax/zipkin`), setting `tracingProvider = "jaeger"` (or `"zipkin"`), and configuring `[ballerinax.jaeger]` `agentHostname`, `agentPort`, `samplerType`, `samplerParam`, `reporterFlushInterval` and `reporterBufferSize`

Export traces and metrics over OTLP with the bundled `ballerina/otel` extension (Swan Lake Update 14+, no import needed) by setting `tracingProvider = "otel"` and `metricsReporter = "otel"` and configuring `[ballerina.otel]` `tracesEndpoint`, `metricsEndpoint`, `metricsServiceName` and optional protocol, sampler and resource-attribute settings

Report to hosted platforms by importing `ballerinax/newrelic as _` (configured with `[ballerinax.newrelic]` `apiKey`) or `ballerinax/moesif as _` (`[ballerinax.moesif]` `applicationId`) and setting them as the tracing provider and metrics reporter

Explain that services, resource and remote functions, client calls, workers and `main` are observed automatically with common tags such as `src.module`, `src.resource.path`, `src.resource.accessor`, `entrypoint.function.name` and `error`, and use `@observe:Observable` to make another function observable
Measure a block of code as a span inside the current system trace with `int spanId = check observe:startSpan("MyLogicSpan")` and close it with `observe:finishSpan(spanId)`

Start an independent trace with `observe:startRootSpan("Parent")` and attach children with `observe:startSpan("Child", (), parentSpanId)`, finishing every span (or `observe:finishSpanWithError(spanId, err)` to record a failure)

Add tags to spans with `observe:addTagToSpan("key", "value")` (current span) or `observe:addTagToSpan("key", "value", spanId)`, add tags to system metrics with `observe:addTagToMetrics`, and read the trace and span IDs with `observe:getSpanContext()`
Count events with `observe:Counter c = new ("total_orders", desc = "...", tags = {...});`, using `increment()` or `increment(amount)`, `reset()` and `getValue()`

Track values that go up and down with `observe:Gauge` using `increment`, `decrement`, `setValue` and `getValue`, and get statistics from `getSnapshot()` configured by `observe:StatisticConfig` (`timeWindow`, `buckets`, `percentiles`), or disable them with an empty config array

Register a counter or gauge in the global registry with `register()` (returns `error?`) so it is reported to the metrics backend, remove it with `unregister()`, and look metrics up with `observe:lookupMetric(name, tags)` or `observe:getAllMetrics()`
Check the observability state at runtime with `observe:isObservabilityEnabled()`, `isMetricsEnabled()`, `isTracingEnabled()`, `getMetricsReporter()` and `getTracingProvider()`

out_of_scope: Logging, log formats and log destinations (lib.log)
Setting up dashboards, collectors and platforms such as Grafana, Datadog or Elastic Stack (topic.observability)
Ballerina.toml build options in general (tool.ballerina_toml)
nodes.notes: Datadog and Elastic Stack guides reuse the Prometheus/Jaeger extensions and log shipping; OpenSearch is also listed in the docs but not reviewed. `ballerina/otel` is bundled from Swan Lake Update 14 per the OpenTelemetry guide.

nodes.title: ballerinax/oracledb
nodes.summary: The Oracle Database connector: an `oracledb:Client` implementing the `sql:Client` API, Oracle connection options, Oracle-specific types (INTERVAL, VARRAY, nested tables, OBJECT types) and OUT parameters, and an `oracledb:CdcListener` based on LogMiner.

must_cover.text: Add the Oracle JDBC drivers by importing `ballerinax/oracledb.driver as _;`, or pin versions in `Ballerina.toml` with `[[platform.java17.dependency]]` entries for `ojdbc11`, `xdb` and `xmlparserv2`

Create an `oracledb:Client` with `new ("localhost", "adminUser", "adminPassword", "ORCLCDB.localdomain", 1521)` (host, user, password, database SID or service name, port) or named arguments, knowing the defaults are user `"sys"` and port 1521
Configure `oracledb:Options` with `ssl: {key: {path, password}, cert: {path, password}}`, `loginTimeout`, `autoCommit`, `connectTimeout`, `socketTimeout` and `useXADatasource`
Pass `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}` or a shared `sql:ConnectionPool` record to `oracledb:Client`, or omit it to use the global pool
Use the `sql:Client` remote methods on `oracledb:Client` (`query`, `queryRow`, `execute`, `batchExecute`, `call`) with `sql:ParameterizedQuery` templates

Represent Oracle `INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH` and `INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND` values with `oracledb:IntervalYearToMonth {years, months, sign}` and `oracledb:IntervalDayToSecond {days, hours, minutes, seconds, sign}`, where `sign` is `oracledb:Sign` (`+1` or `-1`)

Pass Oracle collection types with `oracledb:VarrayValue` wrapping an `oracledb:Varray {name: "CharArrayType", elements: charArray}` and `oracledb:NestedTableValue` wrapping an `oracledb:NestedTableType`

Pass Oracle `OBJECT` type values with `oracledb:ObjectTypeValue` wrapping `oracledb:ObjectType {typename, attributes}`, and capture an Oracle function returning an OBJECT with `oracledb:ObjectOutParameter returnValue = new ("MY_OBJECT_TYPE");` in `` `{${returnValue} = call myFunc(${param})}` ``
Read Oracle-specific procedure results with `oracledb:XmlOutParameter`, `oracledb:IntervalYearToMonthOutParameter` and `oracledb:IntervalDayToSecondOutParameter`, calling `get()` after `call`

Capture Oracle changes with LogMiner by importing `ballerinax/oracledb.cdc.driver as _;` and creating an `oracledb:CdcListener` whose `database` gives `username`, `password`, `databaseName` (the CDB), `pdbName` for a pluggable database, and an `includedTables` regular expression

out_of_scope: Generic query/execute/call semantics and common typed values (lib.sql)
CDC service handlers, snapshot options and offset storage (lib.cdc)

sources.note: Module README (client, custom data types, CDC)
Interval, Varray, ObjectType records; TypedValue and OutParameter classes

nodes.title: ballerina/os
nodes.summary: The `os` module reads, sets and lists environment variables, returns the current OS user's name and home directory, and runs operating system commands as subprocesses through `os:exec` and `os:Process`.

must_cover.text: Read an environment variable with `os:getEnv("HTTP_PORT")`, which returns the value as a `string`, or an empty string when the variable is not set, and fall back to a default when it is empty
Set an environment variable for the current process with `os:setEnv(key, value)` and remove one with `os:unsetEnv(key)`, both returning `os:Error?` (an empty key, or `==` for `setEnv`, is rejected)
Get all environment variables as a `map<string>` with `os:listEnv()` and iterate or look them up by key
Get the current user's name with `os:getUsername()` and home directory with `os:getUserHome()`, each returning an empty string if it cannot be determined

Run an OS command with `os:exec({value: "/usr/bin/git", arguments: ["status"]})`, passing an `os:Command` record with the executable in `value` and each argument as a separate `arguments` element, and get an `os:Process` or an `os:Error`

Pass extra environment variables to the child process as named arguments of `os:exec`, e.g. `os:exec({value: "bal", arguments: ["run", path]}, BAL_CONFIG_FILES = "/abc/Config.toml")`, through the included `os:EnvProperties` record
Wait for a subprocess to finish with `process.waitForExit()`, which returns the exit code as an `int` (0 on success), and branch on non-zero codes
Read a subprocess's standard output as `byte[]` with `process.output()` (or standard error with `process.output(io:stderr)`) and convert it with `string:fromBytes`
Terminate a running subprocess with `process.exit()`
Handle `os:Error` and its subtype `os:ProcessExecError`, which is returned when `os:exec` fails to start the command

Execute commands safely (static rules `ballerina/os:1`, `os:3`, `os:4`): do not build arguments from unsanitised input, do not run a command string through `/bin/sh -c`, and name executables by absolute path rather than relying on `PATH`
Avoid setting environment variables from untrusted input with `os:setEnv` (static rule `ballerina/os:2`), since they affect every process started afterwards

out_of_scope: Configurable variables and Config.toml as the preferred way to supply configuration (tool.config_toml)
File system operations (lib.file)

edges.note: included record parameter `*EnvProperties` passed as named arguments
`io:stdout`/`io:stderr` select the stream for `Process.output`

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-os master 1.10.3 (= latest tag). The module README only lists env vars and user info; `exec`/`Process` details come from the module spec section 4 and process.bal.

nodes.title: ballerina/persist
nodes.summary: Ballerina persist expresses an application's data model as entity record types and uses a generated, type-safe client with resource methods for CRUD, projection and relation queries over pluggable data stores (in-memory, MySQL/MSSQL/PostgreSQL, Google Sheets, Redis).

must_cover.text: Define the data model as record types in a `.bal` file under the project's `persist` directory, where every record type is an entity and the file is used only for model definition, not compiled with the package
Mark identity fields with `readonly` (e.g. `readonly string id;`), using one or more fields for a composite key, and restrict them to `int`, `string`, `float`, `boolean` or `decimal`

Model attributes with simple types (`()`, `boolean`, `int`, `float`, `decimal`, `string`, `byte[]`, `time:Date`, `time:TimeOfDay`, `time:Utc`, `time:Civil`, enums), use `T?` for nullable columns, and avoid unions such as `int|string` and optional `T field?` (allowed only for Redis), knowing supported types vary by data store

Define a one-to-one relation with an `EntityType` field on the owner and an `EntityType?` field on the other entity (e.g. `User owner;` in `Car` and `Car? car;` in `User`), where the owner gets a foreign key such as `ownerId`

Define a one-to-many relation with `User owner;` on one side and `Car[] cars;` on the other, and a many-to-many relation through a join entity holding two `EntityType` fields (e.g. `CarUser` with `Car car; User user;`)

Use the generated derived types for an entity: the entity type itself (with foreign key fields), `EmployeeInsert` for creates, `EmployeeUpdate` with all-optional non-key fields, `EmployeeOptionalized`, `EmployeeWithRelations` and `EmployeeTargetType`

Initialize the generated client with `store:Client sClient = check new ();` after importing the generated module, providing data store settings in `Config.toml` under `[<package>.<module>]` (e.g. `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database` for SQL; `spreadsheetId`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `refreshToken` for Google Sheets; `connectionConfig`/`cacheConfig` for Redis)
Insert one or more records with `sClient->/employees.post([employee1, employee2])`, passing `store:EmployeeInsert` values and receiving the `string[]` of inserted keys
Read all records of an entity as `stream<store:Employee, persist:Error?> employees = sClient->/employees;` and iterate it with a query expression

Read a single record by key with `store:Employee employee = check sClient->/employees/[empId];`, using one path segment per identity field for composite keys, and handle `persist:NotFoundError` when the key does not exist
Project a subset of fields by declaring a custom target record type (e.g. `EmployeeName` with `id`, `firstName`, `lastName`) for `sClient->/employees` or `sClient->/employees/[id]`

Fetch related entities (an SQL join) by declaring a target type with a nested record field for a one-to-one relation or a record-array field for a one-to-many relation (e.g. `DepartmentEmployees` with an `employees` array)
Update a record with `sClient->/employees/[empId].put({hireDate: {...}})`, passing only the fields to change as `store:EmployeeUpdate`, and receive the updated entity
Delete a record with `sClient->/employees/[empId].delete()`, which returns the deleted entity
Filter, sort and limit retrieved streams with query expressions, e.g. `from var e in sClient->/employees where e.gender == "Male" order by e.firstName ascending limit 2 select e`

With SQL data stores, push filtering into the database by passing `sql:ParameterizedQuery` arguments `whereClause`, `orderByClause`, `limitClause` and `groupByClause` to the generated get-all resource method

Run hand-written SQL through the generated client with `sClient->queryNativeSQL(`SELECT ...`)` (returns a stream of the row type) and `sClient->executeNativeSQL(`UPDATE ...`)` (returns an execution result) on SQL data stores

Handle `persist:Error` and its subtypes `persist:NotFoundError`, `persist:AlreadyExistsError` and `persist:ConstraintViolationError` returned by client operations, and close the client with `check sClient.close()`

Customise SQL mapping in the model by importing `ballerinax/persist.sql` and annotating entities and fields with `@sql:Name {value: "people"}`, `@sql:Varchar {length: 100}`, `@sql:Char {length: 12}` and `@sql:Decimal {precision: [10, 2]}`

Declare indexes with `@sql:Index` and `@sql:UniqueIndex` (optionally named, composite by sharing a name), auto-generated keys with `@sql:Generated` on a `readonly int` field (removed from the Insert type), and custom foreign keys with `@sql:Relation {keys: ["userId"]}`

out_of_scope: The `bal persist` CLI commands (`init`, `add`, `generate`, `migrate`) and build integration (tool.bal_persist)
Direct SQL access with the sql client API (lib.sql)
Connection-level options of the underlying database connectors (lib.mysql, lib.postgresql, lib.mssql, lib.redis)

sources.note: Data model (entities, identity, relations, SQL annotations)
Derived types and generated client API
SQL data stores, type mapping, advanced annotations, Config.toml

edges.note: Client and derived types are generated by bal persist
TargetType typedesc parameters

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-persist master (1.7.1), persist.sql 1.7.4, ballerina.io persist-model and persist-client-api pages, and a generated client in persist-tools tests. The `whereClause`/`orderByClause`/`limitClause`/`groupByClause` parameters are confirmed only in generated SQL clients, not in the learn docs; their availability for other data stores was not confirmed. Data store selection (`--datastore`) is a CLI concern for tool.bal_persist.

nodes.title: ballerinax/postgresql
nodes.summary: The PostgreSQL connector: a `postgresql:Client` implementing the `sql:Client` API, PostgreSQL connection options and SSL, PostgreSQL-specific typed values and OUT parameters (JSON, UUID, network, geometric, interval, range types), and a `postgresql:CdcListener` based on logical replication.

must_cover.text: Add the PostgreSQL JDBC driver by importing `ballerinax/postgresql.driver as _;`, or pin a version in `Ballerina.toml` with `[[platform.java17.dependency]]` `groupId = "org.postgresql"`, `artifactId = "postgresql"`

Create a `postgresql:Client` with positional arguments `new ("localhost", "postgres", "postgres", "postgres", 5432)` (host, username, password, database, port) or named arguments such as `new (username = "postgres", password = "postgres", database = "test")`, noting the parameter is `username` (default `"postgres"`) and the default port is 5432

Configure `postgresql:Options` such as `connectTimeout`, `socketTimeout`, `loginTimeout`, `rowFetchSize`, `currentSchema`, `preparedStatementThreshold`, `cancelSignalTimeout`, `keepAliveTcpProbe` and `binaryTransfer`

Connect over SSL with `ssl: {mode: postgresql:REQUIRE, rootcert: "...", key: ...}` in `postgresql:Options`, choosing a mode from `PREFER`, `REQUIRE`, `DISABLE`, `ALLOW`, `VERIFY_CA`, `VERIFY_FULL` and giving the client key either as a `.p12` `crypto:KeyStore` or as a `postgresql:CertKey {certFile, keyFile, keyPassword}`
Pass `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}` or a shared `sql:ConnectionPool` record to `postgresql:Client`, or omit it to use the global pool
Use the `sql:Client` remote methods on `postgresql:Client` (`query`, `queryRow`, `execute`, `batchExecute`, `call`) with `sql:ParameterizedQuery` templates

Insert PostgreSQL `JSON`, `JSONB` and `UUID` columns with `postgresql:JsonValue`, `postgresql:JsonBinaryValue` and `postgresql:UuidValue` (e.g. `postgresql:JsonBinaryValue doc = new ({"a": 1});`) inside a parameterized query

Pass network and geometric types with `postgresql:InetValue`, `postgresql:CidrValue`, `postgresql:MacAddrValue`, and `postgresql:PointValue`, `postgresql:LineSegmentValue`, `postgresql:BoxValue`, `postgresql:CircleValue`, `postgresql:PolygonValue`, using records such as `postgresql:Point {x, y}` or string literals as values

Pass interval and range types with `postgresql:IntervalValue` (from a `postgresql:Interval {years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds}` record) and range values such as `postgresql:IntegerRangeValue`, `postgresql:NumericRangeValue`, `postgresql:TsRangeValue` and `postgresql:DateRangeValue`

Call PostgreSQL functions and procedures that return PostgreSQL-specific types using OUT parameters such as `postgresql:JsonOutParameter`, `postgresql:UuidOutParameter`, `postgresql:IntervalOutParameter` and `postgresql:InetOutParameter`, reading them with `get()`

Enable logical replication (`wal_level = logical`) and configure a `postgresql:CdcListener` with `database: {username, password, databaseName, includedSchemas, includedTables, replicationConfig: {pluginName: postgresql:PGOUTPUT, slotName}, publicationConfig: {publicationName, publicationAutocreateMode: postgresql:FILTERED}}`

out_of_scope: Generic query/execute/call semantics and the common sql:TypedValue/OutParameter types (lib.sql)
CDC service handlers, options and offset storage (lib.cdc)
Using PostgreSQL through generated persist clients (lib.persist)

sources.note: Client init, Options, SSLMode, SecureSocket, CertKey

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-postgresql master (1.19.1). The README lists SSL modes as `postgresql:PREFERRED`/`REQUIRED`, but the source enum is `PREFER`, `REQUIRE`, `DISABLE`, `ALLOW`, `VERIFY_CA`, `VERIFY_FULL`; items follow the source. The README's CDC example sets `pluginName`, `slotName` and `publicationName` at the top of `database`; these are @deprecated in favour of `replicationConfig`/`publicationConfig`, so items use the new form. How PostgreSQL-specific columns map back on `query` was not confirmed and is not claimed.

nodes.title: ballerina/protobuf
nodes.summary: The protobuf library provides Ballerina representations of the protobuf well-known types (wrappers, Any, Empty, Timestamp, Duration, Struct) and the descriptor annotation used by generated gRPC stubs.

must_cover.text: Recognise `@protobuf:Descriptor {value: <DESC_CONSTANT>}` on message record types in generated `*_pb.bal` stubs, which links each record to its protobuf message descriptor

Use the context records from `ballerina/protobuf.types.wrappers` such as `wrappers:ContextString` and `wrappers:ContextInt` (fields `content` and `headers`) to send and receive gRPC headers alongside a scalar message

Pack a record or scalar into the protobuf `Any` type with `'any:pack(value)` (giving an `'any:Any` with `typeUrl` and `value`) and recover it with `'any:unpack(anyValue, TargetType)` from `ballerina/protobuf.types.'any`, handling `'any:TypeMismatchError`

Map protobuf well-known types to Ballerina values: `google.protobuf.Timestamp` to `time:Utc`, `Duration` to `time:Seconds`, `Struct` to `map<anydata>`, `Empty` to `()`, and wrapper types to `int`, `float`, `string`, `boolean` and `byte[]`

sources.note: 3. Protocol buffers to Ballerina data mapping

must_cover.text: Use the typed context and stream records for well-known types, such as `timestamp:ContextTimestamp`, `struct:ContextStruct`, `empty:ContextNil` and `'any:ContextAnyStream`, when an RPC needs headers or streams of those types

out_of_scope: gRPC services and clients (lib.grpc)
Generating stubs from .proto files (tool.bal_grpc)

nodes.title: ballerinax/rabbitmq
nodes.summary: RabbitMQ (AMQP 0-9-1) connector: a `rabbitmq:Client` to declare queues and exchanges, publish and pull messages, and a `rabbitmq:Listener` whose consumer services receive messages through `onMessage`/`onRequest` with data binding, acknowledgements and transactions.

must_cover.text: Create a `rabbitmq:Client` with `check new (rabbitmq:DEFAULT_HOST, rabbitmq:DEFAULT_PORT)` or a custom host and port, optionally passing `rabbitmq:ConnectionConfiguration` fields such as `username`, `password`, `virtualHost`, `connectionTimeout` and `heartbeat`, and close it with `close()`

Declare messaging entities with `queueDeclare(name, {durable, exclusive, autoDelete})`, `queueAutoGenerate()`, `exchangeDeclare(name, rabbitmq:DIRECT_EXCHANGE)` (or `FANOUT_EXCHANGE`, `TOPIC_EXCHANGE`) and bind them with `queueBind(queueName, exchangeName, bindingKey)`
Remove entities with `queueDelete(queueName, ifUnused, ifEmpty)` and `exchangeDelete(name)`, and empty a queue with `queuePurge(queueName)`

Publish with `client->publishMessage({content: newOrder, routingKey: "OrderQueue"})`, where `content` is any `anydata`, optionally setting `exchange` and `properties: rabbitmq:BasicProperties` (`replyTo`, `correlationId`, `contentType`, `headers`)

Pull a single message with `client->consumePayload("OrderQueue")` bound to a type such as `Order`, or with `consumeMessage(queueName, autoAck)` bound to a `rabbitmq:AnydataMessage` subtype, and acknowledge it via the client's `basicAck`/`basicNack`

Attach a consumer service to a `rabbitmq:Listener`, naming the queue either as the service name (`service "OrderQueue" on new rabbitmq:Listener(...)`) or with `@rabbitmq:ServiceConfig {queueName: "OrderQueue"}`, and handle deliveries in `remote function onMessage(Order 'order)`

Bind `onMessage` parameters either to the payload type directly or to a message record such as `record {| *rabbitmq:AnydataMessage; string content; |}` or `rabbitmq:BytesMessage` to also read `routingKey`, `exchange`, `deliveryTag` and `properties`
Reply to request messages by implementing `remote function onRequest(rabbitmq:AnydataMessage message) returns string`, whose return value is sent back to the message's `replyTo` queue

Use client acknowledgement by setting `autoAck: false` in `@rabbitmq:ServiceConfig`, adding a `rabbitmq:Caller caller` parameter to `onMessage`, and calling `caller->basicAck()` or `caller->basicNack(multiple, requeue)`

Validate bound payloads with `@constraint` annotations on the record and handle failures in `remote function onError(rabbitmq:AnydataMessage message, rabbitmq:Error err)` by checking for `rabbitmq:PayloadValidationError` (also returned by `consumePayload` on the client)
Make publishing or acknowledging transactional by calling `publishMessage` or `caller->basicAck()` inside a `transaction { ... check commit; }` block
Limit unacknowledged deliveries per consumer by passing `rabbitmq:QosSettings` (`prefetchCount`, `prefetchSize`, `global`) as the third argument when creating a `rabbitmq:Listener`
Secure client and listener connections with TLS by passing `secureSocket = {cert: "path/public.crt"}` (or a `crypto:TrustStore` and optional `key`) and the TLS port such as 5671
Authenticate with username and password by passing `auth = {username: "alice", password: "alice@123"}` (a `rabbitmq:Credentials` value) when creating the client or listener

out_of_scope: General listener and service declaration semantics (concept.services_listeners)
Transaction statement semantics, commit and rollback handlers (concept.transactions)
Defining constraint annotations (lib.constraint)
Messaging patterns such as request-reply and competing consumers in general (topic.integration_patterns)
nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-rabbitmq master (3.6.1, same as latest on Central). README's negative-ack snippet omits the `caller` parameter; the item follows the Caller API (`basicNack(boolean multiple = false, boolean requeue = true)`).

nodes.title: ballerina/random
nodes.summary: The `random` module generates pseudo-random numbers with a uniform distribution: a `float` between 0.0 and 1.0 with `random:createDecimal` and an `int` in a half-open range with `random:createIntInRange`.

must_cover.text: Generate a pseudo-random `float` between 0.0 and 1.0 with `random:createDecimal()` (despite its name it returns a `float`)
Generate a pseudo-random `int` with `random:createIntInRange(startRange, endRange)`, where the start is inclusive and the end exclusive, e.g. `check random:createIntInRange(1, 100)`
Handle the `random:Error` that `random:createIntInRange` returns when `endRange` is not greater than `startRange`
Fill a fixed-length `byte[16]` with random values by casting `random:createIntInRange(0, 255)` results with `<byte>`, as done for AES keys and IVs in the crypto example
Pick a random element of an array with `items[check random:createIntInRange(0, items.length())]`, or scale `random:createDecimal()` to a custom `float` range
Explain that the generator is a seeded linear congruential generator and is not cryptographically secure, so it should not be used for security-sensitive secrets

sources.note: Doc comment: the generated number is not cryptographically secured

out_of_scope: Cryptographic hashing and encryption (lib.crypto)
Generating random UUIDs (lib.uuid)

nodes.title: ballerinax/redis
nodes.summary: The Redis connector: a `redis:Client` for standalone or cluster Redis servers with remote methods for strings, counters, lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes and key management, usable as a database or cache.

must_cover.text: Create a `redis:Client` with `check new (connection = {host: "localhost", port: 6379})` or a URI such as `connection = "redis://localhost:6379"`, optionally giving `username`, `password` and `options: {database, clientName, connectionTimeout}` in `redis:ConnectionParams`
Enable `connectionPooling: true` or `isClusterConnection: true` in `redis:ConnectionConfig`, and configure TLS with `secureSocket: {cert, key, verifyMode: redis:FULL, startTls}`
Store and read string values with `redis->set("key", "value")`, `redis->get("key")` (which returns `string?`, nil when the key is missing), `setNx`, `mSet` with a map and `mGet`
Cache values with a time-to-live using `redis->setEx(key, value, seconds)`, `expire(key, seconds)`, `ttl(key)` and `persist(key)`
Maintain counters atomically with `incr`, `incrBy`, `decr`, `decrBy` and `incrByFloat` (e.g. for rate limiting)
Use Redis lists with `lPush(key, values)`, `rPush`, `lPop`, `rPop`, `lRange(key, 0, -1)`, `lLen` and the blocking `bLPop(timeout, keys)`
Use Redis sets with `sAdd(key, members)`, `sMembers`, `sIsMember`, `sRem`, `sInter` and `sUnion`
Use sorted sets with `zAdd(key, {"alice": 10.0})` (a member-to-score map), `zRange`, `zRangeByScore`, `zScore`, `zRank` and `zIncrBy`, e.g. for leaderboards
Store objects as hashes with `hSet(key, field, value)`, `hMSet(key, map)`, `hGet`, `hGetAll` (returns `map<any>`), `hDel`, `hExists` and `hIncrBy`
Manage keys with `del([keys])`, `exists([keys])`, `keys(pattern)`, `rename` and `redisType`, and check connectivity with `ping()`
Handle `redis:Error` returned by every operation and close the connection with `check redis.close()`
Implement cache-aside lookups, user session storage and API rate limiting on top of the Redis client

out_of_scope: In-process caching (lib.cache)
Redis as a persist data store via ballerinax/persist.redis (lib.persist)
nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerinax-redis master (3.5.0). The README shows `string value = check redis->get("key");`, but `get` returns `string|Error?`; the item states the nilable result. `set` returns `string|Error` (the server reply).

nodes.title: ballerina/soap
nodes.summary: The SOAP library provides SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 clients (`soap11:Client`, `soap12:Client`) that send XML envelopes over HTTP and apply WS-Security policies to requests and responses.

must_cover.text: Create a SOAP client by importing `ballerina/soap.soap11` or `ballerina/soap.soap12` and calling `check new ("http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx?WSDL")` for `soap11:Client` or `soap12:Client`

Build the request envelope as an `xml` template with interpolated values and call `sendReceive(envelope, "http://tempuri.org/Add")` to get the response `xml`, where the SOAP action is mandatory for SOAP 1.1 and optional for SOAP 1.2
Fire and forget with `sendOnly(envelope, action)`, and use `sendRobust(envelope, action)` when only a SOAP fault should be reported back as an error
Extract values from the response envelope with XML navigation, e.g. declaring `xmlns "http://tempuri.org/" as quer;` and reading `response/**/<quer:AddResult>/*`
Send SOAP attachments by passing `mime:Entity[]` instead of `xml` as the body, and add transport headers with the `headers` map argument
Configure the underlying HTTP client through `httpConfig` in the client config, e.g. `httpConfig: {secureSocket: {cert: "..."}}` for TLS

Apply WS-Security to requests with `outboundSecurity`: a username token `{username, password, passwordType: soap:TEXT}`, timestamp token, X.509 token, symmetric binding, or asymmetric binding with `signatureConfig {keystore, privateKeyAlias, privateKeyPassword}` and `encryptionConfig {keystore, publicKeyAlias}` (single policy or an array)
Verify and decrypt secured responses with `inboundSecurity: {signatureKeystore, decryptKeystore}` using `crypto:KeyStore` values

Handle `soap:Error` results, including SOAP faults as `soap:Soap11FaultError`/`soap:Soap12FaultError` (union `soap:SoapFaultError`) and HTTP-level failures as `soap:HttpApplicationError` or `soap:TransportError`

out_of_scope: Generating typed clients from WSDL (tool.bal_wsdl)
XML language features in depth (concept.xml)
nodes.notes: The README's username-token example also lists a `TRANSPORT_BINDING` policy constant without a module prefix; its exact qualified name was not confirmed, so it is not named in items.

nodes.title: ballerina/sql
nodes.summary: The `sql` module defines the common `sql:Client` API shared by all relational database connectors: parameterized queries built from raw templates, streaming queries with record binding, execute/batch/stored-procedure calls, typed parameter values, connection pooling and a structured error hierarchy.

must_cover.text: Build `sql:ParameterizedQuery` values with backtick templates such as `` `SELECT * FROM students WHERE id < ${id} AND age > ${age}` ``, knowing each `${}` insertion becomes a bound query parameter (not string concatenation), which prevents SQL injection

Compose dynamic queries with `sql:queryConcat(q1, q2, ...)` and expand an array into an `IN (...)` list with `sql:arrayFlattenQuery(ids)`, e.g. `sql:queryConcat(`SELECT * FROM DataTable WHERE id IN (`, sql:arrayFlattenQuery(ids), `)`)`

Explain that only values can be parameterized in a `sql:ParameterizedQuery`; table or column names cannot, so dynamic identifiers must be validated (e.g. against a regular expression) before being embedded with string interpolation

Pass parameters as plain Ballerina values (`string`, `int`, `float`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `byte[]`, `xml`, `time:Date`/`time:Civil`/`time:Utc`, typed arrays) or as `sql:TypedValue` subtypes such as `sql:VarcharValue`, `sql:IntegerValue`, `sql:DecimalValue`, `sql:DateValue` and `sql:TimestampValue` (e.g. `sql:VarcharValue name = new ("James");`) when the exact SQL type must be specified

Run `SELECT` statements with `dbClient->query(query)`, binding the result to `stream<Student, sql:Error?>` via the inferred `rowType` typedesc, and consume it with a query expression, e.g. `return from Album album in albumStream select album;`

Explain how result columns map to record fields: column names match field names case-insensitively, an open record receives extra columns, a closed record returns an error for unmapped columns, and `stream<record {}, sql:Error?>` can be used without a predefined type
Map a database column to a differently named record field with the `@sql:Column {name: "first_name"}` annotation on the field
Group the columns of a joined table into a nested record field (e.g. a `Teachers teachers` field inside `Students`), optionally renaming it with `@sql:Column`

Fetch a single row with `dbClient->queryRow(query)` into a record, or a single scalar such as `int count = check dbClient->queryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students`);`, and handle `sql:NoRowsError` when no row matches (e.g. return `http:NOT_FOUND`)

Release query resources by fully consuming the result stream or calling `check resultStream.close()` when stopping early, knowing the stream is lazily loaded from the database and can be iterated only once

Run DDL and DML (`CREATE TABLE`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`) with `dbClient->execute(query)` and read the returned `sql:ExecutionResult` fields `affectedRowCount` and `lastInsertId` (the auto-generated key)

Insert many rows in one round trip with `dbClient->batchExecute(queries)`, building the `sql:ParameterizedQuery[]` with a query expression, and read the `sql:ExecutionResult[]` (including the `sql:SUCCESS_NO_INFO` and `sql:EXECUTION_FAILED` counts)

Call stored procedures with `dbClient->call(`{CALL get_sales_order(${filterDate}, ${total})}`, [Order])`, read result sets from `sql:ProcedureCallResult.queryResult` (cast to `stream<Order, error?>`), move to further result sets with `getNextQueryResult()`, and always call `result.close()`

Use `sql:IntegerOutParameter`, `sql:VarcharOutParameter` and other `sql:*OutParameter` types, `sql:InOutParameter` and `sql:CursorOutParameter` in call queries and read them with `get()` (e.g. `int total = check totalOut.get();`), including the function-call form `` `{${retVal} = call myFunc(${param})}` ``

Choose between the global shared pool (no `connectionPool` argument), a client-owned pool (inline `connectionPool = {maxOpenConnections: 5}`) and a pool shared by several clients (reusing one `sql:ConnectionPool` record)

Tune `sql:ConnectionPool` fields such as `maxOpenConnections`, `minIdleConnections`, `maxConnectionLifeTime`, `connectionTimeout`, `idleTimeout` and `transactionIsolation` (`sql:TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED`...), and set the global pool defaults in `Config.toml` under `[ballerina.sql]`

Run several `execute` calls atomically inside a `transaction` block, calling `check commit;` on success or `rollback;` when a check fails (e.g. `affectedRowCount == 0`), and handle failures in `on fail`

Handle the `sql:Error` hierarchy: `sql:DatabaseError` (detail `errorCode`, `sqlState`), `sql:BatchExecuteError` (detail `executionResults`), `sql:NoRowsError`, and `sql:ApplicationError` with its `sql:DataError` subtypes (`TypeMismatchError`, `ConversionError`, `FieldMismatchError`, `UnsupportedTypeError`), e.g. `if e is sql:DatabaseError && e.detail().errorCode == 3819`

Create one database client for the application lifetime (e.g. a `private final mysql:Client db` field initialized in a service `init`) and close it only at shutdown with `check dbClient.close()`, which also closes its unshared pool
Write database-agnostic code against the `sql:Client` object type, which every connector client (`mysql:Client`, `postgresql:Client`, `jdbc:Client`...) includes with `*sql:Client`

out_of_scope: Database-specific client construction, options, SSL and custom types (lib.mysql, lib.postgresql, lib.mssql, lib.oracledb, lib.java.jdbc)
ORM-style access through generated clients (lib.persist)
Transaction statement semantics in general (concept.transactions)
Stream and query-expression semantics (concept.streams, concept.query_expressions)
Pool metrics exported through observability (topic.observability)

sources.note: SQL library specification (pool configurables, stream closing, error hierarchy)

edges.note: Raw templates (ParameterizedQuery includes object:RawTemplate)
rowType/returnType are inferred typedesc parameters

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-sql master (1.19.1). `sql:ArrayValue` is deprecated (replaced by plain typed arrays) and omitted. `sql:SchemaClient` (listTables/getTableInfo...) exists only as an abstract type here and no connector README documents a concrete implementation, so it is left out.

nodes.title: ballerina/task
nodes.summary: The `task` module schedules `task:Job` objects to run once at a given time or repeatedly at an interval, manages scheduled jobs (pause, resume, unschedule), and offers a `task:Listener` that runs task services on a trigger with retries and multi-node warm-backup coordination.

must_cover.text: Define a job as a class that includes `*task:Job` and implements `public function execute()`, keeping any state the job needs in its fields

Run a job once at a given time with `task:scheduleOneTimeJob(new Job(), triggerTime)`, where the trigger time is a `time:Civil` (e.g. from `time:utcToCivil(time:utcAddSeconds(time:utcNow(), 3))`), getting back a `task:JobId`

Run a job repeatedly with `task:scheduleJobRecurByFrequency(job, interval)`, where `interval` is in seconds, optionally limiting it with `maxCount` (`-1` runs forever) and a `startTime`/`endTime` given as `time:Civil`

Control failure and overlap handling with a `task:TaskPolicy` (`errorPolicy` of `task:LOG_AND_TERMINATE`, `LOG_AND_CONTINUE`, `TERMINATE` or `CONTINUE`; `waitingPolicy` of `task:WAIT`, `IGNORE` or `LOG_AND_IGNORE`)

Manage scheduled jobs with `task:pauseJob(id)`, `task:resumeJob(id)`, `task:unscheduleJob(id)`, `task:pauseAllJobs()`, `task:resumeAllJobs()` and `task:getRunningJobs()`, which returns the `task:JobId[]` of active jobs
Keep a `main`-based program alive while scheduled jobs run (e.g. with `runtime:sleep`) and stop recurring jobs with `task:unscheduleJob` when done
Size the scheduler's thread pool with `task:configureWorkerPool(workerCount, waitingTime)` or the `globalSchedulerWorkerCount` and `globalSchedulerWaitingTime` configurables

Run scheduled work as a service by declaring `listener task:Listener taskListener = new (trigger = {interval: 2, maxCount: 5});` and attaching `service "job-1" on taskListener` with an `isolated function execute() returns error?` method

Retry failing listener job executions with the trigger's `retryConfig` (`task:RetryConfiguration` with `maxAttempts`, `retryInterval`, `backoffStrategy` of `task:FIXED` or `task:EXPONENTIAL`, and optional `maxInterval`)

Coordinate a task across nodes for high availability with the listener's `warmBackupConfig` (`databaseConfig` as a `task:MysqlConfig` or `task:PostgresqlConfig`, a unique `taskId` per node, a shared `groupId`, `livenessCheckInterval` and `heartbeatFrequency`), so only the active node runs the job

Handle `task:Error`, returned for example when scheduling with a non-positive `maxCount` or a trigger time that is not in the future, with `check`, knowing that a `time:Civil` without `utcOffset` is treated as UTC

out_of_scope: Creating and converting `time:Civil` and `time:Utc` values (lib.time)
Sleeping with `runtime:sleep` (lib.lang.runtime)
Database configuration for MySQL/PostgreSQL in general (lib.mysql, lib.postgresql)

nodes.title: ballerina/tcp
nodes.summary: The TCP library provides a connection-oriented `tcp:Client` for sending and receiving bytes and a `tcp:Listener` whose service returns a `tcp:ConnectionService` per client connection, with optional TLS.

must_cover.text: Connect with `tcp:Client socketClient = check new ("localhost", 9090)`, send data with `writeBytes("Hello".toBytes())`, read the reply as `readonly & byte[]` with `readBytes()`, convert with `string:fromBytes()`, and `close()` the client

Accept connections with `service on new tcp:Listener(9090)` implementing `remote function onConnect(tcp:Caller caller) returns tcp:ConnectionService` and reading connection details such as `caller.remotePort`

Implement a `service class` including `*tcp:ConnectionService` with `remote function onBytes(readonly & byte[] data)` that echoes by returning `byte[]` or writes with `caller->writeBytes(data)`, plus `onError(tcp:Error err)` and `onClose()`
Secure TCP with `secureSocket`: `key: {certFile, keyFile}` (a `tcp:ListenerSecureSocket`) on the listener and `cert` on the client
Configure the client with `tcp:ClientConfiguration` fields such as `timeout` and `writeTimeout` (seconds) and handle `tcp:Error` from reads and writes

out_of_scope: Connectionless datagrams (lib.udp)
Higher-level protocols over TCP such as HTTP (lib.http)

edges.note: Connection-oriented vs connectionless socket libraries with the same listener/caller style

nodes.title: ballerina/test
nodes.summary: The `test` module (Testerina) provides the annotations and functions for writing Ballerina tests: `@test:Config` test functions with groups, dependencies, data providers and before/after hooks, suite/group/each-level setup and teardown, assertions, and function and object mocking.

must_cover.text: Write a test by importing `ballerina/test` and annotating a function with `@test:Config` in a file under the module's `tests` directory, where module-level functions and variables are visible to the test

Assert values with `test:assertEquals(actual, expected, msg = "...")` and `test:assertNotEquals`, which compare by value (including `json`, records and tuples), and read the expected/actual diff printed on failure
Assert conditions with `test:assertTrue` and `test:assertFalse`, and fail a test explicitly with `test:assertFail(msg = "...")`, e.g. when an expected error is not returned
Check reference identity with `test:assertExactEquals` and `test:assertNotExactEquals`, e.g. that two variables refer to the same object
Declare a test function `returns error?` and use `check` inside it, so an unexpected error fails the test
Disable a test with `@test:Config {enable: false}` and tag tests with `groups: ["g1", "g2"]` so they can be selected or excluded by group
Guarantee execution order with `dependsOn: [testFunction1]`, which runs the listed test functions before the annotated one
Run set-up and tear-down code around a single test with the `before` and `after` fields of `@test:Config`, which take function references
Run a function before or after every test in the module with `@test:BeforeEach` and `@test:AfterEach`
Run one-time suite set-up and clean-up with `@test:BeforeSuite` and `@test:AfterSuite` (with `alwaysRun: true` to run even if dependent functions fail)
Run code before or after the tests of specific groups with `@test:BeforeGroups {value: ["g1"]}` and `@test:AfterGroups {value: ["g1"], alwaysRun: true}`
Write a data-driven test with `dataProvider: dataGen`, where the provider returns an array of argument arrays (e.g. `string[][]`) and the test function takes one parameter per value
Use a map-based data provider returning `map<[int, int, string]>|error`, whose keys name each data set case

Mock a function by declaring `@test:Mock {functionName: "intAdd"} test:MockFunction intAddMockFn = new ();` and stubbing it with `test:when(intAddMockFn).thenReturn(20)` or `.withArguments(0, 0).thenReturn(-1)`

Replace a function, including an imported one such as `io:println` (`@test:Mock {moduleName: "ballerina/io", functionName: "println"}`), with a same-signature function via `test:when(mockFn).call("mockPrint")`, and restore it with `callOriginal()`

Replace a function at compile time by annotating a substitute function with `@test:Mock {functionName: "initializeClient"}`, e.g. to return `test:mock(http:Client)` for a `final` client that object mocking cannot reassign
Substitute an object such as an `http:Client` with a test double by assigning `test:mock(http:Client, new MockHttpClient())`, where the mock client class implements only the methods the code calls

Stub object methods with `test:prepare(mockObj).when("get")` followed by `thenReturn(value)`, `withArguments(...).thenReturn(value)`, `thenReturnSequence(v1, v2)` or `doNothing()`, and stub a public field with `getMember("id").thenReturn(value)`

Stub client resource methods with `test:prepare(mockObj).whenResource("employee/:id").onMethod("get")`, optionally narrowed with `withPathParameters({id: "emp014"})` and `withArguments(...)`, then `thenReturn`, `thenReturnSequence` or `doNothing`

Keep a test out of parallel execution with `@test:Config {serialExecution: true}`, and make tests eligible for parallel runs by keeping test, data provider and hook functions `isolated` with `readonly` parameters

out_of_scope: Running tests with `bal test`, selecting groups or tests on the CLI, code coverage and test reports (tool.bal_test)
Test-only Config.toml values and test-scoped dependencies in Ballerina.toml (tool.config_toml, tool.ballerina_toml)
HTTP client and service APIs used inside tests (lib.http)

edges.note: bal test runs the tests written with this module

nodes.notes: The current testerina-core source also has `minPassRate` and `runs` fields on `test:TestConfig` (described as evaluation settings); they are not documented on ballerina.io/learn or in BBEs yet, so they are left out.

nodes.title: ballerina/time
nodes.summary: The `time` module represents instants as `time:Utc` (seconds from the Unix epoch with nanosecond precision) and localized date-times as `time:Civil`, with conversions to and from RFC 3339 and RFC 5322 strings, time zones, durations and monotonic time.

must_cover.text: Get the current instant with `time:utcNow()`, a `time:Utc` tuple `[int, decimal]` of whole seconds and the fractional second since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, optionally with a `precision` argument (e.g. `3` for milliseconds)
Parse an RFC 3339 timestamp with `time:utcFromString("2007-12-03T10:15:30.120Z")` (returns `time:Utc|time:Error`) and format a `time:Utc` with `time:utcToString`
Shift an instant with `time:utcAddSeconds(utc, seconds)` and measure the gap between two instants with `time:utcDiffSeconds(utc1, utc2)`, which returns `time:Seconds` (a `decimal`)
Measure elapsed time with `time:monotonicNow()`, which returns `decimal` seconds from an unspecified epoch and always increases

Build and read a `time:Civil` record with `year`, `month`, `day`, `hour`, `minute`, `second` (`decimal`), optional `utcOffset` (`time:ZoneOffset` with `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`), `timeAbbrev`, `which` and `dayOfWeek`
Convert between instants and civil times with `time:utcToCivil(utc)` and `time:utcFromCivil(civil)`, knowing that `utcFromCivil` needs the `utcOffset` field and returns `time:Utc|time:Error`
Parse an RFC 3339 string with an offset and optional zone, e.g. `"2021-04-12T23:20:50.520+05:30[Asia/Colombo]"`, with `time:civilFromString`, and format a `time:Civil` with `time:civilToString`

Produce and parse RFC 5322 (email header) date strings with `time:utcToEmailString(utc, "Z")`, `time:civilFromEmailString` and `time:civilToEmailString(civil, time:PREFER_ZONE_OFFSET)` (`time:HeaderZoneHandling` also has `PREFER_TIME_ABBREV` and `ZONE_OFFSET_WITH_TIME_ABBREV_COMMENT`)

Look up a zone with `time:getZone("Asia/Tokyo")` (returns `time:Zone?`) or load the system zone with `time:loadSystemZone()` or `new time:TimeZone()`, then convert with the zone's `utcToCivil` and `utcFromCivil` methods

Add or subtract calendar amounts with `time:civilAddDuration(civil, duration)` using a `time:Duration` record (`years`, `months`, `weeks`, `days`, `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`; negative values subtract), or the same method on a `time:Zone`
Validate a `time:Date` with `time:dateValidate(date)` and get its weekday with `time:dayOfWeek(date)`, which returns a `time:DayOfWeek` such as `time:MONDAY`
Handle `time:Error` (and its subtype `time:FormatError`) returned when parsing malformed timestamps or converting incomplete civil values

out_of_scope: Pausing a strand with `runtime:sleep` (lib.lang.runtime)
Scheduling jobs at a `time:Civil` trigger time (lib.task)

nodes.title: ballerina/toml
nodes.summary: The `toml` module parses TOML strings and files into `map<json>` and writes a `map<json>` back as TOML lines or a TOML file, using a linear-time LL(1) parser.

must_cover.text: Parse TOML text into a `map<json>` with `toml:readString(tomlString)`
Parse a TOML file into a `map<json>` with `toml:readFile("config.toml")`
Read values from the parsed `map<json>`, where a TOML table such as `[database]` becomes a nested map, and convert it to a record with `cloneWithType`
Control date-time parsing with the included `toml:ReadConfig` parameter, e.g. `toml:readFile(path, parseOffsetDateTime = false)`; by default offset date-times are converted to `time:Utc`
Serialize a `map<json>` to TOML with `toml:writeString(structure)`, which returns the TOML content as a `string[]` of lines
Write a `map<json>` to a TOML file with `toml:writeFile(path, structure)`

Format TOML output through the included `toml:WriteConfig` parameter, setting `indentationPolicy` (default 2) and `allowDottedKeys` (default `true`, using dotted keys instead of standard tables where applicable)
Handle `toml:Error`, the union of `toml:ParsingError`, `toml:WritingError` and `toml:FileError` (which wraps `io:Error` or `file:Error`)

out_of_scope: Ballerina.toml and Config.toml project files (tool.ballerina_toml, tool.config_toml)
YAML handling (lib.data.yaml)

edges.note: included record parameters passed as named arguments

nodes.notes: Verified against module-ballerina-toml master 0.8.2 (= latest tag). There is no BBE for this module and the README is a two-line overview, so items rely on the public API source (toml.bal, types.bal, errors.bal). The module does not bind directly to record types; conversion to records goes through cloneWithType.

nodes.title: ballerina/udp
nodes.summary: The UDP library sends and receives datagrams with a connectionless `udp:Client`, a peer-bound `udp:ConnectClient`, and a `udp:Listener` service with `onDatagram`/`onBytes` callbacks.

must_cover.text: Send and receive datagrams with `udp:Client socketClient = check new;`, building a `udp:Datagram {remoteHost, remotePort, data}` for `sendDatagram()`, reading `readonly & udp:Datagram` with `receiveDatagram()`, and calling `close()`

Exchange data with a single peer using `udp:ConnectClient` created with `check new ("localhost", 9090)` and its `writeBytes()`/`readBytes()` methods, knowing large byte arrays are split across several datagrams

Handle incoming datagrams with `service on new udp:Listener(9090)` implementing `remote function onDatagram(readonly & udp:Datagram datagram)` (returning a `udp:Datagram` to reply) or `onBytes(readonly & byte[] data, udp:Caller caller)`, plus `onError(udp:Error err)`
Reply through a `udp:Caller` parameter with `caller->sendBytes(data)` or `caller->sendDatagram(datagram)` and read the peer from `caller.remoteHost`/`caller.remotePort`

Configure local binding and timeouts: `localHost` and `timeout` on `udp:ClientConfiguration`/`udp:ConnectClientConfiguration`, and `localHost`, `remoteHost`, `remotePort` on `udp:ListenerConfiguration` to restrict a listener to one peer

out_of_scope: Connection-oriented sockets (lib.tcp)
nodes.notes: Configuration fields confirmed against udp master sources (connect_client.bal, connectionless_client.bal, listener.bal).

nodes.title: ballerina/url
nodes.summary: The `url` module percent-encodes and decodes strings for use in URLs with a given character set through `url:encode` and `url:decode`.

must_cover.text: Percent-encode a URL component with `url:encode(value, "UTF-8")`, e.g. turning `data=value` into `data%3Dvalue`; the function returns `string|url:Error`
Decode a percent-encoded string with `url:decode(value, "UTF-8")`, e.g. `http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A9090` back to `http://localhost:9090`
Explain that `url:encode` encodes a space as `%20` (not `+`) and `*` as `%2A`, and leaves `~` unencoded, so the output is safe in both paths and query strings

sources.note: Tests assert no space, *, + or %7E in encoded output

must_cover.text: Build a query string safely by encoding each parameter value with `url:encode` before concatenating it, e.g. `"/search?q=" + check url:encode(term, "UTF-8")`, for use with an HTTP client path

sources.note: Doc example encodes a value containing ?, = and &

must_cover.text: Handle the `url:Error` returned when the charset name is not supported (e.g. `url:encode(value, "abc")`) with `check` or an `is url:Error` test

out_of_scope: Query and path parameter binding in HTTP services and clients (lib.http)
Base64/Base16 encoding of byte arrays (lib.lang.array)

nodes.title: ballerina/uuid
nodes.summary: The `uuid` module generates RFC 4122 UUIDs of versions 1, 3, 4 and 5 as strings or `uuid:Uuid` records, and validates, inspects and converts UUIDs between string, byte and record forms.

must_cover.text: Generate a random (version 4) UUID string with `uuid:createType4AsString()` or its alias `uuid:createRandomUuid()`, e.g. as an ID for a new record
Generate a version 1 UUID, based on the MAC address and the current time, with `uuid:createType1AsString()` or `uuid:createType1AsRecord()`

Generate deterministic name-based UUIDs with `uuid:createType3AsString(namespace, name)` (MD5) or `uuid:createType5AsString(namespace, name)` (SHA-1), using a `uuid:NamespaceUUID` such as `uuid:NAME_SPACE_DNS`, `NAME_SPACE_URL`, `NAME_SPACE_OID` or `NAME_SPACE_X500`; these return `string|uuid:Error`

Generate UUIDs as `uuid:Uuid` records with the `createType1AsRecord`, `createType3AsRecord`, `createType4AsRecord` and `createType5AsRecord` functions and read the record fields `timeLow`, `timeMid`, `timeHiAndVersion`, `clockSeqHiAndReserved`, `clockSeqLo` and `node`
Get the nil UUID (all zeros) with `uuid:nilAsString()` or `uuid:nilAsRecord()`
Check whether a string is a valid UUID with `uuid:validate(s)`, which returns a `boolean`, e.g. to validate an ID path parameter
Detect the version of a UUID string with `uuid:getVersion(s)`, which returns a `uuid:Version` (`V1`, `V3`, `V4`, `V5`) or a `uuid:Error` for an invalid UUID
Convert UUIDs between forms with `uuid:toBytes(string|uuid:Uuid)`, `uuid:toString(byte[]|uuid:Uuid)` and `uuid:toRecord(string|byte[])`, handling the error returned for an invalid UUID

out_of_scope: Generating random numbers (lib.random)

nodes.title: ballerina/websocket
nodes.summary: The WebSocket library provides a `websocket:Listener` with an upgrade service that returns a `websocket:Service` for full-duplex messaging, and a synchronous `websocket:Client` for reading and writing text and binary messages.

must_cover.text: Write the upgrade service `service /chat on new websocket:Listener(9090)` with `resource function get .() returns websocket:Service` that returns a new `service class` including `*websocket:Service`, optionally taking an `http:Request`, query parameters or `@http:Header` values
Validate the handshake (e.g. the `Origin` header) in the upgrade resource and cancel it by returning an error or `websocket:UpgradeError` instead of a service

Handle incoming messages with `remote function onMessage(websocket:Caller caller, T data)` where `T` may be `string`, `byte[]`, `json`, `xml` or a record for data binding, and reply with `caller->writeMessage(...)`

Use the lower-level `onTextMessage(websocket:Caller, string)` and `onBinaryMessage(websocket:Caller, byte[])` remote methods with `writeTextMessage`/`writeBinaryMessage`, knowing they cannot be combined with `onMessage`

Implement connection lifecycle remote methods `onOpen(websocket:Caller)`, `onClose(websocket:Caller, int statusCode, string reason)`, `onError(websocket:Caller, error)` and `onIdleTimeout(websocket:Caller)` (with `idleTimeout` set in `@websocket:ServiceConfig`)
Handle control frames with `onPing`/`onPong` and `caller->pong(data)`, register a client-side `*websocket:PingPongService` through `pingPongHandler`, and close connections with `close()`

Use `websocket:Client` created with `check new ("ws://localhost:9090/chat")` to `writeMessage()` and `readMessage()` synchronously (binding the read to `string`, `json`, a record and so on), or `writeTextMessage`/`readTextMessage`/`writeBinaryMessage`/`readBinaryMessage`
Validate WebSocket payloads with `@constraint` annotations on the bound type, both in `onMessage` parameters and in `readMessage()` results on the client

Dispatch JSON messages to custom remote methods with `@websocket:ServiceConfig {dispatcherKey: "event"}` so `{"event": "heartbeat"}` goes to `onHeartbeat`, override names with `@websocket:DispatcherConfig {dispatcherValue: ...}`, and handle binding failures in `on<Name>Error`

Tune services with `@websocket:ServiceConfig` fields such as `subProtocols`, `idleTimeout`, `maxFrameSize` and `connectionClosureTimeout`, and enable or disable per-message compression with `webSocketCompressionEnabled`
Use `wss://` by configuring `secureSocket` on the listener (`key: {certFile, keyFile}`, `mutualSsl: {verifyClient: http:REQUIRE, cert}`) and on the client (`cert`, `key`)
Secure WebSocket upgrades with `@websocket:ServiceConfig {auth: [...]}` using `fileUserStoreConfig`, `ldapUserStoreConfig`, `jwtValidatorConfig` or `oauth2IntrospectionConfig` with `scopes`
Authenticate a `websocket:Client` with the `auth` config (Basic, bearer token, self-signed JWT, OAuth2 grant types) over `wss://`
Make clients resilient with `handShakeTimeout` and `retryConfig: {maxCount, interval}` for reconnecting

out_of_scope: HTTP request and header APIs used during the upgrade (lib.http)
AsyncAPI generation for WebSocket services (tool.bal_asyncapi)
