Use completion features: service templates for each available listener, `foreach` and `foreach i` snippets for iterables, `typeguard` for union-typed variables and `Fill Record required fields`, plus hover documentation and signature help
Try a running HTTP service from the editor with the **Try it** CodeLens, which opens a Swagger view where parameters are filled in and requests executed
Open a service with the **Visualize** CodeLens and use the HTTP API Designer to add resources with path, query and header parameters, a payload and response status codes

Build an expression-bodied transformation function such as `function transform(Person person, Course[] courses) returns Student => ...` in the Data Mapper, map fields visually, fix type mismatches in the expression editor and turn array mappings into query expressions with `where`, `let`, `limit`, `order by` and `join` clauses
Create and run Ballerina notebooks (`.balnotebook` files), executing cells with **Run** or `Shift` + `Enter`, viewing variables, and debugging after turning on `ballerina.enableNotebookDebug`

Configure the extension in `settings.json` with keys such as `ballerina.codeLens.all.enabled`, `ballerina.enableConfigurableEditor` (a form for configurable values when running), `ballerina.lowCodeMode`, `ballerina.enableSemanticHighlighting` and `ballerina.home` (with `ballerina.pluginDevMode`)

out_of_scope: The CLI commands the extension calls (tool.bal, tool.bal_test)
Writing transformation logic and query expressions (topic.data_mapping, concept.query_expressions)
HTTP service semantics (lib.http)

nodes.title: AI agents
nodes.summary: Building LLM-powered applications in Ballerina - typed direct LLM calls, natural expressions, tool-using agents exposed as chat services, MCP servers and clients, and retrieval-augmented generation over vector stores.

must_cover.text: Obtain an `ai:ModelProvider` either with `ai:getDefaultModelProvider()` (configured in `Config.toml` by the VS Code "Configure default WSO2 Model Provider" command) or from a provider package such as `check new openai:ModelProvider(apiKey, modelType = openai:GPT_4O)` with the key in a configurable variable
Call an LLM with `model->generate(`Tell me a joke about ${subject}!`)` and bind the answer either to `string` or directly to a record type such as `JokeResponse` declared on the left-hand side

Hold a multi-turn conversation by building an `ai:ChatMessage[]` of `ai:ChatUserMessage` values (`role: ai:USER`), calling `model->chat(messages)`, and pushing each returned `ai:ChatAssistantMessage` back onto the history

Use a natural expression `natural (model) { ... ${count} ... }` whose expected type (e.g. `Attraction[]|error`, with `#`-documented record fields) drives the JSON schema sent to the LLM, and know it is experimental and needs the `--experimental` flag
Expose functions as agent tools by marking them `isolated` and annotating them with `@ai:AgentTool`, guarding shared state such as an `isolated map<Task>` with `lock` and returning cloned values
Create an `ai:Agent` with `systemPrompt: {role: "...", instructions: string `...`}`, `tools: [addTask, listTasks]` and `model`, and drive it with `agent.run(userInput)` in a console loop

Group related tools in an isolated class that includes `*ai:BaseToolKit` and implements `getTools()` returning `ai:getToolConfigs([self.addTask, self.listTasks])`, pass an instance in `tools`, and bound the reasoning loop with `maxIter`
Turn connector operations into tools, e.g. `@ai:AgentTool` functions that call a `gmail:Client` or `calendar:Client` configured with OAuth2 refresh-token credentials from configurable variables
Give an agent the tools of a remote MCP server with `final ai:McpToolKit weatherMcpConn = check new ("http://localhost:9090/mcp");` passed in the agent's `tools`

Expose an agent as a chat service with `service /tasks on new ai:Listener(8080)` and `resource function post chat(@http:Payload ai:ChatReqMessage request) returns ai:ChatRespMessage|error` that calls `agent.run(request.message, request.sessionId)`

Control per-session conversation memory with `memory = check new ai:ShortTermMemory(check new ai:InMemoryShortTermMemoryStore(15))`, make an agent stateless with `memory = ()`, and separate users with `run(query, sessionId = "...")`

Write an MCP server with `listener mcp:Listener mcpListener = new (9090);` and `service mcp:Service /mcp on mcpListener`, where each documented `remote function` (e.g. `getCurrentWeather(string city) returns Weather|error`) becomes a tool

Take full control of tool listing and dispatch with `service mcp:AdvancedService` implementing `onListTools()` returning `mcp:ListToolsResult` and `onCallTool(mcp:CallToolParams params, mcp:Session? session)` returning `mcp:CallToolResult`

Ingest documents for RAG by loading them with `ai:TextDataLoader("./leave_policy.md")` and `loader.load()`, and calling `knowledgeBase.ingest(documents)` on an `ai:VectorKnowledgeBase(vectorStore, embeddingProvider)` backed by `ai:InMemoryVectorStore`

Answer a question with retrieved context by calling `knowledgeBase.retrieve(query, 10)`, collecting `queryMatch.chunk` values with a query expression, and passing `ai:augmentUserQuery(context, query)` to `modelProvider->chat(...)`

Persist embeddings in an external vector database by using `new pinecone:VectorStore(serviceUrl, apiKey)` from `ballerinax/ai.pinecone` as the knowledge base's `ai:VectorStore` with `ai:getDefaultEmbeddingProvider()`

out_of_scope: Full ai module API surface (lib.ai)
MCP protocol details and client API (lib.mcp)
Provider-specific options (lib.ai.openai, lib.ai.anthropic, lib.ai.azure, lib.ai.ollama)
nodes.notes: Natural expressions are experimental (Swan Lake Update 13+, `--experimental`). The `ai:Agent` constructor is shown both with a record argument (`check new ({...})`) and named arguments (`check new (systemPrompt = ..., ...)`) in the BBEs.

nodes.title: Best practices
nodes.summary: Writing idiomatic, maintainable Ballerina following the official style guide (formatting, naming, documentation), the language's error-handling and concurrency idioms, configurability, logging conventions and the rules enforced by the `bal scan` static analyzer.

must_cover.text: Format code per the style guide - four-space indentation, lines of at most 120 characters, a single space between keywords, types and identifiers, the opening brace on the same line, and no spaces inside `map<string>`, `string[]`, `string|int` or `string?`

Break long lines before an operator (e.g. `&& i == 1` on the next line) and after a separator such as a comma in a parameter list, indenting continuation lines by four spaces, and optionally moving `returns ...` to its own line

Name constants in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (`const MIN_AGE = 20;`), omit the type descriptor when the value alone determines it (`const TAX_RATE = 0.15d;`), and add one for readability on compound expressions (`const byte COMPLEX_VALUE = (50 * 2 + 100) % 256;`)

Write imports as `import ballerina/http;` sorted alphabetically by organization and then module name, keep top-level definitions unindented, and keep the listener inline with the service declaration (`service / on new http:Listener(9090) {`)

Write `if valid { ... } else if active { ... }` without parentheses around the condition and with `else` on the closing-brace line, and lay out `match` clauses one per line with a single space around `=>`
Format record and map literals as `{name: "john", age: 20}` on one line or with one block-indented field per line, keep tuples on one line, and split long array literals one member per line
Lay out a class with each field, type inclusion and method on its own line and the `init` method before all other methods, and give each record field (including the rest field) its own line

Document public constructs with Markdown doc comments - `# Description.`, an empty `#` line, then `# + param - Description` and `# + return - Description` - and document records with a comment above the type and above each field
Propagate errors with `check` from functions declared `returns error?` (or handle them with `if result is error`) instead of `checkpanic`, which terminates the program with a panic
Ignore a non-error return value explicitly with `_ = getX();`, and know that `_` cannot discard a value whose type includes `error`, so errors must be handled or propagated
Mark public functions, methods, classes and objects `isolated` so they can be called concurrently, keeping mutable module state in `isolated` variables accessed only inside `lock` blocks

Use `configurable` module variables for environment-specific values and secrets (`configurable string dbHost = "localhost";`, `configurable string password = ?;`) instead of hard-coded literals or constants
Model payloads with record types (closed `record {| ... |}` when the fields are exactly known) rather than working with raw `json`, for type safety, validation and tooling support
Use expression-bodied functions `function inc(int x) returns int => x + 1;`, `let` expressions and conditional expressions where a function or branch just computes a value

Use the `log` module rather than `io:println` for diagnostics (reserving `io:println` for CLI help or usage output), choosing `ERROR`, `WARN`, `INFO` or `DEBUG` by severity and never logging passwords, tokens or personal data
Remove unused function parameters and unused private class fields, and avoid self-assignments and conditions that always evaluate to `true` or `false`
Check code against these rules with `bal scan`, selecting rules with `--include-rules="ballerina:1"` / `--exclude-rules` and listing them with `--list-rules`

out_of_scope: Security-specific rules and practices (topic.security)
Log configuration and structured logging (topic.observability)
Formatter customization via Format.toml (tool.bal)

sources.note: Style guide - coding conventions (incl. logging conventions)

nodes.notes: The style guide is mostly formatting rules that the Ballerina formatter applies; idiom items come from the scan rules and BBEs. No separate official 'Ballerina idioms' page was found.

nodes.title: Connectors
nodes.summary: Using and building Ballerina connectors - importing ballerinax client packages from Ballerina Central, configuring their authentication from configurable values, combining them in SaaS integrations, and generating, testing and publishing a connector from an OpenAPI specification.

must_cover.text: Use a connector from Ballerina Central by importing it with an optional prefix, e.g. `import ballerinax/github;` or `import ballerinax/salesforce as sf;`, and explain that dependencies are resolved from the distribution and Ballerina Central repositories (cached locally)

Initialize a connector client with credentials from configurable variables, e.g. `configurable string githubAccessToken = ?;` and `github:Client github = check new ({auth: {token: githubAccessToken}});`
Configure an OAuth2 connector such as `gmail:Client` with `auth: {refreshToken, clientId, clientSecret, refreshUrl}` read from configurable variables so tokens are refreshed automatically
Point a connector at a tenant-specific endpoint with a `baseUrl` in its config, e.g. `sf:Client salesforce = check new ({baseUrl: salesforceBaseUrl, auth: {token: salesforceAccessToken}});`

Call connector operations both as resource methods (`gmailClient->/users/me/messages(q = "label:INBOX is:unread")`) and as remote methods (`calendarClient->getEvents(userEmail)`), binding results to the connector's record types

Consume paginated connector results returned as streams, e.g. `stream<github:User, github:Error?> collaborators = check github->getCollaborators(org, repo);` processed with `check collaborators.forEach(...)` or a query expression

Move records from a database to a SaaS application by querying a `mysql:Client` into `stream<ProductReceived, error?>`, collecting it with `check from ... select`, mapping each row and creating records through the `salesforce` connector

Query a SaaS backend and update what it returns, e.g. `sfdcClient->query(string `SELECT Id FROM PricebookEntry WHERE ...`)` returning `stream<record {}, error?>`, then `sfdcClient->update("PricebookEntry", id, updatedPrice)`

Combine connectors in a `main` program, e.g. build a summary from `github->search(...)` results and send it with an `email:SmtpClient` created as `new (host = smtpHost, username = smtpUsername, password = smtpPassword)`

Generate a client connector from an OpenAPI definition with `bal openapi -i docs/spec/openapi.yaml --mode client -o ballerina`, producing `client.bal`, `types.bal` and `utils.bal`, and choose method style with `--client-methods resource|remote`

Prepare a third-party OpenAPI definition before generation with `bal openapi flatten -i openapi.yaml -o docs/spec` and `bal openapi align -i flattened_openapi.yaml -o docs/spec`, recording further manual changes in `sanitations.md`
Test a generated connector with test functions under `ballerina/tests` that exercise its key operations, run with `bal test`

Publish a connector by setting `org`, `name`, `version` (and optional `license`, `authors`, `keywords`, `icon`, `repository`) in `Ballerina.toml`, documenting it in `ballerina/README.md`, and running `bal pack` and `bal push`

out_of_scope: Individual SaaS connector APIs (not modelled in this graph)
OpenAPI tool options in general (tool.bal_openapi)
Package publishing, versioning and deprecation (tool.central)
nodes.notes: Connector-specific operations (github, salesforce, gmail, calendar) come from the pre-built integration samples and BBEs; they are illustrations of the pattern, not a complete API reference.

nodes.title: Data mapping
nodes.summary: Transforming messages between formats and schemas in Ballerina - modelling payloads as records, writing expression-bodied mapping functions (as produced by the VS Code data mapper), reshaping collections with query expressions, and converting JSON, XML and CSV to and from typed values.

must_cover.text: Model source and target payloads as record types generated from sample JSON or XML (the VS Code "JSON as Record" / "XML as Record" tools), then tighten them, e.g. closed records `record {| ... |}` and fixed-length arrays such as `int[3] ssn`

Write a mapping as an expression-bodied function, e.g. `isolated function transform(HealthcareReservation r) returns HospitalReservation => let var ssn = r.ssn in {patient: {name: r.firstName + " " + r.lastName, ssn: string `${ssn[0]}-${ssn[1]}-${ssn[2]}`, ...}, ...};`

Build a transform function visually with the VS Code data mapper by connecting input record fields to output record fields, and explain that it generates an ordinary expression-bodied Ballerina function
Map nested arrays with a query expression inside a mapping constructor, e.g. `invoices: from var o in salesData.opportunities select {id: o.id, amount: o.amount, invoiceDate: o.closeDate}`
Rename or project fields with a mapping binding pattern in a query, e.g. `from var {carType, price, resultLink, vendor} in response.result select {carType, price, resultLink, vendor}`
Convert repeated XML elements into records with a query over XML navigation, e.g. `from xml item in response/<Response>/<Car> select {carType: (item/<CarType>).data(), price: (item/<Price>).data()}`

Aggregate data with `group by` and aggregate functions, e.g. `from var {itemName, quantity} in orders group by itemName select {itemName, quantity: sum(quantity)}`, and reduce a whole collection with `collect sum(totPrice)`
Combine and rank data sets with `join string country in countries on entry.country equals country`, `order by entry.deaths descending` and `limit n`

Convert JSON to a record type with `jsondata:parseAsType(jsonValue)`, `jsondata:parseString(str)`, `jsondata:parseBytes(bytes)` or `jsondata:parseStream(byteStream)`, with the target type inferred from the left-hand side

Project only the needed fields by converting JSON into a closed record (extra fields are dropped), and tune behaviour with `jsondata:Options` such as `allowDataProjection` and `enableConstraintValidation`
Map JSON keys that differ from field names with `@jsondata:Name {value: "..."}` on a record field, and produce JSON with `jsondata:toJson(value)` or `value.toJson()`
Convert an in-memory `json` value to a user-defined type with `j.cloneWithType(Coord)` (or with the type inferred), and narrow a single value with `value:ensureType`

sources.note: Convert to a user-defined type - cloneWithType

must_cover.text: Convert XML to records with `xmldata:parseAsType(xmlValue)` (or `parseString`), using `@xmldata:Namespace {prefix, uri}` for namespaces and `@xmldata:Attribute` for attributes
Convert XML to JSON by parsing it into a record with `xmldata:parseAsType` and calling `toJson()`, and go the other way with `xmldata:toXml(recordValue)` or `xmldata:fromJson(jsonValue)`
Parse CSV text into typed records with `csv:parseString(csvString)` into `Book[]`, projecting columns by targeting a closed record such as `BookMinimal`
Read and write CSV files as typed records with `io:fileReadCsv`, `io:fileWriteCsv`, `io:fileWriteCsvFromStream` and `io:fileReadCsvAsStream`

out_of_scope: Query expression semantics in general (concept.query_expressions)
Full data.jsondata, data.xmldata and data.csv APIs (lib.data.jsondata, lib.data.xmldata, lib.data.csv)
XSLT and EDI transformations (lib.xslt, lib.edi)
nodes.notes: The data mapper itself is a VS Code feature; items describe the code it generates as shown in the tutorial. `@jsondata:Name` is confirmed from json_api.bal (`NameConfig {value}`), not from a BBE.

nodes.title: Event-driven
nodes.summary: Building event-driven integrations in Ballerina by producing and consuming typed messages with Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, MQTT and JMS, receiving webhooks with WebSub, reacting to database changes with CDC, and bridging events to HTTP, WebSocket and SaaS endpoints.

must_cover.text: Accept events over HTTP and publish them to Kafka from a service that holds a `private final kafka:Producer` created in `init()`, calling `check self.orderProducer->send({topic: "order-topic", value: newOrder})` and returning `http:ACCEPTED`

Consume a topic with `listener kafka:Listener orderListener = new (kafka:DEFAULT_URL, {groupId: "...", topics: "order-topic"})` and a service whose `remote function onConsumerRecord(Order[] orders)` receives payloads already bound to a record type

Poll Kafka from a `kafka:Consumer` in a loop with `pollPayload(15)` for bound payloads, or `poll(15)` into a record that includes `*kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord` with a typed `value` when record metadata is needed
Commit offsets only after processing by setting `autoCommit: false` on the listener and calling `caller->commit()` from `onConsumerRecord(kafka:Caller caller, ...)`
Validate incoming messages declaratively by adding `@constraint:String {maxLength: 30, minLength: 1}` (or other constraints) to the message record type consumed by a Kafka or RabbitMQ service
Process a received batch with a query action such as `from Order 'order in orders where 'order.isValid do { log:printInfo(...); };`, quoting reserved words like `'order`
Publish to RabbitMQ with a `rabbitmq:Client` created from `rabbitmq:DEFAULT_HOST` and `rabbitmq:DEFAULT_PORT`, calling `publishMessage({content: newOrder, routingKey: "OrderQueue"})`
Consume a queue with `service "OrderQueue" on new rabbitmq:Listener(rabbitmq:DEFAULT_HOST, rabbitmq:DEFAULT_PORT)` and `remote function onMessage(Order 'order) returns error?`
Subscribe to a NATS subject with `service "orders.valid" on new nats:Listener(nats:DEFAULT_URL)` and a typed `onMessage` remote function

Subscribe to MQTT with `service on new mqtt:Listener(mqtt:DEFAULT_URL, "client-id", "mqtt/topic")` and convert `message.payload` bytes to a record with `string:fromBytes` and `value:fromJsonStringWithType`

Consume JMS messages with a `jms:Listener` configured with `initialContextFactory` and `providerUrl`, `@jms:ServiceConfig {queueName: "order-queue"}`, and an `onMessage(jms:Message message)` that type-tests for `jms:MapMessage`

Receive webhooks with a WebSub subscriber, `@websub:SubscriberServiceConfig {target: [hubUrl, topicUrl], secret: "..."}` on `service on new websub:Listener(9090)`, handling `remote function onEventNotification(websub:ContentDistributionMessage event)`

React to database changes with `listener mysql:CdcListener` (importing `ballerinax/mysql.cdc.driver as _`) and a service implementing `onRead`, `onCreate`, `onUpdate` or `onDelete` with a typed row record, e.g. raising a fraud alert for large transactions

Fan out events to browsers by publishing match events to Kafka from an HTTP resource and, per WebSocket connection, creating a `kafka:Consumer` with a unique `groupId` whose payloads are forwarded with `caller->writeMessage(...)` from `onOpen`

Update a SaaS system from a stream of events, e.g. an `isolated remote function onConsumerRecord(ProductPrice[] prices)` that destructures each record and calls a `salesforce:Client` to update the matching record

out_of_scope: Broker client configuration, security (SSL/SASL) and full APIs (lib.kafka, lib.rabbitmq, lib.nats, lib.mqtt, lib.java.jms)
Consumer error handling and acknowledgements for reliability (topic.resiliency)
WebSub hubs (lib.websubhub)
AsyncAPI code generation (tool.bal_asyncapi)

sources.note: Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, MQTT, JMS, WebSub and CDC BBE categories

nodes.notes: CDC service callbacks onUpdate/onDelete are named in the CDC guide text; the BBE shows onRead/onCreate.

nodes.title: Integration patterns
nodes.summary: Implementing enterprise integration patterns (routing, splitting, aggregation, scatter-gather, enrichment, translation, wire tap, idempotency, claim check) and service orchestration in Ballerina with HTTP services and clients, typed records, match, workers and query expressions.

must_cover.text: Write a service whose `resource function get doctors/[string category]()` forwards the call to a backend through a module-level `final http:Client queryDoctorEP = check new (healthcareBackend);`, binding the reply with `Doctor[]|http:ClientError resp = queryDoctorEP->/[category];`

Route each message to the right backend with a `match` statement on an enum-typed field (e.g. `match reservation.hospital_id { grandoak => {...} clemency => {...} _ => {...} }`), selecting the `http:Client` to call

Orchestrate several backend calls in sequence (reserve, fetch fee, pay), checking each result with `if appointment !is Appointment` and mapping `http:ClientRequestError` to `http:NotFound` and other failures to `http:InternalServerError`

Implement a message filter and a recipient list by iterating recipients with `foreach var {contact, subscription} in recipientList.get(category)` and dispatching with `match subscription { "EMAIL" => ... "SMS" => ... }`
Split a composite request into one outbound message per element with nested `foreach` loops over `request.events` and `event.attendees`, calling a helper that returns `error?` with `check`
Aggregate related messages by buffering them in a `final map<json[]>` keyed by a correlation header and forwarding the combined message once the expected count arrives, then removing the entry

Call several providers in parallel with named `worker` blocks inside a resource, collect results with `wait {hotwire, avis}`, and build the response with `map from var [vendor, result] in responses.entries() where result !is error select [vendor, result]`
Enrich a message with data from a lookup call and build the outgoing value with a spread, e.g. `{...req, bankCode: ibanRes.bank_code}`

Translate between two record schemas in a dedicated function (e.g. `translate(SalesData) returns QuickBooksInvoice`) using field mapping and a query expression for nested arrays, then forward the result with `targetType = http:Response`
Accept heterogeneous payloads with `@http:Payload json|xml request`, branch with `if request is json`, read XML fields with `(request/<subject>).data()`, and normalize both into one canonical shape
Copy messages to a secondary channel without delaying the main response by starting a `worker w returns error? { check wiretap(...); }` inside the resource before returning the result

Make a `put` resource idempotent by comparing the incoming state with the stored state (e.g. in a `map<OrderStatus>`) and returning `http:STATUS_NO_CONTENT` for repeats and `http:STATUS_CREATED` for changes

Apply the claim check pattern by storing a large payload (a byte stream) in an object store with an `http:Client` `put`, publishing only a generated `uuid:createType1AsString()` reference to Kafka, and fetching the payload back in the consumer
Implement a routing slip by computing a `string[]` of processing steps from lookups and attaching it to the message with `{...request, routingSlip: routingSlip}` before invoking the steps
Finish an orchestration by sending a confirmation email with an `email:SmtpClient` created from configurable `host`, `username` and `password`, calling `smtpClient->sendMessage({to, subject, body})`
Externalize backend URLs as `configurable string hospitalServicesBackend = "http://localhost:9090";` and initialize module-level `final http:Client` objects from them

out_of_scope: Message-broker based publish-subscribe and point-to-point channels (topic.event_driven)
Detailed data transformation techniques (topic.data_mapping)
Retry, failover and polling with back-off (topic.resiliency)
nodes.notes: EIP samples call mocked endpoints (`*.balmock.io`); the samples elide some helper code with `⋯`.

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.summary: Observing Ballerina services through the three pillars of metrics, tracing and logging - enabling observability at build time, exporting to Prometheus, Jaeger or OpenTelemetry, adding custom spans and metrics, and writing structured, configurable logs.

must_cover.text: Include observability in the executable with `observabilityIncluded = true` under `[build-options]` in `Ballerina.toml` or with `bal run --observability-included`, and explain that services and client connectors are observable by default once it is enabled
Turn on metrics and tracing at runtime in `Config.toml` with `[ballerina.observe]` keys `metricsEnabled`, `metricsReporter`, `tracingEnabled` and `tracingProvider`

Publish metrics to Prometheus by adding `import ballerinax/prometheus as _;`, setting `metricsReporter = "prometheus"` and `[ballerinax.prometheus]` `port = 9797` / `host`, and pointing a Prometheus scrape target (visualised in Grafana) at the `/metrics` endpoint

Send traces to Jaeger by adding `import ballerinax/jaeger as _;`, setting `tracingProvider = "jaeger"` and `[ballerinax.jaeger]` options such as `agentHostname`, `agentPort = 4317`, `samplerType` and `samplerParam`

Export traces and metrics over OTLP by setting `tracingProvider = "otel"` and `metricsReporter = "otel"` with `[ballerina.otel]` `tracesEndpoint`, `metricsEndpoint` and `metricsServiceName`, and add resource attributes under `[ballerina.otel.tracesResourceAttributes]`

Trace a block of business logic with `observe:startSpan("name")`, start an independent trace with `observe:startRootSpan(...)`, nest spans by passing a parent span id, and close each with `observe:finishSpan(spanId)`
Attach business context to the current or a given span with `observe:addTagToSpan("key", "value")`
Count business events with an `observe:Counter` created with a name, `desc` and `tags`, registered with `register()` and updated with `increment()` / `increment(10)`

Track values that go up and down with an `observe:Gauge` using `increment`, `decrement` and `setValue`, and configure summary statistics with `observe:StatisticConfig {timeWindow, percentiles, buckets}`

Name a service in metrics and traces with `@display {label: "Shopping Service"}`, and explain the common tags such as `src.resource.path`, `src.resource.accessor` and `entrypoint.service.name` attached to observations

Write structured logs with key-value context such as `log:printInfo("Processing order", orderId = 845315, amount = 99.99)`, passing records as values and choosing `printDebug`, `printInfo`, `printWarn` or `printError` by severity
Log failures with the error value and extra context, e.g. `log:printError("Reservation request failed", err, operation = "reserve")`, including errors that carry a cause and detail fields

Build log messages with raw templates (`` log:printInfo(`Started with delay ${delay}`) ``) instead of string concatenation, and pass a function as a key value (`duration = getDuration`) so it is evaluated only if the level is enabled

Configure logging in `Config.toml` with `[ballerina.log]` `level` and `format = "json"`, per-module levels under `[[ballerina.log.modules]]`, file `destinations` with `rotation`, and root context under `[ballerina.log.keyValues]`

Enable HTTP access logs with `[ballerina.http.accessLogConfig]` `console = true` (plus `format`, `attributes` and a rotated `file`), and HTTP trace logs with `[ballerina.http.traceLogAdvancedConfig]` or `-Cballerina.http.traceLogConsole=true`

out_of_scope: Full log module API such as custom and child loggers (lib.log)
Masking sensitive fields in logs (topic.security)
Vendor-specific platforms such as New Relic, Datadog and Elastic Stack setup
nodes.notes: The Prometheus extension is `ballerinax/prometheus` and Jaeger `ballerinax/jaeger` (imported with `as _`); the OpenTelemetry page says the otel extension is bundled and needs no import. Grafana is covered only as a dashboard over Prometheus.

nodes.title: Resiliency
nodes.summary: Making Ballerina integrations tolerate slow or failing dependencies with HTTP client timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, load balancing and failover, the language retry statement, broker-level error handling and graceful shutdown.

must_cover.text: Set a request timeout in seconds on an `http:Client`, e.g. `http:Client albumClient = check new ("localhost:9090", {timeout: 10});`, and handle the resulting error
Configure an `http:Client` with `retryConfig = {interval: 3, count: 3, backOffFactor: 2.0, maxWaitInterval: 20}` so failed requests are retried with exponential back-off capped at `maxWaitInterval`
Retry only on selected HTTP response codes by setting `statusCodes` (e.g. `[502, 503]`) in the client's `http:RetryConfig`

sources.note: RetryConfig has count, interval, backOffFactor, maxWaitInterval, statusCodes

must_cover.text: Protect a backend with `circuitBreaker = {rollingWindow: {timeWindow: 10, bucketSize: 2, requestVolumeThreshold: 0}, failureThreshold: 0.2, resetTime: 10, statusCodes: [400, 404, 500]}` on an `http:Client`, and explain when the circuit trips and resets

Spread requests across several backend instances with `http:LoadBalanceClient` configured with `targets: [{url: ...}, ...]` and a `timeout`, calling it with resource access syntax like a normal client
Fall back to secondary endpoints with `http:FailoverClient` configured with `targets`, `failoverCodes: [501, 502, 503]`, `interval` and `timeout`

Wrap a failure-prone block in a `retry { ... }` statement, which by default uses `error:DefaultRetryManager` and re-runs the block up to 3 times while it fails with an `error:Retriable` error, and pass a count with `retry(5) { ... }`

Write a class with a `public function shouldRetry(error e) returns boolean` method (the `RetryManager` object type), and use it as `retry<MyRetryManager>(args) { ... }` to decide which errors are retried and how often
Use `retry transaction { ...; check commit; }` so a transaction whose stages fail with `error:Retriable` is retried (3 times by default)
Recover locally from failures with `do { ... } on fail error e { ... }` instead of letting `check` propagate the error to the caller or listener
Make a `websocket:Client` reconnect automatically with `retryConfig: {maxCount: 5, interval: 5}`

Handle undeliverable Kafka records by setting `autoSeekOnValidationFailure: false` and implementing `remote function onError(kafka:Error 'error, kafka:Caller caller)` that logs `kafka:PayloadBindingError` / `kafka:PayloadValidationError` and calls `caller->seek({partition, offset: offset + 1})` to skip the bad record
Acknowledge RabbitMQ messages only after successful processing by setting `autoAck: false` in `@rabbitmq:ServiceConfig` and calling `caller->basicAck()` (or `basicNack`) from `onMessage`

Poll a slow backend a bounded number of times with `foreach int _ in 0 ..< 10`, pausing with `runtime:sleep(5)` (which does not block the thread) and returning an error such as `error("Payment timed out")` when attempts run out
Register cleanup logic for graceful shutdown with `runtime:onGracefulStop(handler)` from a module `init` function

out_of_scope: Full retry statement and RetryManager semantics (concept.retry)
Transaction semantics (concept.transactions)
HTTP client configuration beyond resiliency settings (lib.http)
Kafka and RabbitMQ APIs in general (lib.kafka, lib.rabbitmq)
nodes.notes: The spec's retry statement wording is `retry-spec := [type-parameter] [ ( arg-list ) ]`; `retry(5)` passes 5 to `DefaultRetryManager.init(int count = 3)`. `retryConfig.statusCodes` is confirmed from http source (client_config.bal), not from a BBE.

nodes.title: REST APIs
nodes.summary: Building RESTful HTTP services and clients in Ballerina by combining services, resource methods, record-typed payloads, typed status-code responses, interceptors and the OpenAPI tool.

must_cover.text: Write an HTTP service such as `service /covid/status on new http:Listener(9000)` that puts the shared URL prefix in the service base path and exposes `resource function get countries()` and `resource function post countries(...)` on the same resource path

Read a path segment with a path parameter such as `resource function get countries/[string iso_code]()` and look the entity up in a `table<T> key(k)` with `covidTable[iso_code]`, returning a not-found response when the result is `()`

Accept query parameters as plain resource parameters (e.g. `resource function get albums(string artist)`), using nilable (`string?`) or defaultable parameters for optional ones, and filter the collection with a query expression

Read request headers with `@http:Header` parameters (e.g. `@http:Header string accept`) and return `http:NOT_ACCEPTABLE` when the client asks for an unsupported media type; know a missing non-optional header yields `400 Bad Request`
Bind a JSON request body to a record or record array resource parameter (implicitly or with `@http:Payload`) and return records or arrays, which Ballerina serializes to JSON automatically
Explain that a resource returning a plain value responds with `200 OK`, except a `post` resource which responds with `201 Created`

Return status-code constants such as `http:CONFLICT`, `http:NOT_FOUND` or `http:NOT_ACCEPTABLE` from a resource declared as `returns Album|http:Conflict`, e.g. when a POST would create a duplicate key

Define response records that include a status-code type, e.g. `type InvalidIsoCodeError record {| *http:NotFound; ErrorMsg body; |}`, and return them in the union return type so error payloads are typed and appear in the generated OpenAPI specification

Return `http:Created` (or a record including `*http:Created`) with a `headers` map such as a `Location` header and a `body`, and type custom response headers with a `headers` record field as in a record including `*http:Ok`

sources.note: Created includes CommonResponse with headers and body

must_cover.text: Validate request payloads by annotating record fields with `@constraint:String {minLength: 1, maxLength: 5}` (and other `constraint` annotations) so invalid payloads are rejected with `400 Bad Request` before the resource runs

Propagate failures from a resource with `check` (the listener replies `500 Internal Server Error` and logs the error), or handle them and return `http:NotFound` / `http:InternalServerError` explicitly, e.g. mapping `http:ClientRequestError` from a backend call to `http:NotFound`

Write an `http:RequestInterceptor` service class with `resource function 'default [string... path](http:RequestContext ctx, ...)` that checks a header and returns `ctx.next()`, and engage it from an `http:InterceptableService` via `createInterceptors()`

Centralize error responses with an `http:ResponseErrorInterceptor` whose `remote function interceptResponseError(error err)` returns a status-code response such as `http:BadRequest` with a custom body

Configure CORS with `@http:ServiceConfig {cors: {allowOrigins: [...], allowCredentials: ..., allowHeaders: [...]}}` and override it per resource with `@http:ResourceConfig {cors: ...}`, listing specific trusted origins rather than `*`
Annotate a resource return type with `@http:Cache {maxAge: 15}` so responses carry `Cache-Control`, `ETag` and `Last-Modified` headers, e.g. `returns @http:Cache {maxAge: 15} Album|http:NotFound`

Call a REST API with an `http:Client` using resource access syntax, binding the response to the expected type (`Album[] albums = check albumClient->/albums;`) and posting records with `client->/path.post(payload)`

Export an OpenAPI contract from a service with `bal openapi -i service.bal`, and generate a service skeleton or service contract type from a specification with `bal openapi -i spec.yaml --mode service [--with-service-contract]`
Test a REST service from a `@test:Config` function that calls it with an `http:Client` and asserts `response.statusCode` and the payload with `test:assertEquals`

out_of_scope: Full http module API surface such as SSE, multipart, HTTP/2 and compression (lib.http)
Authentication, authorization and TLS on REST services (topic.security)
Client retries, timeouts, circuit breakers and failover (topic.resiliency)
GraphQL and gRPC APIs (lib.graphql, lib.grpc)

sources.note: Write a RESTful API with Ballerina (COVID-19 CRUD service)
StatusCodeResponse records and CommonResponse (mediaType, headers, body)

nodes.notes: The `Location` header item relies on `http:Created` including `http:CommonResponse` (fields `mediaType`, `headers`, `body`); the BBE shows the `headers` pattern with `*http:Ok`, not specifically `Location`.

nodes.title: Security
nodes.summary: Securing Ballerina services and clients end to end with TLS and mutual TLS, declarative Basic/JWT/OAuth2 authentication and scope-based authorization, outbound client credentials, JWT issuing and validation, safe cryptography and secret handling.

must_cover.text: Serve HTTPS by creating `listener http:Listener securedEP = new (9090, secureSocket = {key: {certFile: "...", keyFile: "..."}});` and attaching services to it

Require client certificates with `mutualSsl: {verifyClient: http:REQUIRE, cert: ...}` in the listener `secureSocket`, and configure the client side with both `key` and `cert` in `http:Client` `secureSocket`

Make an `http:Client` trust a server by setting `secureSocket = {cert: "public.crt"}` or a PKCS12 truststore `cert: {path: truststorePath, password: truststorePassword}` read from configurable variables

Protect a service with Basic auth backed by the file user store using `@http:ServiceConfig {auth: [{fileUserStoreConfig: {}, scopes: ["admin"]}]}` and `[[ballerina.auth.users]]` entries (username, password, scopes) in `Config.toml`, and explain the `401` vs `403` responses

Secure a service with JWT using `auth: [{jwtValidatorConfig: {issuer: "wso2", audience: "ballerina", signatureConfig: {certFile: "..."}, scopeKey: "scp"}, scopes: ["admin"]}]` in `@http:ServiceConfig`
Secure a service with OAuth2 token introspection using `oauth2IntrospectionConfig: {url: "...", tokenTypeHint: "access_token", scopeKey: "scp", clientConfig: {...}}` and required `scopes`
Override service-level authentication and authorization for a single resource with `@http:ResourceConfig {auth: [...]}`, e.g. requiring an extra scope on a write operation

sources.note: configs can be overwritten at the resource level

must_cover.text: Send credentials from an `http:Client` with `auth = {token: "..."}` (bearer token) or `auth = {username: "...", password: "..."}` (Basic auth) together with `secureSocket`
Have an `http:Client` sign its own JWT per request with `auth = {username, issuer, audience, keyId, customClaims: {"scp": "admin"}, expTime: 3600, signatureConfig: {config: {keyFile: "..."}}}`

Obtain OAuth2 access tokens automatically in an `http:Client` with the client credentials grant (`auth = {tokenUrl, clientId, clientSecret, scopes}`) or the refresh token grant (`auth = {refreshUrl, refreshToken, clientId, clientSecret}`)
Issue a JWT with `jwt:issue(jwt:IssuerConfig)` and validate one with `jwt:validate(token, jwt:ValidatorConfig)`, always pinning `issuer` and `audience`, keeping `expTime` short and `clockSkew` small
Keep passwords, API keys and tokens out of source code by declaring them as `configurable string password = ?;` supplied through `Config.toml`, and never printing or logging configurable values

Hash stored passwords with a slow algorithm such as `crypto:hashArgon2(password, iterations = 3, memory = 65536, parallelism = 4)` or `crypto:hashBcrypt(password, 14)` instead of `crypto:hashSha256` or `crypto:hashMd5`
Encrypt data with `crypto:encryptAesGcm(data, key, iv)` rather than ECB or CBC modes, and use OAEP padding such as `crypto:OAEPwithSHA512andMGF1` with `crypto:encryptRsaEcb`

Sign data with `crypto:signRsaSha256(input, privateKey)` and check it with `crypto:verifyRsaSha256Signature`, loading keys with `crypto:decodeRsaPrivateKeyFromKeyFile` / `crypto:decodeRsaPublicKeyFromCertFile`, and compute message MACs with `crypto:hmacSha256(input, key)`
Mark record fields with `@log:Sensitive` (optionally with `strategy: {replacement: "****"}` or a masking function) so passwords and card numbers are masked when the record is logged
Use explicit accessors such as `resource function delete ...` instead of `resource function default ...` for state-changing operations, and restrict CORS `allowOrigins` to trusted origins

out_of_scope: LDAP user stores (lib.ldap)
Security on gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket and message-broker clients (lib.grpc, lib.graphql, lib.websocket, lib.kafka)
Full crypto, jwt, oauth2 and auth module APIs (lib.crypto, lib.jwt, lib.oauth2, lib.auth)
Running `bal scan` (tool.bal_scan)

sources.note: REST service security and HTTP client security BBE categories

nodes.notes: Password-hashing parameters follow the OWASP guidance quoted on the scan-rules page (bcrypt work factor >= 10, Argon2 memory >= 19456 KB).
